name.zh: 迦腻色伽即位（罗巴塔克铭文）

summary.en: The Bactrian-language Rabatak inscription, found in northern Afghanistan in 1993, records Kanishka’s royal genealogy and the first year of his era, when Kushan authority reached cities of the Ganges plain. Most scholars now place that year near 127 CE.
summary.zh: 1993年在阿富汗北部发现的大夏语罗巴塔克铭文记载了迦腻色伽的王统世系及其纪元元年，当时贵霜势力已达恒河平原诸城。今多数学者将该元年定在公元127年前后。

sources.title: N. Sims-Williams & J. Cribb, “A new Bactrian inscription of Kanishka the Great”, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 4 (1996)
Harry Falk, “The yuga of Sphujiddhvaja and the era of the Kuṣāṇas”, Silk Road Art and Archaeology 7 (2001)

note: Kanishka’s accession has been placed anywhere between 78 and 144 CE; 127 follows Falk (2001) and is now the majority view. The inscription itself gives only regnal year 1.

story.en:
In 1993 Afghan fighters digging a trench near the village of Rabatak in Baghlan province, northern Afghanistan, unearthed a stone block covered in Greek letters. The language turned out to be Bactrian, the Iranian tongue of the Kushans, and the text was a royal proclamation of Kanishka.

It says that in year one of his reign Kanishka “issued a Greek edict and then put it into Aryan”, meaning that he switched official writing from Greek to Bactrian. It lists the cities of the Ganges plain that obeyed him, from Saketa and Kaushambi to Pataliputra and Champa, and gives his ancestry: great-grandson of Kujula Kadphises, grandson of Vima Taktu, son of Vima Kadphises. The name of Vima Taktu, until then known only as the nameless “Great Saviour” king of the coins, settled the dynasty’s order.

The inscription names Iranian and Indian gods together, matching Kanishka’s coins, which show Greek, Iranian, Hindu and Buddhist deities. It gives no date in any outside era, so the debate over when Kanishka reigned continues, though most scholars now accept about 127 CE.
story.zh:
1993年，几名阿富汗武装人员在北部巴格兰省罗巴塔克村附近挖掘战壕时，挖出一块刻满希腊字母的石块。经研究，其语言是贵霜人的伊朗语族语言大夏语，内容是迦腻色伽的王室诏令。

铭文说，迦腻色伽在位第一年“颁布了希腊文诏令，随后改用雅利安语”，即把官方文字从希腊语改为大夏语。它列出了恒河平原上服从他的城市，从娑祇多、憍赏弥到华氏城和瞻波，并交代了他的世系：丘就却的曾孙、维玛·塔克图的孙子、阎膏珍的儿子。维玛·塔克图此前只以钱币上无名的“伟大救世主”之王为人所知，这一名字由此理清了王朝的世系顺序。

铭文同时提到伊朗诸神和印度诸神，与迦腻色伽钱币上并列希腊、伊朗、印度教和佛教神祇的情形相符。铭文没有使用任何外部纪年，因此关于迦腻色伽在位年代的争论仍在继续，不过如今多数学者接受约公元127年之说。

summary.en: The accession of Chandragupta I, linked in Gupta coinage to his marriage alliance with the Licchavis, became the epoch of the Gupta era used in inscriptions across northern India for centuries.
summary.zh: 旃陀罗笈多一世即位，笈多钱币将此与其和离车族的联姻相联系；这一年成为笈多纪元的起点，此后数百年间北印度碑铭普遍采用。

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)

note: The era’s epoch is reckoned as 319–320 CE; Wikidata dates the broader “Gupta era” period from 318.

story.en:
Chandragupta I began as a minor king in the middle Ganges valley. His decisive step was marriage to Kumaradevi, a princess of the Licchavis, an old and prestigious clan of north Bihar. Gold coins struck by him or his son show the king and queen together, with the legend “Licchavayah” (the Licchavis), and Samudragupta proudly called himself “son of the daughter of the Licchavis”.

At about this time Chandragupta took the title Maharajadhiraja, “great king of kings”, and his accession is usually taken as year one of a new era. Later Gupta inscriptions, and those of many kings who came after them, count their years from it; the 11th-century scholar al-Biruni recorded that the Gupta era began 241 years after the Shaka era of 78 CE, which fixes its start at 319–320.

The era outlived the dynasty by centuries and is one of the anchors historians use to date Indian inscriptions.
story.zh:
旃陀罗笈多一世起初只是恒河中游的一个小国君主。他的关键一步是迎娶北比哈尔古老而显赫的离车族公主鸠摩罗提鞞。他或其子所铸的金币上，国王与王后并肩而立，铭文为“离车”；沙摩陀罗笈多也自豪地自称“离车之女的儿子”。

大约此时，旃陀罗笈多取称号“摩诃罗阇提罗阇”（众王之大王），一般认为他的即位之年即新纪元的元年。后来的笈多铭文以及其后许多国王的铭文都以此纪年；11世纪学者比鲁尼记载，笈多纪元始于公元78年塞种纪元之后241年，由此确定其起点为319至320年。

这一纪元比王朝延续了好几个世纪，是历史学家为印度铭文断代的重要依据之一。

summary.en: A seven-metre wrought-iron column bearing a Sanskrit eulogy of a king “Chandra”, usually identified with Chandragupta II, it was forged around 400 CE and has resisted corrosion remarkably; it now stands in the Qutb complex in Delhi.
summary.zh: 这根约七米高的熟铁柱刻有赞颂“旃陀罗”王的梵文铭文，一般认为即旃陀罗笈多二世；约铸于公元400年，至今几乎不锈，现立于德里顾特卜建筑群内。

sources.title: R. Balasubramaniam, Delhi Iron Pillar: New Insights (2002)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Iron pillar of Delhi

note: Dated by palaeography to c. 400 CE (Wikidata: 5th century); it was probably moved to Delhi from elsewhere, possibly Udayagiri, centuries later.

name.zh: 阿旃陀石窟（伐迦陀迦时期）

summary.en: Under the Vakataka king Harisena, Buddhist patrons cut most of Ajanta’s richly painted caves within a few decades, adding to an earlier group of the 2nd–1st centuries BCE. The murals are the finest surviving ancient Indian paintings.
summary.zh: 在伐迦陀迦王诃利犀那统治时期，佛教施主于数十年间开凿了阿旃陀的大部分彩绘石窟，与公元前2至前1世纪的早期洞窟相接续。其壁画是现存最精美的古印度绘画。

sources.title: Walter M. Spink, Ajanta: History and Development, vol. 1 (2005)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Ajanta Caves

note: Spink’s short chronology (c. 460–480) is influential but debated; Wikidata’s start date (c. 2nd century BCE) refers to the earliest caves.

summary.en: Founded under the Gupta king Kumaragupta I, Nalanda grew into Asia’s foremost Buddhist monastic university, drawing scholars such as Xuanzang and Yijing, until it declined after attacks around 1200.
summary.zh: 那烂陀寺创建于笈多王鸠摩罗笈多一世时期，发展为亚洲首屈一指的佛教寺院大学，玄奘、义净等皆曾来此求学，约1200年遭攻击后衰落。

sources.title: Xuanzang, Da Tang Xiyu Ji (Records of the Western Regions), tr. Samuel Beal (1884)
UNESCO World Heritage List: Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara at Nalanda, Bihar

note: The c. 427 founding date is conventional, resting on seals naming Kumaragupta I (r. c. 415–455) and on Xuanzang’s account.

story.en:
Nalanda grew from a cluster of monasteries near Rajgir, a place associated with the Buddha’s disciples, into a great residential university. Xuanzang credits the first royal foundation to a king called Shakraditya, usually identified with Kumaragupta I, and a seal found at the site also names Shakraditya as founder, and later Gupta, Harsha and Pala kings added monasteries, temples and endowments of villages to feed the monks.

Xuanzang, who studied there for about five years in the 630s, described several thousand monks, lofty towers and debates so demanding that most applicants were turned away at the gate. Teachers such as Shilabhadra taught Yogacara philosophy, logic and grammar. Yijing, who came a few decades later, wrote a detailed account of its monastic rules.

In the 8th century Nalanda scholars such as Shantarakshita helped establish Buddhism in Tibet. The monastery was devastated around 1200 and slowly abandoned. Its brick ruins, excavated from 1915, are a World Heritage site, and a new Nalanda University opened nearby in 2014.
story.zh:
那烂陀起初是王舍城附近一组与佛陀弟子有关的寺院，后来发展成一所规模宏大的住宿制大学。玄奘把第一次王室创建归于一位名叫“铄迦罗阿迭多”（帝日王）的国王，一般认为即鸠摩罗笈多一世，遗址出土的一枚印章也称铄迦罗阿迭多为创建者；此后笈多、戒日王和波罗诸王又陆续增建寺院、神殿，并捐赠村庄供养僧众。

630年代在此求学约五年的玄奘描述说，这里有数千名僧人和高耸的楼阁，入学辩难极其严格，大多数求学者在门口就被拒之门外。戒贤等大师讲授瑜伽行派哲学、因明和声明。数十年后来到这里的义净则详细记录了寺院的戒律。

8世纪，寂护等那烂陀学者帮助佛教在西藏扎根。约1200年寺院遭到毁灭性打击，随后逐渐荒废。1915年起发掘的砖砌遗址如今是世界遗产，2014年附近又开办了新的那烂陀大学。

name.zh: 迦叶波一世营建狮子岩

summary.en: King Kashyapa I of Anuradhapura moved his court to this granite monolith, crowning it with a palace and surrounding it with frescoes, water gardens and a lion gateway; after his fall it became a Buddhist monastery.
summary.zh: 阿努拉德普勒王迦叶波一世将宫廷迁至这块花岗岩巨石，在其顶部建宫殿，四周饰以壁画、水园和狮爪门；其败亡后此地改为佛教寺院。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Ancient City of Sigiriya
K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (1981)

note: Kashyapa’s reign (c. 477–495) is dated from the Culavamsa chronicle.

name.zh: 阿耶波多著《阿耶波多历书》

summary.en: Writing at Kusumapura (Pataliputra) aged 23, Aryabhata set out place-value computation, an accurate value of π, a sine table and the daily rotation of the Earth, shaping Indian mathematical astronomy for a millennium.
summary.zh: 阿耶波多23岁时在拘苏摩补罗（华氏城）写成此书，阐述位值计算、精确的圆周率、正弦表以及地球自转之说，影响印度数理天文学达千年之久。

story.en:
Aryabhata says in his own book that he was 23 years old when 3,600 years of the Kali Age had passed, which works out to 499 CE, and that he wrote at Kusumapura, usually identified with Pataliputra. The Aryabhatiya is short, only 121 verses, written in a compressed style that encoded numbers in syllables.

Into those verses he packed a value of π as 62,832/20,000 (3.1416), described as “approximate”, a table of sine differences, rules for arithmetic and algebra, and a complete astronomical system. Most daringly he argued that the stars stand still and the Earth turns on its axis, like a man in a boat who sees the bank moving backwards. He also explained eclipses as shadows rather than the work of the demon Rahu.

Later astronomers, including Brahmagupta, attacked the rotating Earth, but the book remained the basis of a school of astronomy in south India and Kerala for a thousand years. India named its first satellite Aryabhata in 1975.
story.zh:
阿耶波多在书中自述，迦利时代过去3,600年时他23岁，折算为公元499年；他在拘苏摩补罗写作，一般认为即华氏城。《阿耶波多历书》篇幅很短，只有121颂，文体极为凝练，用音节来编码数字。

在这些诗句中，他给出圆周率为62,832/20,000（3.1416），并称之为“近似值”；还有正弦差值表、算术和代数规则，以及一套完整的天文体系。最大胆的是，他主张恒星静止、地球绕轴自转，就像坐船的人看到河岸向后移动。他还把日月食解释为影子，而非魔怪罗睺所为。

包括婆罗摩笈多在内的后世天文学家抨击地球自转之说，但此书在南印度和喀拉拉作为一个天文学派的基础延续了一千年。1975年印度把第一颗人造卫星命名为“阿耶波多”。

summary.en: The Chinese monk Xuanzang studied at Nalanda, met King Harsha at Kannauj and toured the subcontinent before returning to Chang’an with hundreds of texts; his Records of the Western Regions (646) is a key source for 7th-century India.
summary.zh: 唐僧玄奘在那烂陀寺求学，于曲女城会见戒日王，并遍游南亚次大陆，后携数百部经典返回长安；其《大唐西域记》（646年）是研究7世纪印度的重要史料。

sources.title: Xuanzang, Da Tang Xiyu Ji (Records of the Western Regions), tr. Samuel Beal (1884)
Huili, A Biography of the Tripitaka Master of the Great Ci’en Monastery

note: The QID is the Records (completed 646); the travel dates (c. 630–645) come from that text and Huili’s biography.

story.en:
Xuanzang left Chang’an in 629 against an imperial ban on foreign travel, slipping past border watchtowers at night. He crossed the Gobi and the Tian Shan, was welcomed by the Turkic khagan, and entered India through Gandhara, where he found many Buddhist monasteries already in ruins.

At Nalanda he studied Yogacara philosophy under the aged abbot Shilabhadra and became famous as a debater. Later he toured the south as far as Kanchi, the Pallava capital, then returned to Nalanda. In about 642 King Harsha summoned him to Kannauj and held a great assembly where, according to Xuanzang’s biographer Huili, no one could refute him. He then attended Harsha’s quinquennial distribution of alms at Prayaga before setting out for home.

He returned in 645 with 657 texts carried on horses, was received by Emperor Taizong, and spent the rest of his life translating. His Records of the Western Regions, finished in 646, describes 138 kingdoms and remains a basic source for Indian archaeology; British archaeologists used it to find Buddhist sites in the 19th century.
story.zh:
629年，玄奘违背朝廷禁止出境的禁令离开长安，夜间偷越边境烽燧。他穿越戈壁和天山，受到突厥可汗的款待，经犍陀罗进入印度，在那里看到许多佛寺已成废墟。

他在那烂陀随年迈的住持戒贤学习瑜伽行派哲学，并以辩论闻名。此后他南游远至帕拉瓦王朝的都城建志，然后回到那烂陀。约642年，戒日王召他到曲女城，举行盛大法会；据其传记作者慧立记载，无人能驳倒他。此后他参加了戒日王在钵逻耶伽每五年一次的布施大会，随即启程回国。

645年他带着用马驮运的657部经卷回国，受到唐太宗接见，余生致力于翻译。646年完成的《大唐西域记》记述了138个国家，至今仍是印度考古的基本史料；19世纪英国考古学家就曾借助它寻找佛教遗址。

summary.en: Harsha’s southward advance was halted on the Narmada by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, a victory celebrated in the Aihole inscription of 634; the river became the frontier between their realms.
summary.zh: 戒日王南下的攻势在讷尔默达河畔被遮娄其王补罗稽舍二世阻止，634年的艾霍莱铭文颂扬此胜；此后该河成为两国的分界。

sources.title: Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II (634 CE), Epigraphia Indica vol. 6
Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008)

note: Dated variously 618–619 or c. 630s; the exact battlefield on the Narmada is unknown, so the coordinates are approximate.

summary.en: The Arab commander Muhammad ibn al-Qasim took the port of Debal, defeated King Dahir and occupied Sindh and Multan, bringing the lower Indus valley into the caliphate.
summary.zh: 阿拉伯将领穆罕默德·本·卡西姆攻克德巴尔港，击败达希尔王，占领信德和木尔坦，将印度河下游纳入哈里发国。

sources.title: Chach Nama (13th-century Persian history of the conquest)

name.zh: 布里哈迪希瓦拉神庙落成

summary.en: Rajaraja I dedicated this granite Shiva temple at Thanjavur, whose 66-metre vimana was among the tallest buildings of its age; its inscriptions record the Chola state’s revenues, staff and endowments.
summary.zh: 罗阇罗阇一世在坦贾武尔建成这座花岗岩湿婆神庙，其66米高的主塔在当时世界上数一数二；庙中铭文记录了朱罗王朝的税收、人员与捐赠。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Great Living Chola Temples
K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Cōḻas, 2nd ed. (1955)

name.zh: 朱罗王朝远征室利佛逝

summary.en: Rajendra Chola I’s fleet raided the Srivijaya maritime realm, sacking ports in Sumatra and the Malay Peninsula including Kadaram (Kedah) and capturing its king; the Tanjore inscription of 1030–31 lists the places taken.
summary.zh: 拉金德拉一世的舰队袭击海上强国室利佛逝，洗劫苏门答腊和马来半岛诸港，包括羯荼（吉打），并俘获其国王；1030—1031年的坦贾武尔铭文列出了所攻占之地。

label.zh: 马纳卡瓦拉姆（尼科巴群岛）

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Cōḻas, 2nd ed. (1955)
Hermann Kulke, K. Kesavapany & Vijay Sakhuja (eds.), Nagapattinam to Suvarnadwipa: Reflections on the Chola Naval Expeditions to Southeast Asia (2009)

note: The inscription lists conquered places but not an itinerary; the route order is a reconstruction.

story.en:
Srivijaya, based in Sumatra, controlled the Strait of Malacca, the chokepoint of the sea route between India and China. Relations with the Cholas had been friendly: a Srivijayan king had endowed a Buddhist monastery at the Chola port of Nagapattinam. Why Rajendra I turned on it is not recorded; many historians think the Cholas wanted to break Srivijaya’s hold on trade and its tolls on Tamil merchants.

Rajendra’s Tanjore inscription lists the conquests in a long sequence: Srivijaya itself, Pannai, Malaiyur, Ilangasoka (in southern Thailand), Tamralinga, the Nicobar Islands and Kadaram (Kedah), whose king, Sangrama Vijayottungavarman, it says was captured with his elephants and his treasure, including a jewelled “gate of war”.

The raid did not create a lasting empire; Srivijaya survived, and when Virarajendra sent a fleet to Kedah around 1068 it was to restore a friendly king. But it was without parallel among the overseas campaigns of premodern Indian states, and Tamil merchant guilds remained active across Southeast Asia for two centuries.
story.zh:
以苏门答腊为基地的室利佛逝控制着马六甲海峡，这是印度与中国海上航线的咽喉。它与朱罗的关系原本友好：一位室利佛逝国王曾在朱罗港口讷加帕蒂南捐建佛寺。拉金德拉一世为何翻脸，史无明文；许多历史学家认为，朱罗想打破室利佛逝对贸易的控制及其对泰米尔商人征收的过路税。

拉金德拉的坦贾武尔铭文按顺序列出一长串征服之地：室利佛逝本土、班乃、末罗瑜、狼牙修（今泰国南部）、单马令、尼科巴群岛和羯荼（吉打）；铭文称羯荼国王僧伽罗摩·毗阇耶东伽跋摩连同他的大象和财宝被俘，其中包括一座镶满珠宝的“战争之门”。

这次远征并未建立持久的帝国：室利佛逝得以延续；约1068年维拉拉金德拉再派舰队到吉打，也只是为了扶立一位友好的国王。但它在前近代印度国家的海外征战中绝无仅有，此后两个世纪泰米尔商人行会仍活跃于东南亚各地。

name.zh: 加兹尼的马哈茂德洗劫索姆纳特

summary.en: Climaxing some seventeen raids into India, Mahmud crossed the Thar desert, took the Somnath temple on the Gujarat coast and carried off its treasure; the episode became a contested symbol in later memory.
summary.zh: 马哈茂德前后约十七次入侵印度，此役穿越塔尔沙漠，攻陷古吉拉特海岸的索姆纳特神庙并掠走其财宝；此事在后世记忆中成为争议性的象征。

sources.title: Romila Thapar, Somanatha: The Many Voices of a History (2004)

note: Mahmud left Ghazni in late 1025; the temple fell in January 1026.

story.en:
Mahmud of Ghazni raided India almost every winter for a quarter of a century, using its temple treasuries to fund his wars and adorn his capital. In October 1025 he set out from Ghazni for Somnath, a Shiva temple on the Gujarat coast famous for its wealth and for the tides that, pilgrims said, washed its linga daily.

Crossing the Thar desert with camels carrying water, his army reached the temple in January 1026. Persian chroniclers say the defenders fought on the walls for days before the city fell, that some 50,000 were killed, and that Mahmud broke the idol and sent pieces to Ghazni to be laid at the mosque’s threshold. On the way home, avoiding hostile Hindu chiefs, his army took a hard route through Kutch, Sindh and the desert and suffered badly.

The temple was rebuilt within decades, and Jain and Sanskrit records of the period barely mention the raid. Historians such as Romila Thapar argue that its later fame as a national trauma owes much to 19th-century British and Indian writers; others stress the chroniclers’ own boasts of destruction. The present temple was rebuilt after independence and consecrated in 1951.
story.zh:
伽色尼的马哈茂德在四分之一个世纪里几乎每年冬天都袭掠印度，用神庙的财富供养战争、装点都城。1025年10月，他从伽色尼出发前往索姆纳特，这座位于古吉拉特海岸的湿婆神庙以富有著称，朝圣者说潮水每天都会冲洗庙中的林伽。

他的军队用骆驼驮水穿越塔尔沙漠，于1026年1月抵达神庙。波斯史家说，守军在城墙上苦战数日城市才陷落，约五万人被杀；马哈茂德击碎神像，并把碎块送回伽色尼，铺在清真寺门槛下。归途中为避开敌对的印度教首领，他的军队取道卡奇、信德和沙漠，饥渴交加，损失惨重。

神庙在数十年内即被重建，同时代的耆那教和梵文文献几乎没有提及这次袭击。罗米拉·塔帕尔等历史学家认为，它后来作为民族创伤而闻名，很大程度上源于19世纪英国和印度作家的书写；另一些学者则强调当时史家本身对破坏的夸耀。现在的神庙是独立后重建的，于1951年落成开光。

summary.en: A Rajput coalition under Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad of Ghor near Taraori in Haryana, wounding the Ghurid ruler and checking his advance into the Ganges plain.
summary.zh: 普里特维拉杰·乔汉率领的拉其普特联军在哈里亚纳的塔拉奥里附近击败古尔王朝的穆罕默德，使其负伤，暂时阻止了他向恒河平原的推进。

sources.title: Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)

summary.en: Returning with mounted archers, Muhammad of Ghor routed Prithviraj Chauhan on the same field; Prithviraj was captured and killed, opening north India to Ghurid rule and the later Delhi Sultanate.
summary.zh: 古尔的穆罕默德率骑射手卷土重来，在同一战场击溃普里特维拉杰·乔汉，后者被俘遇害，北印度从此向古尔王朝及其后的德里苏丹国敞开。

sources.title: Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)
Minhaj-i Siraj Juzjani, Tabaqat-i Nasiri (tr. H. G. Raverty, 1881)

story.en:
In 1191 Prithviraj Chauhan, king of Ajmer and Delhi, had routed Muhammad of Ghor at Tarain, north of Delhi; Muhammad himself was wounded and barely escaped. Later chroniclers such as Firishta say he spent the next year in shame, refusing to sleep with his wives or change his clothes, and raised a new army of Turkic, Tajik and Afghan horsemen.

In 1192 he returned to the same field. This time he avoided a frontal clash with Prithviraj’s elephants and massed infantry. Divisions of mounted archers harassed the Rajput army all day from the flanks and rear, and in the afternoon Muhammad threw in a fresh reserve of 10,000–12,000 horsemen. The Rajput host broke. Prithviraj fled on horseback and was captured near Sarsuti (probably modern Sirsa); most accounts say he was later executed at Ajmer.

Within about a decade Ghurid generals held Delhi, Ajmer, Kannauj and Bihar. Muhammad’s slave commander Qutb ud-Din Aibak, left in charge at Delhi, became the first sultan of Delhi in 1206. In later legend, notably the Prithviraj Raso, Prithviraj became a romantic hero who took revenge by shooting his captor.
story.zh:
1191年，阿杰梅尔和德里之王普里特维拉杰·乔汉在德里以北的塔拉因击溃古尔的穆罕默德；穆罕默德本人负伤，侥幸逃脱。据菲里什塔等后世史家记载，此后一年他深感羞耻，不与妻妾同寝、不换衣服，并重新招募了一支由突厥、塔吉克和阿富汗骑兵组成的军队。

1192年他回到原来的战场。这一次他避免与普里特维拉杰的战象和密集步兵正面交锋。骑射兵分队整日从侧翼和后方袭扰拉杰普特军队，到了下午，穆罕默德投入一万至一万二千名生力骑兵。拉杰普特大军崩溃。普里特维拉杰骑马逃走，在萨尔苏蒂（可能即今锡尔萨）附近被俘；多数记载说他后来在阿杰梅尔被处死。

约十年之内，古尔将领就控制了德里、阿杰梅尔、卡瑙季和比哈尔。穆罕默德留守德里的奴隶将领库特布丁·艾伊拜克于1206年成为德里第一位苏丹。在后来的传说中，尤其是《普里特维拉杰颂》里，普里特维拉杰成了浪漫英雄，最终射杀了俘获他的仇人。

summary.en: Qutb ud-Din Aibak began this fluted sandstone victory tower beside Delhi’s first congregational mosque after the Ghurid conquest; Iltutmish added storeys, and at about 73 m it is the tallest medieval minaret in India.
summary.zh: 古尔王朝征服后，库特布丁·艾巴克在德里第一座聚礼清真寺旁兴建这座带棱纹的砂岩胜利塔，伊勒图特米什续建上层；塔高约73米，是印度最高的中世纪宣礼塔。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi
Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)

note: Construction start c. 1199 is conventional (Wikidata gives no date); the top storeys were rebuilt by Firuz Shah Tughluq in 1369.

summary.en: Alauddin Khalji’s army met a large Chagatai Mongol force under Qutlugh Khwaja at Kili near Delhi; the Mongols withdrew after heavy fighting, one of several invasions the sultanate repelled around 1300.
summary.zh: 阿拉乌丁·卡尔吉的军队在德里附近的基利迎战忽都鲁·火者率领的察合台蒙古大军，激战后蒙古人撤退；这是约1300年前后德里苏丹国击退的多次蒙古入侵之一。

sources.title: Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)

summary.en: Timur crossed the Indus, defeated Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Tughluq outside Delhi and let his army plunder the city for days, leaving the sultanate shattered before he returned to Samarkand with captives and craftsmen.
summary.zh: 帖木儿渡过印度河，在德里城外击败图格鲁克王朝苏丹纳绥尔丁·马哈茂德，纵兵劫掠全城数日，德里苏丹国由此残破；随后他携俘虏和工匠返回撒马尔罕。

sources.title: Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate: A Political and Military History (1999)
Beatrice Forbes Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)

note: The date is the battle outside Delhi; the sack followed over the next days.

story.en:
Timur gave his reason for invading India as the Delhi sultans’ excessive tolerance of their Hindu subjects, but the Tughluq sultanate was weak and rich, and plunder was the attraction. He crossed the Indus in September 1398, and his army moved through the Punjab destroying towns that resisted.

Outside Delhi, fearing a revolt among the roughly 100,000 prisoners his army had taken, he ordered them killed, according to his own court histories. On 17 December he defeated Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud, whose war elephants, one account says, were thrown into panic by burning camels. The sultan fled.

Timur entered Delhi and granted protection in return for ransom, but clashes between his soldiers and townspeople turned into a sack that lasted several days. When he left, he took thousands of craftsmen, especially stonemasons, to build the Bibi Khanym mosque in Samarkand. Chroniclers describe the city left deserted and starving for months afterwards; the sultanate broke into regional kingdoms.
story.zh:
帖木儿声称入侵印度的理由是德里苏丹对印度教臣民过于宽容，但真正吸引他的是图格鲁克苏丹国的虚弱与富庶。1398年9月他渡过印度河，大军穿过旁遮普，摧毁一切抵抗的城镇。

据他本人的宫廷史书记载，在德里城外，他担心军中约十万名俘虏发生叛乱，下令将他们全部处死。12月17日，他击败苏丹纳绥尔丁·马哈茂德；据一种记载，苏丹的战象被身上着火的骆驼吓得四散奔逃。苏丹弃城而逃。

帖木儿进入德里，答应以赎金换取保护，但士兵与市民的冲突演变成持续数日的洗劫。离开时他带走了数千名工匠，尤其是石匠，去撒马尔罕修建比比哈努姆清真寺。史家记载，此后数月德里城空寂、饥荒蔓延；苏丹国则分裂成各地的地方王国。

summary.en: Guided across the Arabian Sea from Malindi, the Portuguese fleet anchored near Calicut, the Zamorin’s spice port, completing the first sea voyage from Europe to India and opening the era of European sea power in the Indian Ocean.
summary.zh: 葡萄牙船队在马林迪领航员引导下横渡阿拉伯海，停泊于扎莫林的香料港卡利卡特附近，完成了从欧洲到印度的首次航行，开启了欧洲海上势力进入印度洋的时代。

sources.title: Álvaro Velho (attrib.), Roteiro da primeira viagem de Vasco da Gama (journal of the first voyage)
Sanjay Subrahmanyam, The Career and Legend of Vasco da Gama (1997)

note: QID is the 1st Portuguese India Armada (1497–1499); coordinates are Kappad beach, the traditional landing place near Calicut (Kozhikode).

story.en:
Vasco da Gama’s fleet had rounded the Cape of Good Hope, broken up its store ship and worked up the East African coast with three vessels, where the ruler of Malindi gave him a pilot familiar with the monsoon route. On 20 May 1498, after nearly four weeks crossing the Arabian Sea, they anchored off Kappad near Calicut. The first man sent ashore met two Muslims from Tunis who asked him, in Castilian, what the devil had brought him there. He answered: Christians and spices.

The Zamorin received da Gama with courtesy, but the Portuguese gifts of cloth, hats and washbasins were laughed at by his officials, and the Muslim merchants who dominated Calicut’s trade warned against the newcomers. After three months of tense bargaining da Gama sailed home with a cargo of pepper and cinnamon and a few hostages; more than half his crew died on the voyage.

The cargo paid for the expedition many times over. Within a few years Portuguese fleets returned armed, bombarded Calicut and set out to control the Indian Ocean spice trade by force.
story.zh:
瓦斯科·达伽马的船队绕过好望角后拆毁了补给船，余下三艘沿东非海岸北上；马林迪的统治者为他提供了一位熟悉季风航线的领航员。横渡阿拉伯海近四个星期后，船队于1498年5月20日在卡利卡特附近的卡帕德下锚。第一个被派上岸的人遇到两名来自突尼斯的穆斯林，他们用卡斯蒂利亚语问他，究竟什么鬼把他带到这里。他回答：为了基督徒和香料。

扎莫林礼貌地接见了达伽马，但葡萄牙人送上的布匹、帽子和脸盆遭到他手下官员的嘲笑，而主导卡利卡特贸易的穆斯林商人也警告要提防这些新来者。经过三个月紧张的讨价还价，达伽马带着胡椒、肉桂和几名人质返航；途中一半以上的船员死去。

这批货物的价值是远航成本的许多倍。几年之内，全副武装的葡萄牙舰队卷土重来，炮轰卡利卡特，试图以武力控制印度洋香料贸易。

summary.en: Afonso de Albuquerque stormed Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate at the second attempt; it became the capital of Portuguese India and stayed Portuguese until 1961.
summary.zh: 阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克第二次进攻时从比贾布尔苏丹国手中夺取果阿；此地成为葡属印度首府，直至1961年仍归葡萄牙所有。

sources.title: Sanjay Subrahmanyam, The Portuguese Empire in Asia, 1500–1700 (1993)

story.en:
Afonso de Albuquerque, the second Portuguese governor in the Indian Ocean, wanted a permanent base rather than trading posts at the mercy of local rulers. Goa, an island port of the Bijapur Sultanate famous for its trade in Arabian horses, was the target. He took it in March 1510 with the encouragement of a local Hindu commander, Timoja, but was driven out by Bijapur’s army in May and spent a miserable monsoon trapped on his ships in the river.

On 25 November 1510 he returned with reinforcements and stormed the town; the Muslim defenders were massacred. Albuquerque encouraged his soldiers to marry local women and confirmed Hindu village councils in their old rights.

Goa became the capital of the Estado da India, with churches, a cathedral and, from 1560, the Inquisition. Its prosperity faded in the 17th century, but it remained Portuguese for 451 years, until the Indian army took it in December 1961.
story.zh:
葡萄牙在印度洋的第二任总督阿方索·德·阿尔布克尔克想要一个永久基地，而不是受制于当地统治者的商站。以阿拉伯马贸易闻名的比贾布尔苏丹国岛港果阿成了目标。1510年3月，他在当地印度教将领蒂莫贾的鼓动下攻占果阿，但5月被比贾布尔军队赶走，只好困在河口的船上度过一个凄惨的雨季。

1510年11月25日，他带着援军卷土重来，攻破城池，穆斯林守军遭到屠杀。阿尔布克尔克鼓励士兵娶当地女子为妻，并确认印度教村社保留原有权利。

果阿成为“葡属印度”的首府，城中建起教堂、大教堂，1560年起还设立了宗教裁判所。17世纪其繁荣渐衰，但它在葡萄牙手中保持了451年，直到1961年12月被印度军队收回。

summary.en: Babur’s smaller army, using field guns behind a wagon barricade and flanking cavalry, defeated Sultan Ibrahim Lodi, who died on the field; the victory ended the Delhi Sultanate and founded the Mughal Empire.
summary.zh: 巴布尔兵力较少，以车阵掩护火炮并辅以侧翼骑兵，击败苏丹易卜拉欣·洛迪，后者阵亡；此战终结了德里苏丹国，开创莫卧儿帝国。

sources.title: John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)

note: 21 April 1526 is the Julian date used by most historians; Wikidata stores the proleptic Gregorian equivalent (1 May).

story.en:
Babur, a Timurid prince who had lost his homeland of Fergana and ruled Kabul, had raided the Punjab four times. In late 1525 he came to stay. With an army that his memoir counts at about 12,000, servants and followers included, he met Sultan Ibrahim Lodi’s army of perhaps 100,000 men and a thousand elephants at Panipat, north of Delhi.

Babur borrowed tactics from the Ottomans. He lashed some 700 carts together with ropes of rawhide, left gaps for cavalry charges, and placed matchlockmen and cannon under his gunners Ustad Ali Quli and Mustafa behind them. On 21 April 1526 Ibrahim’s army attacked the barrier head-on; Babur’s flanking horsemen wheeled round with the Central Asian tulughma manoeuvre and shot into the packed ranks. By noon the battle was over and Ibrahim lay dead with thousands of his men.

Babur sent his son Humayun to seize the treasury at Agra. In his memoir, the Baburnama, he complained about India’s lack of good melons and running water, but he founded a dynasty that ruled for over three centuries.
story.zh:
巴布尔是一位失去故乡费尔干纳、转而统治喀布尔的帖木儿王子，此前已四次袭掠旁遮普。1525年底，他这次是来扎根的。他的回忆录记载其军队连同仆从在内约12,000人，他率此军在德里以北的帕尼帕特迎战苏丹易卜拉欣·洛迪约十万人和上千头战象的大军。

巴布尔借鉴了奥斯曼人的战术。他用生牛皮绳把约700辆大车连在一起，留出供骑兵冲锋的缺口，把火绳枪手以及由炮手乌斯塔德·阿里·库利和穆斯塔法掌管的火炮布置在车阵后面。1526年4月21日，易卜拉欣的军队正面冲击车阵；巴布尔的侧翼骑兵以中亚的“图鲁格玛”战术迂回包抄，向密集的敌阵放箭。到中午战斗就结束了，易卜拉欣和他的数千名士兵阵亡。

巴布尔派儿子胡马雍去夺取阿格拉的国库。他在回忆录《巴布尔纪》中抱怨印度没有好甜瓜和流水，但他建立的王朝统治了三个多世纪。

summary.en: Babur defeated the Rajput confederacy of Rana Sanga of Mewar near Fatehpur Sikri, securing Mughal control of the upper Ganges plain against its strongest rival.
summary.zh: 巴布尔在法塔赫布尔西格里附近击败梅瓦尔的拉纳·桑加所领导的拉其普特联盟，确保了莫卧儿王朝对恒河上游平原的控制。

sources.title: John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)

summary.en: Akbar’s regent Bairam Khan defeated Hemu, the Sur dynasty general who had just seized Delhi; Hemu was struck by an arrow and captured, restoring Mughal rule under the 14-year-old Akbar.
summary.zh: 阿克巴的摄政拜拉姆汗击败刚刚夺取德里的苏尔王朝将领赫穆；希穆中箭被俘，莫卧儿王朝在14岁的阿克巴治下得以复兴。

sources.title: John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)

story.en:
When Humayun died after falling down his library stairs in January 1556, his son Akbar was 13 and campaigning in the Punjab, and Mughal rule, restored in Delhi and Agra only the year before, was still fragile. In October Hemu, a Hindu merchant from Rewari who had risen to command the Sur armies and won some twenty battles, took Delhi and crowned himself Raja Vikramaditya.

Akbar’s guardian Bairam Khan marched to meet him. On 5 November the two armies met at Panipat, on the field where Babur had won thirty years earlier. Hemu, commanding from the back of an elephant, had the advantage at first, until an arrow struck him in the eye and he collapsed in his howdah. Seeing their leader fall, his troops fled.

The unconscious Hemu was brought to the Mughal camp, where Bairam Khan, or by some accounts the boy Akbar at his urging, beheaded him. Hemu’s head was sent to Kabul and his body hung at a gate of Delhi. The battle restored the Mughal Empire, and four years later Akbar took power in his own right.
story.zh:
1556年1月胡马雍从藏书楼台阶上摔下身亡时，其子阿克巴年仅13岁，正在旁遮普征战，而莫卧儿人前一年才收复德里和阿格拉，统治仍很脆弱。同年10月，出身雷瓦里的印度教商人赫穆攻占德里，自立为“超日王”；他已升任苏尔军队统帅，赢得过约二十场战役。

阿克巴的监护人拜拉姆汗率军迎战。11月5日，两军在帕尼帕特相遇，正是三十年前巴布尔获胜的战场。赫穆在象背上指挥，起初占据优势，直到一支箭射中他的眼睛，他倒在象轿中。士兵们见主帅倒下，四散奔逃。

昏迷的赫穆被带到莫卧儿营中，拜拉姆汗（或据某些记载，是少年阿克巴在他的催促下）将其斩首。赫穆的首级被送往喀布尔，尸身悬挂在德里城门上。这场战役恢复了莫卧儿帝国，四年后阿克巴亲政。

summary.en: An alliance of the Deccan sultanates defeated Vijayanagara’s regent Rama Raya, who was beheaded; the capital at Hampi was then sacked and the empire never regained its power.
summary.zh: 德干诸苏丹国联军击败毗奢耶那伽罗的摄政罗摩·罗耶，并将其斩首；都城亨比随后遭洗劫，帝国从此一蹶不振。

sources.title: Burton Stein, Vijayanagara (New Cambridge History of India I.2, 1989)

note: Some sources give 23 January 1565.

story.en:
In the 1550s Vijayanagara’s regent, Rama Raya, played the five Deccan sultanates against one another, allying now with one, now with another, and his armies sacked their towns. Alarmed, Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar set aside their feuds and allied in 1564, sealing the pact with royal marriages.

The armies met in January 1565 near the Krishna river, at Rakkasa-Tangadi south of Talikota. Vijayanagara’s army was larger, and the aged Rama Raya seemed to be winning. But the sultans’ artillery, firing at close range (later accounts say with bags of copper coins), tore into the attackers, and two Muslim commanders in Vijayanagara’s service are said to have changed sides. Rama Raya was captured and beheaded by Husain Nizam Shah of Ahmadnagar.

The royal family fled with the treasury, and for months the victors and local plunderers looted the undefended capital. The empire survived at Penukonda and Chandragiri for decades, but the great city was abandoned and never recovered.
story.zh:
16世纪50年代，毗奢耶那伽罗的摄政罗摩·罗耶在德干五苏丹国之间纵横捭阖，时而与这个结盟，时而与那个联手，他的军队还洗劫了它们的城镇。比贾布尔、艾哈迈德讷格尔、戈尔康达和比德尔深感惊恐，于1564年捐弃前嫌结成联盟，并以王室联姻巩固盟约。

1565年1月，两军在塔利科塔以南克里希纳河畔的拉卡萨-坦加迪相遇。毗奢耶那伽罗兵力更多，年迈的罗摩·罗耶起初似乎占了上风。但苏丹们的火炮在近距离开火（据后世记载用的是装满铜币的弹袋），重创进攻者；据说毗奢耶那伽罗麾下两名穆斯林将领临阵倒戈。罗摩·罗耶被俘，被艾哈迈德讷格尔的侯赛因·尼扎姆·沙斩首。

王室带着国库出逃，此后数月胜利者和当地劫掠者洗劫了不设防的都城。帝国在佩努孔达和钱德拉吉里又延续了数十年，但这座伟大的城市从此荒废，再未恢复元气。

summary.en: Mughal forces under Man Singh fought Maharana Pratap of Mewar in a narrow Aravalli pass; Pratap withdrew but kept up resistance and became a lasting emblem of Rajput defiance.
summary.zh: 曼·辛格率领的莫卧儿军队在阿拉瓦利山的狭窄山口与梅瓦尔的普拉塔普王交战；普拉塔普虽撤退但坚持抵抗，成为拉其普特人不屈的长久象征。

sources.title: John F. Richards, The Mughal Empire (New Cambridge History of India I.5, 1993)

name.zh: 阿克巴营建法塔赫布尔西格里

summary.en: Akbar raised a red-sandstone capital at Sikri to honour the Sufi Shaikh Salim Chishti, who had foretold the birth of his heir; it hosted his religious debates in the Ibadat Khana before the court left around 1585.
summary.zh: 阿克巴在西格里兴建红砂岩新都，以纪念曾预言其继承人诞生的苏菲长老萨利姆·契斯提；宫廷约1585年迁离之前，阿克巴在此的“礼拜堂”主持宗教辩论。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Fatehpur Sikri

note: Work began in 1569 (Wikidata); the city was proclaimed capital in 1571.

summary.en: Guru Arjan built the Harmandir Sahib in the sacred pool of Amritsar and installed the newly compiled Adi Granth there in 1604; rebuilt and gilded under Ranjit Singh, the Golden Temple is Sikhism’s holiest shrine.
summary.zh: 古鲁阿尔琼在阿姆利则圣池中建造哈曼迪尔寺，并于1604年将新编成的《阿迪·格兰特》供奉于此；该寺在兰吉特·辛格时期重建并贴金，即锡克教最神圣的金庙。

sources.title: J. S. Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (New Cambridge History of India II.3, 1990)

note: The 1589 foundation follows Wikidata; some accounts place the start in 1581 or 1588.

summary.en: Shah Jahan commissioned this white-marble mausoleum at Agra for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631; built by thousands of artisans over two decades, it is the masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
summary.zh: 沙贾汗为1631年去世的皇后慕塔芝·玛哈在阿格拉修建这座白色大理石陵墓；数千名工匠历时二十余年建成，是莫卧儿建筑的巅峰之作。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List: Taj Mahal
Ebba Koch, The Complete Taj Mahal (2006)

story.en:
Mumtaz Mahal, Shah Jahan’s favourite wife, died in June 1631 at Burhanpur in the Deccan giving birth to their fourteenth child; she had accompanied him on campaign. The grieving emperor, court historians say, withdrew into mourning and gave up music and fine dress for two years. Her body was later brought to Agra, where work on a tomb began on the bank of the Yamuna.

The complex, planned as a garden paradise with the tomb at the river end, took over twenty years. Some 20,000 workers are said to have been employed; white marble came from Makrana in Rajasthan, and inlays of jasper, lapis, carnelian and other stones from across Asia. The chief architect is usually named as Ustad Ahmad Lahauri.

In 1658 Shah Jahan was deposed by his son Aurangzeb and confined in Agra Fort, from where, tradition says, he gazed at the tomb until his death in 1666. He was buried beside Mumtaz, the one conspicuous break in the design’s symmetry. The story of a matching black Taj across the river is a later legend.
story.zh:
沙贾汗最宠爱的妻子慕塔芝·玛哈随他出征德干，1631年6月在布尔汉布尔生下第十四个孩子时去世。据宫廷史家记载，悲痛的皇帝闭门服丧，两年间不听音乐、不穿华服。她的遗体后来被运回阿格拉，在亚穆纳河畔开始兴建陵墓。

整个建筑群被规划为天堂花园，陵墓位于临河一端，耗时二十余年。据说动用了约两万名工匠；白色大理石采自拉贾斯坦的马克拉纳，镶嵌所用的碧玉、青金石、红玉髓等宝石来自亚洲各地。总建筑师通常被认为是乌斯塔德·艾哈迈德·拉霍里。

1658年沙贾汗被儿子奥朗则布废黜，软禁在阿格拉堡；相传他在那里凝望陵墓，直到1666年去世。他被葬在慕塔芝身旁，这是整个设计中最明显打破对称的地方。所谓河对岸还有一座黑色泰姬陵的说法，是后来的传说。

summary.en: Nader Shah of Persia routed the far larger army of the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah, then occupied and plundered Delhi, carrying off the Peacock Throne and exposing Mughal weakness.
summary.zh: 波斯的纳迪尔沙击溃兵力远胜于己的莫卧儿皇帝穆罕默德·沙的军队，随即占领并劫掠德里，掠走孔雀宝座，莫卧儿王朝的衰弱暴露无遗。

sources.title: Michael Axworthy, The Sword of Persia (2006)

story.en:
Nader Shah, a former bandit who had driven the Afghans out of Persia and made himself shah in 1736, turned on Mughal India in 1738, using as pretext the shelter it gave to Afghan fugitives. He took Kabul, crossed the Khyber and met the Mughal army of the emperor Muhammad Shah at Karnal, north of Delhi, on 24 February 1739.

The Mughal camp was huge but divided between rival nobles, and the battle lasted only a few hours. Nader’s musketeers and swivel guns mounted on camels broke the Mughal charges, the general Khan Dauran was mortally wounded, and the emperor soon submitted.

Nader entered Delhi in March. When a rumour of his death sparked attacks on his soldiers, he ordered a massacre in which some 20,000 to 30,000 people died in a single day. He left in May with the imperial treasury, the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond, wealth so great that he cancelled Persia’s taxes for three years. The Mughal Empire never recovered its prestige.
story.zh:
纳迪尔沙原是一名盗匪，他把阿富汗人赶出波斯，并于1736年自立为沙。1738年他以莫卧儿印度收留阿富汗逃犯为借口进攻印度，攻取喀布尔，越过开伯尔山口，1739年2月24日在德里以北的卡尔纳尔与莫卧儿皇帝穆罕默德·沙的大军相遇。

莫卧儿大营规模庞大，却被相互倾轧的贵族分割，战斗只持续了几个小时。纳迪尔的火枪手和架在骆驼背上的回旋炮打垮了莫卧儿军的冲锋，大将汗·道兰受了致命伤，皇帝随后屈服求和。

纳迪尔于3月进入德里。一则他已死去的谣言引发了对其士兵的袭击，他便下令屠城，一天之内约有两三万人遇难。5月他带着帝国国库、孔雀宝座和光之山钻石离去，财富之多使他免除了波斯三年的赋税。莫卧儿帝国的威望从此一蹶不振。

summary.en: Robert Clive’s East India Company force defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, Nawab of Bengal, after his commander Mir Jafar defected; the battle made the Company the power behind the Bengal throne and began British territorial rule in India.
summary.zh: 罗伯特·克莱武率领的东印度公司军队在孟加拉纳瓦布西拉吉·乌德-达乌拉的将领米尔·贾法尔倒戈后将其击败；公司由此操纵孟加拉政权，英国在印度的领土统治自此开始。

sources.title: P. J. Marshall, Bengal: The British Bridgehead (New Cambridge History of India II.2, 1987)

story.en:
In June 1756 the young Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah, angered by the East India Company’s fortifications and abuse of trade privileges, captured Calcutta. Some of the British prisoners died overnight in a cramped guardroom, the “Black Hole”, an episode later inflated in British memory. Robert Clive came from Madras with troops, retook Calcutta and began negotiating secretly with the nawab’s discontented courtiers and with the banking house of the Jagat Seths.

The deal was that Mir Jafar, the nawab’s commander-in-chief, would stand aside and become nawab himself. On 23 June 1757 Clive, with about 3,000 men, faced some 50,000 in a mango grove at Palashi. A monsoon downpour soaked the nawab’s gunpowder while the British kept theirs covered, Mir Jafar’s large division did not move, and by the end of the day the nawab’s army had melted away. Siraj fled and was soon murdered.

Mir Jafar paid huge sums to the Company and to Clive personally. Within a decade the Company was the real ruler of Bengal, the richest province of India, and used its revenues to conquer the rest.
story.zh:
1756年6月，年轻的孟加拉纳瓦布西拉吉·乌德-达乌拉因东印度公司擅建防御工事、滥用贸易特权而大怒，攻占了加尔各答。一些英国俘虏在一间狭小的禁闭室里过夜时死去，这就是“黑洞”事件，后来在英国人的记忆中被夸大。罗伯特·克莱武率军从马德拉斯赶来，收复加尔各答，并开始与纳瓦布心怀不满的廷臣以及贾加特·塞特银行家族秘密谈判。

交易的内容是：纳瓦布的总司令米尔·贾法尔按兵不动，事后自己出任纳瓦布。1757年6月23日，克莱武率约3,000人，在帕拉希的芒果林中迎战约五万敌军。一场季风暴雨淋湿了纳瓦布的火药，英军则把火药遮盖得好好的；米尔·贾法尔的大部队纹丝不动；到傍晚时分，纳瓦布的军队已土崩瓦解。西拉吉出逃，不久被杀。

米尔·贾法尔向公司和克莱武本人支付了巨额款项。不到十年，公司成了印度最富庶的孟加拉省的真正统治者，并用其税收征服了印度其余地方。

summary.en: Ahmad Shah Durrani’s Afghan army, with Rohilla and Awadh allies, crushed the Maratha army under Sadashivrao Bhau in one of the largest battles of the 18th century, halting Maratha expansion in the north.
summary.zh: 艾哈迈德·沙·杜兰尼的阿富汗军队联合罗赫拉人和奥德军队，击溃萨达希夫拉奥·鲍率领的马拉塔大军；这是18世纪规模最大的战役之一，遏止了马拉塔人向北扩张。

sources.title: Stewart Gordon, The Marathas 1600–1818 (New Cambridge History of India II.4, 1993)

story.en:
By the 1750s Maratha armies were collecting tribute as far north as the Punjab, which brought them into conflict with Ahmad Shah Durrani, the Afghan ruler who claimed it. The Peshwa sent a great army north under his cousin Sadashivrao Bhau, accompanied by tens of thousands of pilgrims and camp followers.

The two armies dug in facing each other at Panipat for two months in the winter of 1760–61. Durrani’s forces cut the Maratha supply lines and the camp starved. On 14 January 1761 the Marathas broke out and attacked. Their guns and musketeers under Ibrahim Khan Gardi, who had learnt French methods under Bussy, did great damage, but in the afternoon Durrani committed his reserves, and the Peshwa’s son Vishwasrao was killed. The Bhau charged into the fight and disappeared. Tens of thousands of soldiers and non-combatants were killed in battle or in the slaughter that followed.

A famous message reached the Peshwa in coded words: two pearls dissolved, 27 gold coins lost, silver and copper beyond counting. Durrani went home, but the Marathas’ northern expansion was checked just as the British were rising in Bengal.
story.zh:
到18世纪50年代，马拉塔军队已北上至旁遮普征收贡赋，与声称拥有旁遮普的阿富汗统治者艾哈迈德·沙·杜兰尼发生冲突。佩什瓦派堂弟萨达希夫拉奥·鲍率大军北上，随军还有数以万计的朝圣者和随营人员。

1760至1761年冬，两军在帕尼帕特挖壕对峙两个月。杜兰尼军切断了马拉塔人的补给线，营中断粮。1761年1月14日，马拉塔人突围进攻。曾在布西麾下习得法式战法的易卜拉欣汗·加尔迪所率的火炮和火枪兵给敌军造成重创，但下午杜兰尼投入预备队，佩什瓦之子维什瓦斯拉奥阵亡。鲍冲入战阵后下落不明。数万名士兵和非战斗人员死于战场或随后的屠杀。

一封著名的暗语信送到佩什瓦手中：两颗珍珠溶化了，27枚金币丢失了，银币和铜币不计其数。杜兰尼回国了，但就在英国人在孟加拉崛起之际，马拉塔人向北的扩张被遏止。

summary.en: Company troops under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II; the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) then gave the Company the revenue rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
summary.zh: 赫克托·芒罗率领的东印度公司军队击败米尔·卡西姆、奥德的舒贾·乌德-达乌拉与莫卧儿皇帝沙·阿拉姆二世的联军；1765年的《阿拉哈巴德条约》使公司获得孟加拉、比哈尔和奥里萨的财税权。

sources.title: P. J. Marshall, Bengal: The British Bridgehead (New Cambridge History of India II.2, 1987)

note: Standard histories date the battle 22–23 October 1764; Wikidata records 6 November 1764, which appears to be an error.

story.en:
After Plassey the Company made and unmade nawabs. Mir Qasim, whom it installed in 1760, proved too independent: he moved his capital to Monghyr, modernised his army and tried to stop Company servants trading duty-free. War broke out in 1763; defeated, he fled west to Awadh and formed an alliance with its nawab, Shuja-ud-Daulah, and the fugitive Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

On 22–23 October 1764 their combined army, perhaps 40,000 strong, met about 7,000 Company troops, most of them Indian sepoys, under Major Hector Munro at Buxar on the Ganges. Discipline and artillery told; the allies were routed within hours.

The settlement mattered more than the battle. By the Treaty of Allahabad (1765) Clive restored Awadh to Shuja and received from Shah Alam the diwani, the right to collect the revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, in return for an annual tribute. A trading company had become, in law, an officer of the Mughal emperor governing tens of millions of people.
story.zh:
普拉西之战后，东印度公司随意废立纳瓦布。1760年由公司扶植的米尔·卡西姆却过于独立：他把首府迁到蒙吉尔，改革军队，并试图阻止公司职员免税经商。1763年战争爆发；战败后他西逃奥德，与奥德纳瓦布舒贾·乌德-达乌拉以及流亡的莫卧儿皇帝沙·阿拉姆二世结成联盟。

1764年10月22至23日，三方约四万人的联军在恒河畔的布克萨尔迎战赫克托·芒罗少校统率的约7,000名公司军队，其中大多数是印度籍士兵。纪律与火炮决定了胜负，联军在数小时内溃败。

战后的安排比战役本身更重要。根据《阿拉哈巴德条约》（1765年），克莱武把奥德归还舒贾，并从沙·阿拉姆手中获得孟加拉、比哈尔和奥里萨的“迪瓦尼”（征税权），条件是每年进贡。一家贸易公司在法律上成了莫卧儿皇帝的官员，统治着数千万人。

summary.en: Four wars between the East India Company and Mysore under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, whose rocket corps and French ties made them the Company’s most formidable southern foe; they ended with Mysore reduced to a subsidiary state.
summary.zh: 东印度公司与海德尔·阿里和蒂普苏丹统治下的迈索尔之间的四次战争；迈索尔凭借火箭部队和与法国的联系，成为公司在南印度最强劲的对手，最终沦为附属国。

sources.title: Kate Brittlebank, Tipu Sultan’s Search for Legitimacy (1997)

note: Plotted at Srirangapatna, Mysore’s capital; Wikidata gives a generic point (13°N 77°E) for the wars.

summary.en: British and Hyderabad troops stormed Tipu Sultan’s island capital; Tipu was killed defending a breach, and the Company restored the Wodeyar dynasty over a reduced Mysore.
summary.zh: 英军与海得拉巴军队攻陷蒂普苏丹的河洲都城；蒂普在城墙缺口处战死，公司随后在缩小了的迈索尔恢复沃迪亚尔王朝。

sources.title: Kate Brittlebank, Tipu Sultan’s Search for Legitimacy (1997)

summary.en: After a revolt at Multan, Company armies fought the Sikh Khalsa at Chillianwala and Gujrat; victory led to the annexation of the Punjab in March 1849 and the exile of the boy-maharaja Duleep Singh.
summary.zh: 木尔坦叛乱后，东印度公司军队在奇利安瓦拉和古杰拉特与锡克卡尔萨军交战；获胜后于1849年3月吞并旁遮普，少年土邦主杜利普·辛格被流放。

sources.title: J. S. Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (New Cambridge History of India II.3, 1990)

note: Plotted at Gujrat, site of the decisive battle (21 February 1849).

summary.en: Beginning with a sepoy mutiny at Meerut, revolt spread across north and central India, rallying around the Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah II; after its suppression the Crown abolished Company rule and ended the Mughal dynasty.
summary.zh: 起义始于密拉特的印度兵哗变，迅速蔓延至北印度和中印度，起义者拥戴莫卧儿皇帝巴哈杜尔·沙二世；镇压之后，英国王室废除东印度公司统治，莫卧儿王朝亦告终结。

story.en:
The spark was the Enfield rifle, whose cartridges, sepoys believed, were greased with cow and pig fat. Deeper grievances lay behind it: annexations such as Awadh in 1856, the doctrine of lapse that let the Company seize states without a natural heir, land revenue demands and fear of forced conversion.

On 10 May 1857 sepoys at Meerut, angered by the public humiliation of comrades jailed for refusing the cartridges, shot their officers and rode to Delhi, where they proclaimed the aged Mughal Bahadur Shah II their emperor. The revolt spread through the Ganges plain and central India. At Kanpur, besieged British men, women and children were killed after a promise of safe conduct; British columns retaliated by hanging villagers and blowing rebels from cannon.

Delhi was retaken in September after a long siege, and Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died fighting at Gwalior in June 1858. Bahadur Shah was exiled to Rangoon. Parliament abolished the East India Company’s rule, and Queen Victoria’s proclamation of November 1858 promised religious non-interference.
story.zh:
导火索是恩菲尔德步枪，印度兵相信它的弹药纸筒涂有牛油和猪油。其背后有更深层的不满：1856年吞并奥德等兼并行动，允许公司夺取无亲生继承人之邦国的“无嗣失权”原则，沉重的田赋，以及对被迫改宗的恐惧。

1857年5月10日，密拉特的印度兵因拒用弹药而入狱的同伴遭到当众羞辱，愤而射杀军官，骑马奔向德里，拥立年迈的莫卧儿君主巴哈杜尔·沙二世为皇帝。起义蔓延到恒河平原和印度中部。在坎普尔，被围困的英国男女老幼在得到安全撤离的承诺后遭到杀害；英军纵队则以绞死村民、用炮口炸死起义者进行报复。

经过长期围攻，英军于9月收复德里；1858年6月，詹西女王拉克希米·巴伊在瓜廖尔战死。巴哈杜尔·沙被流放仰光。议会废除了东印度公司的统治，1858年11月维多利亚女王发表公告，承诺不干涉宗教。

summary.en: Seventy-two delegates met in Bombay for the first session of the Indian National Congress, convened with the help of A. O. Hume; it became the main vehicle of the independence movement.
summary.zh: 72名代表在孟买召开印度国民大会党首届会议，会议得到休谟协助召集；国大党后来成为独立运动的主要力量。

story.en:
By the 1880s a new class of English-educated Indian lawyers, teachers and journalists had formed associations in the presidency towns, and the Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883, when Europeans protested against Indian judges trying them, had shown them both British racial attitudes and the value of organised agitation.

Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, helped bring them together. The first session met on 28 December 1885 at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay, moved from Poona because of a cholera outbreak. Seventy-two delegates attended, chaired by the Calcutta barrister W. C. Bonnerjee. They passed loyal resolutions asking for more Indians in the councils and the civil service.

For two decades the Congress remained a moderate body of petitions. Dadabhai Naoroji, who presided in 1886, developed the theory that British rule was draining India’s wealth. After 1905 younger leaders such as Tilak demanded self-rule, and under Gandhi from 1920 the Congress became a mass movement.
story.zh:
到19世纪80年代，各管区城市里一批受英语教育的印度律师、教师和记者组建了各种协会。1883年的伊尔伯特法案之争中，欧洲人抗议由印度法官审理他们的案件，这让他们既看清了英国人的种族态度，也看到了有组织鼓动的价值。

退休的英国文官艾伦·奥克塔维安·休姆帮助把他们联合起来。首届年会于1885年12月28日在孟买的戈库尔达斯·特杰帕尔梵文学院召开，原定在浦那举行，因霍乱流行而改址。72名代表出席，由加尔各答大律师W. C. 邦纳吉主持。会议通过了措辞恭顺的决议，要求让更多印度人进入立法会议和文官系统。

此后二十年，国大党一直是以请愿为主的温和团体。1886年担任主席的达达拜·瑙罗吉提出英国统治使印度财富“外流”的理论。1905年后，提拉克等年轻领袖要求自治；1920年起在甘地领导下，国大党成为群众运动。

summary.en: Viceroy Lord Curzon split Bengal, separating the largely Muslim east; mass protest and the Swadeshi boycott forced its reversal in 1911, when the capital of British India also moved from Calcutta to Delhi.
summary.zh: 总督寇松将孟加拉一分为二，使以穆斯林为主的东部独立成省；大规模抗议和“司瓦德西”抵制运动迫使英国于1911年撤销分治，同年英属印度首都由加尔各答迁往德里。

sources.title: Sumit Sarkar, The Swadeshi Movement in Bengal 1903–1908 (1973)

name.zh: 阿姆利则惨案（扎连瓦拉园惨案）

summary.en: Troops under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fired without warning on a crowd in an enclosed garden at Amritsar, killing hundreds (379 by the official count, many more by Indian estimates); it turned many moderates against British rule.
summary.zh: 戴尔准将率部在阿姆利则一处封闭园地内不加警告地向人群开枪，造成数百人死亡（官方统计379人，印方估计远多于此），使许多温和派转而反对英国统治。

sources.title: Kim A. Wagner, Amritsar 1919: An Empire of Fear and the Making of a Massacre (2019)

story.en:
In spring 1919 the Rowlatt Act extended wartime powers of detention without trial, and Gandhi called a nationwide protest. In Amritsar the arrest of two local leaders led to riots on 10 April in which several Europeans were killed; the next day a woman missionary was beaten. Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer took command and banned public meetings, though the order was poorly announced.

On the afternoon of 13 April, the Baisakhi festival, a crowd of perhaps 10,000 to 20,000, including many villagers in town for the fair, gathered in the Jallianwala Bagh, a walled garden with few narrow exits. Dyer arrived with 50 riflemen, blocked the main entrance and, without warning, ordered fire. The shooting went on for about ten minutes, until the ammunition ran low. Many people jumped into a well to escape.

The official count was 379 dead; Indian estimates were around a thousand or more. Dyer told the Hunter Committee that he had meant to produce a moral effect throughout the Punjab. Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest, and the massacre turned Gandhi and millions of others against the Empire.
story.zh:
1919年春，《罗拉特法》延长了战时未经审判即可拘押的权力，甘地号召全国抗议。在阿姆利则，两名当地领袖被捕引发了4月10日的骚乱，数名欧洲人被杀；次日一名女传教士遭殴打。准将雷金纳德·戴尔接管指挥，下令禁止公共集会，但命令并未广泛传达。

4月13日下午正值拜萨基节，约一万至两万人聚集在扎连瓦拉园，其中许多是进城赶集的村民。这是一座四面围墙、只有几个狭窄出口的园子。戴尔带着50名步枪手赶到，堵住主入口，未经警告即下令开枪。射击持续约十分钟，直到弹药将尽。许多人为逃命跳进一口井里。

官方统计死亡379人，印度方面估计约有一千人甚至更多。戴尔对亨特委员会说，他是要在整个旁遮普产生一种“震慑效果”。泰戈尔为此放弃了爵士称号，这场屠杀使甘地和千百万人转而反对帝国。

summary.en: Gandhi and 78 followers walked about 390 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to make salt in defiance of the British salt tax; the march launched nationwide civil disobedience and drew world attention.
summary.zh: 甘地与78名追随者从萨巴尔马蒂修道院步行约390公里至丹迪海边自行制盐，以抗议英国的盐税；此举掀起全国性的不合作运动，引起世界关注。

label.zh: 萨巴尔马蒂修道院（3月12日）

sources.title: Judith M. Brown, Gandhi: Prisoner of Hope (1989)
Thomas Weber, On the Salt March (1997)

story.en:
The Congress had declared complete independence its goal on 26 January 1930 and asked Gandhi to begin civil disobedience. Many colleagues were puzzled when he chose the salt tax as the target. But every Indian needed salt, the British monopoly forbade collecting it from the sea, and the issue cut across class and religion.

On 12 March Gandhi, aged 60, set out from his Sabarmati Ashram at Ahmedabad with 78 chosen followers. They walked about 390 km in 24 days, stopping in villages where Gandhi preached against untouchability and liquor, while newsreel cameras and foreign correspondents followed. On the morning of 6 April at Dandi he picked up a lump of natural salt from the mudflats and declared that he was shaking the foundations of the British Empire.

Across India people made salt, boycotted foreign cloth and refused taxes, and some 60,000 were jailed. At the Dharasana salt works in May, the American reporter Webb Miller described volunteers walking forward in rows to be beaten down by police without raising a hand. The march made Gandhi a world figure.
story.zh:
1930年1月26日，国大党宣布以完全独立为目标，并请甘地发起公民不服从运动。当甘地选定盐税作为目标时，许多同事感到不解。但每个印度人都需要盐，英国的专卖制度禁止从海中取盐，这一问题跨越了阶级与宗教。

3月12日，60岁的甘地带着78名精选的追随者从艾哈迈达巴德的萨巴尔马蒂修道院出发。他们在24天里步行约390公里，沿途在村庄停留，甘地宣讲反对不可接触制和酗酒，新闻摄影机和外国记者一路跟随。4月6日清晨，他在丹迪的海滩泥滩上拾起一块天然盐，宣称自己正在动摇大英帝国的根基。

印度各地民众纷纷煮盐、抵制洋布、拒绝纳税，约六万人入狱。5月在达拉萨纳盐场，美国记者韦伯·米勒描写志愿者一排排向前走去，被警察打倒在地，却始终不举手还击。食盐进军使甘地成为世界性人物。

summary.en: At its Lahore session the All-India Muslim League under Jinnah demanded independent states for the Muslim-majority regions of north-western and eastern India—the founding demand of the Pakistan movement.
summary.zh: 全印穆斯林联盟在真纳领导下于拉合尔年会上要求在印度西北部和东部穆斯林占多数的地区建立独立国家，这成为巴基斯坦运动的纲领性诉求。

note: Moved on 23 March and adopted on 24 March 1940.

story.en:
The 1937 provincial elections convinced Muhammad Ali Jinnah that Muslims could not expect fair treatment from Congress governments, which had refused to share power with the Muslim League in the United Provinces. By 1940, with the Congress ministries resigned over the war, the League had grown rapidly.

At its session in Lahore’s Minto Park on 22–24 March 1940, Jinnah told a vast crowd that Hindus and Muslims were two nations with different religions, philosophies and literatures. The resolution, moved by A. K. Fazlul Huq of Bengal, demanded that the Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east of India be grouped into “independent states”, autonomous and sovereign.

The word Pakistan does not appear in the text; Hindu newspapers called it the Pakistan Resolution, and the name stuck. Bengali politicians would later argue that its plural “states” had promised a separate eastern state. In 1946 the League changed it to one state. The site is now marked by the Minar-e-Pakistan, and 23 March is Pakistan Day.
story.zh:
1937年的省级选举使穆罕默德·阿里·真纳相信，穆斯林无法指望国大党政府的公平对待，因为国大党拒绝在联合省与穆斯林联盟分享权力。到1940年，国大党各省政府因战争问题辞职，穆斯林联盟迅速壮大。

1940年3月22至24日，联盟在拉合尔明托公园举行年会，真纳对广大群众说，印度教徒和穆斯林是宗教、哲学和文学各不相同的两个民族。由孟加拉的A. K. 法兹卢尔·哈克提出的决议要求，把印度西北部和东部穆斯林占多数的地区组成自治、主权的“独立国家”（复数）。

决议文本中没有出现“巴基斯坦”一词；印度教报纸称之为“巴基斯坦决议”，这个名称便流传开来。孟加拉政治人物后来认为，“国家”一词的复数形式意味着东部应单独建国。1946年联盟把它改为单一国家。会址如今立有巴基斯坦塔，3月23日是巴基斯坦日。

summary.en: British India was divided into the dominions of India and Pakistan at midnight on 14–15 August 1947; the partition of Punjab and Bengal brought communal massacres and displaced roughly 12–15 million people.
summary.zh: 1947年8月14日至15日午夜，英属印度分为印度和巴基斯坦两个自治领；旁遮普和孟加拉的分割引发教派屠杀，约1200万至1500万人流离失所。

sources.title: Yasmin Khan, The Great Partition: The Making of India and Pakistan (2007)

story.en:
In February 1947 the British government announced it would leave India by June 1948. The last viceroy, Lord Mountbatten, decided within weeks that the Congress and the Muslim League could not agree on a united India, and brought the date forward to August 1947. The boundaries of Punjab and Bengal were drawn in five weeks by Cyril Radcliffe, a lawyer who had never visited India, and published only two days after independence.

At midnight on 14–15 August Nehru told the Constituent Assembly in Delhi that India was awaking “to life and freedom”; Pakistan celebrated its independence on 14 August, with Jinnah as governor-general in Karachi. Gandhi spent the day in Calcutta, fasting and trying to calm communal violence.

In Punjab, Hindus, Sikhs and Muslims fled in both directions, and trains arrived full of the dead. Estimates of those killed range from 200,000 to two million, and 12 to 15 million people were uprooted, one of the largest migrations in history. Tens of thousands of women were abducted. The violence shaped relations between India and Pakistan ever after.
story.zh:
1947年2月，英国政府宣布将于1948年6月前撤离印度。末任总督蒙巴顿勋爵在几周内就断定国大党和穆斯林联盟无法就统一的印度达成一致，于是把撤离日期提前到1947年8月。旁遮普和孟加拉的分界线由从未到过印度的律师西里尔·拉德克利夫在五周内划定，直到独立两天后才公布。

8月14日至15日午夜，尼赫鲁在德里对制宪会议说，印度正在苏醒，迎来“生命与自由”；巴基斯坦于8月14日庆祝独立，真纳在卡拉奇出任总督。甘地这一天待在加尔各答，以绝食努力平息教派暴力。

在旁遮普，印度教徒、锡克教徒和穆斯林向相反方向逃难，列车运到时满载尸体。死亡人数估计从二十万到两百万不等，一千二百万至一千五百万人背井离乡，这是历史上规模最大的迁徙之一。数万名妇女被掳。这场暴力此后一直影响着印巴关系。

summary.en: Ceylon became an independent dominion within the Commonwealth under Prime Minister D. S. Senanayake; it became the Republic of Sri Lanka in 1972.
summary.zh: 锡兰在总理森那那亚克领导下成为英联邦内的独立自治领，1972年改为斯里兰卡共和国。

sources.title: K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (1981)

note: No Wikidata item exists for the independence event itself (checked 2026-11): Q2670092 (Dominion of Ceylon) is the polity and Q6016023 the annual Independence Day holiday, so no QID is given here.

name.en: Constitution of India comes into force

summary.en: Drafted by the Constituent Assembly, with B. R. Ambedkar chairing its drafting committee, the constitution made India a sovereign democratic republic with universal adult suffrage.
summary.zh: 由制宪会议起草、安贝德卡尔主持起草委员会的宪法正式生效，印度成为实行成人普选的主权民主共和国。

sources.title: Granville Austin, The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation (1966)

story.en:
The Constituent Assembly first met in December 1946, before independence, and sat for almost three years. Its 299 members, most from the Congress, included lawyers, princes’ representatives, 15 women and leaders of the depressed classes. B. R. Ambedkar, once a fierce critic of the Congress, chaired the drafting committee.

The result, adopted on 26 November 1949, was one of the longest constitutions in the world, drawing on the British parliamentary system, the American bill of rights and judicial review, and Irish directive principles. It abolished untouchability, guaranteed equality before the law and gave every adult a vote, at a time when most Indians were poor and illiterate, a step many observers thought reckless.

It came into force on 26 January 1950, chosen because on that date in 1930 the Congress had declared its goal of complete independence. Rajendra Prasad became the first president. In his final speech Ambedkar warned that India was entering a life of contradictions: equality in politics and inequality in social and economic life.
story.zh:
制宪会议在独立之前的1946年12月首次开会，历时近三年。299名成员大多来自国大党，其中有律师、土邦代表、15名女性和受压迫阶层领袖。曾激烈批评国大党的B. R. 安贝德卡尔担任起草委员会主席。

1949年11月26日通过的宪法是世界上最长的宪法之一，借鉴了英国议会制、美国权利法案和司法审查以及爱尔兰的指导原则。它废除不可接触制，保障法律面前人人平等，并给予每个成年人选举权；当时大多数印度人贫穷且不识字，许多观察者认为这一步过于冒险。

宪法于1950年1月26日生效，选择这一天是因为1930年的这一天国大党宣布了完全独立的目标。拉金德拉·普拉萨德成为首任总统。安贝德卡尔在最后的演讲中警告说，印度正在进入一种充满矛盾的生活：政治上平等，社会和经济生活中却不平等。

summary.en: After Pakistan’s army cracked down in East Pakistan in March 1971, Bengali forces fought for independence; millions fled to India, which intervened in December, and Pakistani forces surrendered at Dhaka on 16 December.
summary.zh: 1971年3月巴基斯坦军队在东巴基斯坦实施镇压后，孟加拉人武装争取独立；数百万难民逃往印度，印度于12月出兵干预，巴军于12月16日在达卡投降。

sources.title: Srinath Raghavan, 1971: A Global History of the Creation of Bangladesh (2013)

story.en:
In the December 1970 elections Sheikh Mujibur Rahman’s Awami League won 160 of East Pakistan’s 162 general seats, a majority in the whole national assembly. The military government of Yahya Khan and the West Pakistani politician Zulfikar Ali Bhutto would not let him form a government. Talks failed, and on the night of 25 March 1971 the army launched Operation Searchlight in Dhaka, attacking the university, police barracks and Hindu neighbourhoods. Mujib was arrested; a declaration of independence was broadcast from Chittagong.

Over the following months the army and allied militias killed large numbers of civilians, estimated at anywhere from about 300,000 to three million (the official Bangladeshi figure), and committed mass rapes; about ten million refugees crossed into India. Bengali soldiers and students formed the Mukti Bahini guerrilla army, trained and supplied by India.

After Pakistan bombed Indian airfields on 3 December, India entered the war openly. In thirteen days Indian and Bangladeshi forces converged on Dhaka, and on 16 December General A. A. K. Niazi surrendered; about 93,000 Pakistani soldiers and officials became prisoners of war. Mujib returned in January 1972 to lead the new state of Bangladesh.
story.zh:
在1970年12月的选举中，谢赫·穆吉布·拉赫曼领导的人民联盟赢得东巴基斯坦162个普通议席中的160席，在整个国民议会中占多数。叶海亚·汗的军政府和西巴基斯坦政治家佐勒菲卡尔·阿里·布托却不让他组阁。谈判破裂后，1971年3月25日夜，军队在达卡发动“探照灯行动”，袭击大学、警察营地和印度教徒聚居区。穆吉布被捕；吉大港电台播出了独立宣言。

此后数月，军队及其附属民兵杀害了大批平民，估计数字从约30万到300万（孟加拉国官方数字）不等，并大规模施暴；约一千万难民逃入印度。孟加拉军人和学生组成“解放军”游击队，由印度训练和补给。

12月3日巴基斯坦轰炸印度机场后，印度公开参战。十三天内，印度和孟加拉部队向达卡合围；12月16日，A. A. K. 尼亚齐将军投降，约九万三千名巴基斯坦军人和官员成为战俘。1972年1月穆吉布回国，领导新生的孟加拉国。

summary.en: War between the Sri Lankan state and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, who sought a separate Tamil state in the north and east, killed an estimated 80,000 to 100,000 or more people; it ended with the army’s defeat of the LTTE in May 2009.
summary.zh: 斯里兰卡政府与谋求在北部和东部建立泰米尔国家的“泰米尔伊拉姆猛虎解放组织”之间的战争估计造成8万至10万甚至更多人死亡，2009年5月政府军击败猛虎组织后结束。

sources.title: K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka, rev. ed. (2005)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sri Lankan Civil War

story.en:
After independence, Sinhala-majority governments made Sinhala the sole official language (1956), limited Tamil access to universities and settled Sinhalese farmers in Tamil areas. Peaceful Tamil protest gave way to militant groups, of which the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) under Velupillai Prabhakaran became dominant, eliminating rival Tamil groups.

In July 1983 the Tigers killed 13 soldiers near Jaffna; in the anti-Tamil riots that followed in Colombo, hundreds or perhaps thousands of Tamils were killed, and the war began in earnest. An Indian peacekeeping force (1987–90) ended up fighting the Tigers. The LTTE built a navy and a suicide squad, assassinated Rajiv Gandhi in 1991 and the Sri Lankan president Premadasa in 1993, and ran a de facto state in the north.

A Norwegian-brokered ceasefire in 2002 collapsed. In 2008–09 the army pushed the Tigers and some 300,000 civilians into a narrow coastal strip at Mullaitivu. Prabhakaran was killed in May 2009. A UN panel found credible allegations of serious violations by both the army and the Tigers, and that tens of thousands of civilians may have died in the final months.
story.zh:
独立后，以僧伽罗人为主的政府把僧伽罗语定为唯一官方语言（1956年），限制泰米尔人进入大学，并在泰米尔地区安置僧伽罗农民。泰米尔人的和平抗议逐渐让位于武装团体，其中韦卢皮莱·普拉巴卡兰领导的“泰米尔伊拉姆猛虎解放组织”剪除其他泰米尔团体，占据主导。

1983年7月，猛虎组织在贾夫纳附近杀死13名士兵；随后科伦坡爆发反泰米尔骚乱，数百甚至数千名泰米尔人被杀，战争全面爆发。印度维和部队（1987–1990年）最终与猛虎组织兵戎相见。猛虎组织建立了海军和自杀突击队，1991年刺杀拉吉夫·甘地，1993年刺杀斯里兰卡总统普雷马达萨，并在北部建立了事实上的政权。

2002年挪威斡旋的停火破裂。2008至2009年，政府军把猛虎组织和约30万平民压缩到穆莱蒂武狭窄的沿海地带。2009年5月普拉巴卡兰被击毙。联合国专家小组认为，政府军和猛虎组织双方都有严重违法行为的可信指控，最后几个月可能有数万平民死亡。

summary.en: Methyl isocyanate gas escaped from a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, killing thousands within days and injuring hundreds of thousands—the world’s worst industrial disaster.
summary.zh: 博帕尔一家联合碳化物公司农药厂泄漏异氰酸甲酯毒气，数日内致数千人死亡，数十万人受伤，是世界上最严重的工业灾难。

sources.title: Edward Broughton, “The Bhopal disaster and its aftermath: a review”, Environmental Health 4 (2005)

story.en:
Union Carbide India built its pesticide plant on the edge of Bhopal’s old city, next to crowded slums. By 1984 it was losing money; safety systems had been cut back or switched off, and a refrigeration unit meant to keep the toxic methyl isocyanate cool had been shut down.

Late on 2 December water entered tank 610, which held about 42 tonnes of MIC. The reaction drove up heat and pressure, and shortly after midnight some 30 to 40 tonnes of gas escaped through a vent. The heavy cloud drifted over sleeping neighbourhoods. People woke coughing and blinded and ran into the streets, where many collapsed. The Madhya Pradesh government later put the death toll at about 3,800; other estimates put deaths in the first weeks near 8,000, and deaths from the after-effects in the years since at many thousands more.

In 1989 Union Carbide paid $470 million in a settlement with the Indian government, widely criticised as inadequate. The site was never fully cleaned, and contaminated groundwater still affects nearby residents.
story.zh:
印度联合碳化物公司把农药厂建在博帕尔老城边缘，紧挨着拥挤的贫民窟。到1984年工厂已经亏损，安全系统被削减或关闭，本应为剧毒的甲基异氰酸酯降温的冷冻装置也停了。

12月2日深夜，水进入了储存约42吨甲基异氰酸酯的610号储罐。反应导致温度和压力急剧上升，午夜过后约30至40吨毒气从排气口泄出。沉重的毒云飘过熟睡的街区。人们咳嗽着、失明地醒来，跑到街上，许多人倒地不起。中央邦政府后来公布的死亡人数约为3,800人；其他估计认为最初几周就有近8,000人死亡，此后多年间因后遗症死亡者又有数千乃至上万人。

1989年联合碳化物公司与印度政府达成和解，赔付4.7亿美元，被普遍批评为远远不够。厂址从未得到彻底清理，受污染的地下水至今仍危害附近居民。

name.en: Nepal’s Constituent Assembly ends the monarchy
name.zh: 尼泊尔制宪会议废除君主制

summary.en: After a decade of Maoist insurgency and the 2006 people’s movement, Nepal elected a Constituent Assembly in April 2008, which at its first sitting on 28 May abolished the 240-year Shah monarchy and declared a federal republic.
summary.zh: 经历十年毛派武装斗争和2006年人民运动后，尼泊尔于2008年4月选出制宪会议；该会议在5月28日首次会议上废除延续240年的沙阿王朝君主制，宣布成立联邦共和国。

sources.title: John Whelpton, A History of Nepal (2005)

note: The date is the Constituent Assembly’s first sitting, which abolished the monarchy (28 May 2008); the QID is the Assembly election of 10 April 2008, as no separate Wikidata item exists for the abolition.

name.en: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea and the monsoon trade
name.zh: 《爱利脱利亚海周航记》与季风贸易

summary.en: A Greek-speaking merchant from Roman Egypt wrote a guide to the ports of the Red Sea, East Africa, Arabia and India, explaining how ships used the monsoon winds to cross the open sea. It names Muziris on the Malabar coast, where Roman gold and wine bought pepper and gems.
summary.zh: 一位来自罗马埃及、讲希腊语的商人撰写了这部介绍红海、东非、阿拉伯和印度沿岸港口的指南，说明商船如何借助季风横渡大洋。书中提到马拉巴尔海岸的穆济里斯，罗马的黄金和葡萄酒在此换取胡椒和宝石。

sources.title: Lionel Casson (ed. and trans.), The Periplus Maris Erythraei (1989)
Fordham University Internet History Sourcebooks: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
Wikipedia: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea

note: Usually dated c. 40–70 CE; Muziris is generally identified with the excavated site of Pattanam in Kerala, where the marker is placed.

story.en:
The author never gives his name. He was a Greek-speaking merchant or ship’s officer from Roman Egypt, writing a practical handbook: which ports had good anchorages, what gifts local kings expected, what to sell and what to buy. For India he lists Barygaza (Bharuch) in Gujarat, with its tidal bore that could wreck ships, and the pepper ports of the Chera country.

The key was the monsoon. Sailing from the Red Sea in July, ships could ride the south-west wind straight across the open sea to Malabar and return with the north-east wind in winter. At Muziris Romans paid mainly in gold coin, with some wine, for pepper, pearls, ivory and silk.

Archaeology has borne him out. Roman amphorae and other Mediterranean wares have been dug up at Pattanam in Kerala and Arikamedu near Pondicherry, and a papyrus now in Vienna records a loan for a cargo shipped from Muziris worth, by modern reckoning, almost nine million sesterces.
story.zh:
作者从未留下姓名。他是一位来自罗马埃及、讲希腊语的商人或船员，写的是一本实用手册：哪些港口锚地好，当地国王期待什么礼物，卖什么、买什么。关于印度，他列出了古吉拉特的巴里加扎（布罗奇），那里的涌潮足以毁坏船只，还有哲罗国的胡椒港。

关键在于季风。7月从红海出航，船只可以乘西南季风直接横渡大洋抵达马拉巴尔，冬季再乘东北季风返航。在穆济里斯，罗马人主要用金币、外加少量葡萄酒换取胡椒、珍珠、象牙和丝绸。

考古发现证实了他的记述。喀拉拉的帕塔南和本地治里附近的阿里卡梅杜都出土了罗马双耳陶罐等地中海器物；现藏维也纳的一份纸草文书记载了一笔贷款，所涉从穆济里斯运出的货物按现代估算价值近九百万塞斯特斯。

name.zh: 婆罗摩笈多著《婆罗摩历算书》

summary.en: Working at Bhillamala (Bhinmal) in Rajasthan, Brahmagupta wrote an astronomical treatise containing the first known rules for arithmetic with zero and negative numbers and methods for quadratic and indeterminate equations. Translated into Arabic in Baghdad around 771, it shaped Islamic astronomy and mathematics.
summary.zh: 婆罗摩笈多在拉贾斯坦的毗罗摩罗（今宾马尔）撰写这部天文学著作，其中包含已知最早的零与负数运算规则，以及二次方程和不定方程的解法。约771年该书在巴格达被译成阿拉伯文，影响了伊斯兰天文学和数学。

story.en:
Brahmagupta finished his “Correctly Established Doctrine of Brahma” in 628, at the age of thirty, at Bhillamala in what is now Rajasthan, under a local king of the Chapa dynasty. Most of its 24 chapters are astronomy, but two deal with mathematics.

There, for the first time in any surviving text, zero is treated as a number in its own right with stated rules: a number minus itself is zero; a debt subtracted from zero becomes a fortune; zero multiplied by anything is zero. He also gave rules for “fortunes” and “debts”, our positive and negative numbers, a general solution of quadratic equations, a formula for the area of a cyclic quadrilateral, and methods for equations in whole numbers that European mathematicians reached only in the 17th century. Not every rule was right: he held that zero divided by zero is zero.

In about 771 an Indian astronomer brought the work to the Abbasid court in Baghdad, where it was translated into Arabic as the Sindhind. Through it Indian numerals and methods entered Islamic and, later, European science.
story.zh:
婆罗摩笈多于628年、三十岁时在今拉贾斯坦的毗罗摩罗（宾马尔）完成《婆罗摩历算书》（意为“婆罗摩正确确立的学说”），当时他在恰帕王朝的一位地方国王治下。全书24章大多讲天文，其中两章专论数学。

在这里，零在现存文献中第一次被当作一个独立的数，并有明确的运算规则：一个数减去自身得零；从零中减去债务就成了财富；零乘以任何数都得零。他还给出“财富”与“债务”即正数与负数的运算规则、一般二次方程的解法、圆内接四边形面积公式，以及欧洲数学家直到17世纪才得出的整数方程解法。并非每条规则都正确：他认为零除以零等于零。

约771年，一位印度天文学家把此书带到巴格达的阿拔斯宫廷，被译成阿拉伯文，称《信德罕德》。印度数字和算法由此进入伊斯兰科学，后来又传入欧洲。

name.zh: 埃洛拉凯拉萨神庙开凿

summary.en: Under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I, workers cut a complete Shiva temple, with shrine, halls and courtyard, downward into a single basalt hillside at Ellora. It is the largest monolithic rock-cut monument in the world, part of a site with Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves.
summary.zh: 在罗湿陀罗拘陀王朝国王克里希纳一世治下，工匠在埃洛拉从一整块玄武岩山体向下凿出一座完整的湿婆神庙，包括主殿、厅堂和庭院。这是世界上最大的整石凿成的古迹，所在的石窟群兼有佛教、印度教和耆那教洞窟。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ellora Caves

note: Span is the reign of Krishna I (c. 756–773), to whom the Baroda copper plates of 812 attribute the temple; work may have continued under his successors.

story.en:
Most temples are built up from the ground. The Kailasa at Ellora was carved down from the top. Workers first cut three deep trenches into the basalt hillside to free a block about 50 metres long and 30 metres high, then hollowed and sculpted it from the summit downward into a shrine, an entrance gateway, a hall for Shiva’s bull Nandi, life-size elephants and two free-standing victory pillars. Estimates of the rock removed run to some 200,000 tonnes.

The temple represents Mount Kailasa, Shiva’s Himalayan home. Its most dramatic panel shows the demon king Ravana shaking the mountain while Shiva calmly presses it down with his toe.

A copper-plate grant of 812 credits the temple to the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I and says that the gods in their aerial cars, seeing it, wondered whether it could have been made by human hands. It sits among 34 caves at Ellora, Buddhist, Hindu and Jain, made over five centuries, a World Heritage site since 1983.
story.zh:
大多数神庙是从地面向上建造的，埃洛拉的凯拉萨神庙却是从顶部向下雕凿而成。工匠先在玄武岩山坡上凿出三道深沟，分离出一块长约50米、高约30米的岩体，再从顶部向下掏空、雕刻，形成主殿、门楼、供奉湿婆坐骑南迪牛的殿堂、真象大小的石象和两根独立的胜利柱。据估计，被凿去的岩石约有20万吨。

神庙象征湿婆在喜马拉雅的居所凯拉萨山。最震撼的一幅浮雕刻画魔王罗波那摇撼神山，而湿婆只用脚趾轻轻一按便将其镇住。

812年的一份铜板赐地文书把神庙归功于罗湿陀罗拘陀国王克里希纳一世，并说乘飞车经过的众神见到它，都惊疑这是否出自人手。它坐落在埃洛拉的34座石窟之中，这些佛教、印度教和耆那教石窟历时五个世纪开凿而成，1983年列入世界遗产。

name.zh: 亚洲学会在加尔各答成立

summary.en: The judge and philologist William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta to study Asia's languages, history and sciences. His 1786 address to the Society, noting that Sanskrit, Greek and Latin shared a common source, helped found comparative linguistics and the idea of an Indo-European family.
summary.zh: 法官兼语文学家威廉·琼斯在加尔各答创立亚洲学会，研究亚洲的语言、历史和科学。他1786年在学会的演讲指出梵语、希腊语和拉丁语同出一源，为比较语言学和印欧语系概念奠定了基础。

summary.en: Wartime inflation, the loss of rice imports from Burma, a cyclone and crop disease, and the failure of the colonial and British governments to respond turned scarcity into famine in Bengal. An estimated 2.1 to 3 million people died of starvation and disease.
summary.zh: 战时通货膨胀、缅甸大米进口断绝、气旋与稻作病害，加之殖民政府和英国政府应对失当，使孟加拉的粮食短缺演变为大饥荒。估计有210万至300万人死于饥饿和疾病。

sources.title: Amartya Sen, Poverty and Famines: An Essay on Entitlement and Deprivation (1981)

note: Death estimates range from about 2.1 million (Dyson and Maharatna) to 3 million.

story.en:
Bengal’s food supply fell short in 1943, though historians still debate by how much. What it certainly had was a war. Japan’s conquest of Burma in 1942 cut off rice imports; fearing invasion, the authorities seized boats and removed or destroyed rice stocks in coastal districts under a “denial policy”; a cyclone in October 1942 and a fungal disease damaged the crop; and army purchases and wartime inflation drove prices beyond the reach of labourers and fishermen.

By mid-1943 hundreds of thousands of starving villagers were walking into Calcutta, where many died on the pavements, often in front of well-stocked food shops. The provincial government denied there was a famine. In London the War Cabinet turned down or cut repeated requests for grain imports, citing shipping shortages; Churchill’s comments on the subject are still quoted in arguments about responsibility.

The new viceroy, Lord Wavell, ordered the army to distribute food in late 1943, but deaths from disease went on into 1944. The economist Amartya Sen, who as a boy saw the famine, later argued that it was caused not by a lack of food but by the collapse of poor people’s ability to buy it.
story.zh:
1943年孟加拉的粮食供应确有短缺，但短缺程度至今仍有争议；可以肯定的是，它遭遇了战争。1942年日本征服缅甸，切断了大米进口；当局担心日军入侵，在沿海各县推行“拒敌政策”，没收船只，运走或销毁大米库存；1942年10月的一场气旋和真菌病害损害了庄稼；军队采购和战时通货膨胀使米价远远超出劳工和渔民的承受能力。

到1943年年中，数十万饥饿的村民涌入加尔各答，许多人倒毙在人行道上，身旁往往就是货源充足的粮店。省政府否认发生了饥荒。在伦敦，战时内阁以船运紧张为由，一再拒绝或削减粮食进口请求；丘吉尔对此事的言论至今仍在关于责任的争论中被引用。

新任总督韦弗尔勋爵在1943年底下令军队分发粮食，但因疾病死亡的人一直持续到1944年。童年时目睹这场饥荒的经济学家阿马蒂亚·森后来指出，饥荒的原因不是缺少粮食，而是穷人购买粮食的能力崩溃了。

summary.en: A severe cyclone drove a storm surge across the low islands and coast of East Pakistan on the night of 12–13 November 1970, killing an estimated 300,000–500,000 people, the deadliest tropical cyclone on record. Anger at the government's slow relief fed the movement that led to Bangladesh's independence.
summary.zh: 1970年11月12日至13日夜，一场强烈气旋引发的风暴潮横扫东巴基斯坦的低洼岛屿和沿海地区，估计造成30万至50万人死亡，是有记录以来最致命的热带气旋。政府救灾迟缓引发的愤怒推动了最终导致孟加拉国独立的运动。

sources.title: World Meteorological Organization: WMO Weather and Climate Extremes Archive

note: WMO lists it as the deadliest tropical cyclone on record (about 300,000 deaths); other estimates reach 500,000. Marker at Bhola Island.

story.en:
The storm formed over the Bay of Bengal in early November 1970 and struck the coast of East Pakistan on the night of 12 November, at high tide. A storm surge of up to ten metres swept over the low islands of the Ganges–Brahmaputra delta, where farmers and fishermen lived only a metre or two above the sea, with few shelters and almost no warning that people could understand.

In the morning whole islands had been scoured clean. The island of Bhola and the Char areas lost a large share of their people; bodies lay in the rice fields and floated in the rivers, and survivors lacked food and drinking water for days. The death toll is usually put at about 300,000 and may have been 500,000.

The Pakistani government, based in the West on the far side of India, was slow and grudging with relief, while foreign governments sent large amounts of aid. Anger at that response helped give the Awami League its landslide in the elections a month later, the road to the war of 1971. In Bangladesh the disaster later led to a network of cyclone shelters and warning volunteers that has greatly reduced deaths in later storms.
story.zh:
这场风暴于1970年11月初在孟加拉湾形成，11月12日夜间恰逢涨潮时登陆东巴基斯坦海岸。高达十米的风暴潮席卷恒河-布拉马普特拉河三角洲的低洼岛屿，那里的农民和渔民居住地仅高出海面一两米，几乎没有避难所，也几乎收不到人们能够理解的预警。

第二天早晨，一座座岛屿被冲刷得一干二净。博拉岛和沙洲地区失去了很大一部分人口；尸体横陈稻田、漂浮河中，幸存者数日缺粮缺水。死亡人数通常估计为约30万，也可能达到50万。

远在印度另一侧西巴基斯坦的中央政府救灾迟缓且吝啬，而外国政府送来了大量援助。民众对此的愤怒帮助人民联盟在一个月后的选举中大胜，从而走向1971年的战争。此后孟加拉国因这场灾难建立了避风所网络和预警志愿者体系，大大减少了后来风暴中的死亡人数。

name.en: Sangam poetry of the Tamil kingdoms
name.zh: 泰米尔诸王国的桑伽姆诗歌

summary.en: Some 2,400 Tamil poems, later gathered into the Eight Anthologies and Ten Idylls, describe love (akam) and war and kingship (puram) in the lands of the Chera, Chola and Pandya kings. They are the earliest known literature of South India.
summary.zh: 约2,400首泰米尔语诗歌，后被编入《八卷诗集》和《十卷长歌》，描写哲罗、朱罗、潘地亚诸王国的爱情（阿含）与战争、王权（布拉姆）。它们是已知最早的南印度文学。

sources.title: A. K. Ramanujan, Poems of Love and War (1985)
Kamil Zvelebil, The Smile of Murugan: On Tamil Literature of South India (1973)

note: The poems are dated very roughly to the 1st–3rd centuries CE (some scholars say 2nd century BCE–3rd century CE); the three Madurai academies are legend.

story.en:
Later Tamil tradition told of three literary academies (sangams) at Madurai lasting nearly ten thousand years, two of them swallowed by the sea. The legend is late, but the poems it gave its name to are real: short, highly conventional verses by more than 470 named poets, including some thirty women such as Avvaiyar.

The poets sorted life into two halves. Akam poems are about love, each set in one of five landscapes (hills for lovers meeting, the seashore for anxious waiting). Puram poems praise kings, mourn heroes and beg patrons for gifts. Poems of both kinds mention wine brought by the Yavanas (westerners, mostly Roman subjects) and the gold their ships carried to the Chera port of Muziris.

The anthologies were almost forgotten until the scholar U. V. Swaminatha Iyer spent decades from the 1880s hunting palm-leaf manuscripts in monastery libraries and printing them. A. K. Ramanujan’s translations later brought them a world readership.
story.zh:
后世泰米尔传统说马杜赖曾有三座文学学院（桑伽姆），延续近万年，其中两座被大海吞没。这一传说出现得很晚，但以它命名的诗歌确实存在：470多位有名可考的诗人留下了短小而高度程式化的诗篇，其中约有三十位女性，如阿维雅尔。

诗人把人生分为两半。“阿含”诗写爱情，每首置于五种景观之一（山地是恋人幽会之所，海岸是焦急等待之地）；“布拉姆”诗颂扬国王、哀悼英雄、向赞助者乞求赏赐。两类诗中都提到“耶槃那”（西方来客，多为罗马治下的商人）带来的酒，以及他们的船只运到哲罗港口穆济里斯的黄金。

这些诗集几乎被人遗忘，直到学者U. V. 斯瓦米纳塔·艾耶尔自19世纪80年代起花数十年在寺院藏书中搜寻棕榈叶抄本并付印。A. K. 拉马努詹的译本后来使它们拥有了世界读者。

name.zh: 鲁陀罗达曼的朱纳格特摩崖铭文

summary.en: Carved on the same boulder as Ashoka’s edicts at Girnar, the inscription records how the Western Satrap Rudradaman I rebuilt the Sudarshana lake dam after a storm, without forced labour or extra taxes. It is the earliest long inscription in ornate Sanskrit prose.
summary.zh: 铭文刻在吉尔纳尔阿育王敕令所在的同一块巨石上，记载西部总督鲁陀罗达曼一世在风暴后重建苏达尔沙纳湖堤坝，既未征发劳役，也未加征赋税。这是现存最早的长篇华丽梵文散文铭文。

sources.title: F. Kielhorn, ‘Junagadh rock inscription of Rudradaman: the year 72’, Epigraphia Indica VIII (1905–06)

note: Dated year 72 of the Shaka era, i.e. 150 CE.

name.en: Bakhshali manuscript and the dot for zero
name.zh: 巴赫沙利手稿与表示零的圆点

summary.en: Seventy birch-bark leaves dug up in a field near Peshawar in 1881 contain a practical arithmetic textbook that writes zero as a dot in a place-value system. Radiocarbon dating in 2017 seemed to place some leaves as early as the 3rd–4th centuries, but a 2024 retest put all the tested leaves in the 8th–11th centuries.
summary.zh: 1881年在白沙瓦附近田地里出土的七十片桦树皮写本，是一部实用算术教材，书中在位值制里用圆点表示零。2017年的放射性碳测年一度显示部分叶片早至3至4世纪，但2024年的复测将所有受测叶片定在8至11世纪。

sources.title: Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford: Carbon dating finds Bakhshali manuscript contains oldest recorded origins of the symbol ‘zero’ (2017)
Kim Plofker, Mathematics in India (2009), ch. 6
Takao Hayashi, The Bakhshālī Manuscript: An Ancient Indian Mathematical Treatise (1995)
Chivall, Lladó-Buisán, Howell & Evison, Radiocarbon dating of the Bakhshālī manuscript (University of Oxford, 2024)

note: The 2017 Oxford radiocarbon tests gave three ranges (224–383, 680–779 and 885–993 CE); in 2024 the laboratory reported that a retest showed the earliest result was inaccurate, and all five leaves tested now fall between about 773 and 1032 CE. Hayashi dated the work to the 7th century on internal grounds. The span shown runs from Hayashi’s date for the text to the end of the revised leaf dates.

story.en:
In 1881 a farmer digging near the village of Bakhshali, outside Peshawar, found a bundle of birch bark leaves. They held problems and worked answers, from dividing profits among merchants to solving equations, written in a mix of Sanskrit and local language. Each number used a dot for an empty place, the ancestor of the circle we now call zero.

The Bodleian Library in Oxford, which has kept the leaves since 1902, announced in 2017 that radiocarbon tests dated some of them to the 3rd or 4th century, centuries older than expected. Critics soon pointed out that the three leaves tested gave widely separated dates. In 2024 the Oxford laboratory reported that a retest had shown the early result to be wrong: five leaves now date to the late 8th to early 11th centuries.

Whatever its date, the manuscript shows zero as a working tool of merchants’ arithmetic. By the time of Brahmagupta (628) Indian mathematicians treated zero as a number with its own rules, and the Arabic translators of Baghdad passed the system to Europe.
story.zh:
1881年，一位农民在白沙瓦城外巴赫沙利村附近挖地时，发现了一捆桦树皮写本。里面写满了习题与解答，从商人分利到解方程，用的是梵语与当地语言的混合体。每个数字都用一个圆点表示空位，这就是今天所说的“零”这个圆圈的祖先。

自1902年起收藏这批写本的牛津博德利图书馆在2017年宣布，放射性碳测年显示其中部分叶片属于3或4世纪，比原先估计早了好几百年。批评者很快指出，受测的三片叶子年代相距甚远。2024年，牛津的实验室报告称复测表明早期结果有误：五片叶子的年代均在8世纪末至11世纪初之间。

无论其确切年代如何，这部手稿表明零已是商业算术中的实用工具。到婆罗摩笈多时代（628年），印度数学家已把零当作有自身运算规则的数，巴格达的阿拉伯译者又把这一体系传到了欧洲。

name.en: Samudragupta’s eulogy on the Allahabad pillar
name.zh: 阿拉哈巴德石柱上的沙摩陀罗笈多颂词

summary.en: The court poet Harishena carved a long Sanskrit praise of Samudragupta onto an Ashokan pillar, listing kings he uprooted in the north, rulers of the south he defeated and released, and frontier peoples who paid him homage. It is the main source for the making of the Gupta Empire.
summary.zh: 宫廷诗人诃利仙那在一根阿育王石柱上刻下赞美沙摩陀罗笈多的长篇梵文颂词，列举了他在北方铲除的诸王、在南方击败后又释放的君主，以及向他称臣的边疆诸族。这是研究笈多帝国形成的主要史料。

sources.title: J. F. Fleet, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum III: Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings (1888), no. 1
Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008), ch. 9

note: The QID is the pillar itself, an Ashokan monument of the 3rd century BCE; the inscription is undated and placed c. 350–375.

story.en:
The pillar already carried Ashoka’s edicts when, some six centuries later, Samudragupta’s minister and poet Harishena added his master’s praise below them. Later still the Mughal emperor Jahangir had his own genealogy cut into the same stone, so one column holds three empires.

Harishena’s verses sort the conquered into types. Eight named kings of Aryavarta, the Ganges heartland, were “violently uprooted” and their lands annexed.
