Twelve kings of the south, from Kosala to Kanchi, were captured and then freed, a sign that Samudragupta wanted tribute, not distant provinces. Forest chiefs became servants; frontier kingdoms such as Nepala and Samatata paid taxes, and distant rulers, including the “Daivaputra Shahi Shahanushahi” (the Kushans) and the people of Simhala (Sri Lanka), are said to have sent gifts and maidens.

A poet’s boast must be read with care, but coins confirm the picture: Samudragupta minted gold showing himself performing the horse sacrifice of a universal king.
story.zh:
早在约六个世纪前，这根石柱上就已刻有阿育王敕令。后来沙摩陀罗笈多的大臣兼诗人诃利仙那在其下方加刻了对君主的颂词。再后来，莫卧儿皇帝贾汉吉尔又把自己的世系刻在同一块石头上，于是一根石柱承载了三个帝国。

诃利仙那的诗句把被征服者分门别类：雅利安伐尔多（恒河腹地）有名可考的八位国王被“连根拔除”，领土被吞并；从憍萨罗到建志的十二位南方国王被俘后又获释放，说明沙摩陀罗笈多要的是贡赋而非遥远的行省；森林部落酋长沦为仆从；尼泊罗、三摩呾吒等边疆王国缴纳赋税；远方君主，包括“天子沙希王中之王”（贵霜）和僧伽罗（斯里兰卡）人，据说也献上礼物和少女。

诗人的夸耀须谨慎看待，但钱币印证了大致情形：沙摩陀罗笈多铸造的金币上，正是他举行象征天下共主的马祭的形象。

name.en: Faxian’s pilgrimage in India and Sri Lanka
name.zh: 法显在印度和斯里兰卡的求法之旅

summary.en: The Chinese monk Faxian crossed the Pamirs in search of complete Vinaya texts, spent years copying them in the Gupta heartland and in Sri Lanka, and sailed home via Java. His Record of Buddhist Kingdoms praises the peace and charity he saw under Chandragupta II.
summary.zh: 中国僧人法显为求完整的律藏翻越葱岭，在笈多王朝腹地和斯里兰卡抄经多年，后经爪哇乘船归国。他的《佛国记》称赞了旃陀罗笈多二世治下的安定与慈善。

label.en: Tamralipti: two more years, then by sea
label.zh: 多摩梨帝：再留两年后乘船
阿努拉德普勒：无畏山寺

sources.title: Faxian, A Record of Buddhistic Kingdoms, tr. James Legge (1886)
Max Deeg, Das Gaoseng-Faxian-Zhuan als religionsgeschichtliche Quelle (2005)

note: The QID is the travel record, finished c. 414–416; years of the stops are approximate.

name.zh: 塞建陀笈多击退匈人（比塔里石柱）

summary.en: Skandagupta’s pillar at Bhitari says that the Gupta prince restored his family’s fallen fortunes, sleeping on the bare ground, and fought the Hunas so fiercely that the earth shook. The victory held off the Alchon Huns for a generation.
summary.zh: 塞建陀笈多在比塔里所立石柱的铭文称，这位笈多王子露宿于地，重振衰落的家业，与匈人激战，大地为之震动。这场胜利使阿尔孔匈人的入侵推迟了一代人。

sources.title: J. F. Fleet, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum III (1888), no. 13: Bhitari pillar inscription
Hans T. Bakker, The Alkhan: A Hunnic People in South Asia (2020)

note: The inscription is undated; the Huna war is placed c. 455–460 at the start of Skandagupta’s reign.

name.zh: 昌古·纳拉扬神庙的摩那提婆石柱

summary.en: A pillar at the hilltop Vishnu temple of Changu Narayan bears the first dated record of the Licchavi king Manadeva I, long held to be the oldest inscription in Nepal. It tells how he talked his widowed mother out of following her husband in death and, at her urging, marched east and west to subdue rebellious vassals.
summary.zh: 昌古·纳拉扬山顶毗湿奴神庙前的石柱上刻有李查维国王摩那提婆一世最早的纪年铭文，长期被视为尼泊尔最古老的铭文。铭文记载他劝阻寡母殉夫，并应母亲之请东征西讨，平定叛乱的诸侯。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Kathmandu Valley
Theodore Riccardi Jr., ‘The inscription of King Mānadeva at Changu Narayan’, Journal of the American Oriental Society 109 (1989)

note: Samvat 386, read as 464 CE. Older dated inscriptions found in the valley since (e.g. the Jayavarma statue, 185 CE) have displaced its claim to be the earliest. Wikidata’s start date (325) is a traditional founding date of the temple.

summary.en: Monks of the Mahavihara at Anuradhapura composed the Mahavamsa, a Pali verse chronicle of Sri Lanka from the legendary arrival of Prince Vijaya to the 4th century. Continued as the Culavamsa down to 1815, it is one of the longest unbroken historical traditions in Asia.
summary.zh: 阿努拉德普勒大寺的僧人用巴利语诗体编成《大史》，记述斯里兰卡从传说中维阇耶王子登岛到4世纪的历史。其续编《小史》一直写到1815年，是亚洲延续最久的史学传统之一。

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World: Mahavamsa (2023)

note: Traditionally ascribed to a monk named Mahanama; dated to the late 5th or early 6th century.

summary.en: King Yashodharman of Malwa defeated the Alchon Hun ruler Mihirakula, whom Buddhist sources remember as a persecutor. Victory pillars at Sondani near Mandsaur boast that Mihirakula bowed at Yashodharman’s feet, and Hun rule in the Indian plains collapsed.
summary.zh: 马尔瓦国王耶输陀摩击败阿尔孔匈人君主米希拉古拉（佛教文献记其为迫害者）。曼达索尔附近松达尼的胜利石柱夸耀米希拉古拉曾拜倒在耶输陀摩脚下，匈人在印度平原的统治随之瓦解。

sources.title: J. F. Fleet, Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum III (1888), nos. 33–35: Mandasor inscriptions
Hans T. Bakker, The Alkhan: A Hunnic People in South Asia (2020)

note: The victory pillars are undated; 528 is the conventional date. Xuanzang credits the defeat of Mihirakula to a Gupta king, Baladitya.

summary.en: The early Chalukyas cut four cave temples into the red sandstone cliff above their capital Vatapi, three Hindu and one Jain. Cave 3, dedicated to Vishnu, carries an inscription of 578 by Mangalesha and huge reliefs of Vishnu as the dwarf who strides across the cosmos.
summary.zh: 早期遮娄其王朝在都城伐陀比上方的红砂岩崖壁上开凿了四座石窟神庙，三座属印度教，一座属耆那教。供奉毗湿奴的第三窟有曼加勒沙578年的铭文，以及毗湿奴化身侏儒跨越宇宙的巨型浮雕。

sources.title: George Michell, Temple Architecture and Art of the Early Chalukyas (2014)
Archaeological Survey of India: Cave temples, Badami

name.zh: 补罗稽舍二世的艾霍莱铭文

summary.en: The poet Ravikirti composed a Sanskrit eulogy of Pulakeshin II for the Meguti Jain temple at Aihole, recounting his defeat of Harsha and his wars with the Pallavas. Dated by both the Kali Yuga and Shaka eras, it fixes the chronology of 7th-century India.
summary.zh: 诗人拉维基尔提为艾霍莱的梅古提耆那教神庙撰写赞美补罗稽舍二世的梵文颂词，叙述他击败戒日王和与帕拉瓦作战的经过。铭文同时用迦利时代纪年和塞种纪年，确定了7世纪印度的年代学。

sources.title: F. Kielhorn, ‘Aihole inscription of Pulikesin II, Saka-Samvat 556’, Epigraphia Indica VI (1900)

name.zh: 默哈伯利布勒姆的帕拉瓦古迹

summary.en: At their port of Mamallapuram the Pallava kings carved granite outcrops into cave shrines, monolithic temples (the five rathas), the vast relief known as the Descent of the Ganges or Arjuna’s Penance, and finally the structural Shore Temple, the seed of Dravidian temple architecture.
summary.zh: 帕拉瓦国王在港口玛玛拉普兰把花岗岩露头雕成石窟神殿、整石神庙（五车神庙）、被称为“恒河降凡”或“阿周那苦行”的巨型浮雕，最后建起砌筑的海岸神庙，开创了达罗毗荼式神庙建筑。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
Michael Lockwood et al., Mamallapuram and the Pallavas (1982)
Padma Kaimal, ‘Early Cōḷa kings and “early Cōḷa temples”’, Artibus Asiae 56 (1996)

note: Most works are attributed to Narasimhavarman I “Mamalla” (r. 630–668) and Rajasimha (r. c. 690–728); attributions of individual monuments are debated.

story.en:
The town takes its name from Narasimhavarman I, called Mamalla, “the great wrestler”, the Pallava king who sacked the Chalukya capital in 642. From his reign and his successors’ come monuments that look like an open-air workshop of Indian architecture: five free-standing “chariots” (rathas) cut from single boulders, each imitating a different kind of wooden or thatched building, and cave halls framed by lion pillars.

The great relief, on a rock face nearly 30 metres long, shows gods, sages, hunters, elephants and a cat mocking an ascetic by standing on one leg. A natural cleft down the middle was once fed with water, so a real stream ran past carved serpent deities: the river Ganges descending to earth.

Early in the 8th century the king Rajasimha built the Shore Temple of dressed stone on the beach. European sailors called the site the Seven Pagodas. In 2004 the Indian Ocean tsunami exposed the remains of older structures on the shore and offshore.
story.zh:
城名源于帕拉瓦国王那罗辛哈跋摩一世的称号“玛玛拉”（大力士），正是他在642年攻陷了遮娄其都城。他及其后继者留下的古迹宛如一座露天的印度建筑工坊：五座用整块巨石雕成的独立“车殿”（拉塔），各自模仿一种木构或茅草建筑，还有以狮柱为框的石窟殿堂。

一面近30米长的岩壁上的巨型浮雕刻有神祇、圣人、猎人、大象，还有一只单腿站立、嘲弄苦行者的猫。浮雕中央有一道天然裂缝，过去曾引水注入，让真实的水流从雕刻的蛇神身旁流过，象征恒河降临人间。

8世纪初，国王罗阇辛哈在海滩上用琢石建起海岸神庙。欧洲水手称此地为“七塔”。2004年印度洋海啸冲刷海岸，使岸边和近海处更古老建筑的遗迹显露出来。

summary.en: The Pallava king Narasimhavarman I, with help from the Sri Lankan prince Manavamma, invaded the Chalukya kingdom, killed Pulakeshin II and occupied his capital Vatapi (Badami), taking the title Vatapikonda, “conqueror of Vatapi”. The Chalukyas recovered within about thirteen years.
summary.zh: 帕拉瓦国王那罗辛哈跋摩一世在斯里兰卡王子摩那跋摩的协助下进攻遮娄其王国，杀死补罗稽舍二世，占领其都城伐陀比（巴达米），并取称号“伐陀比征服者”。遮娄其约十三年后恢复。

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India (1955)

name.zh: 争夺曲女城的三方之争

summary.en: For more than a century the Gurjara-Pratiharas of the west, the Palas of Bengal and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan fought for Kannauj, the old imperial city of Harsha. Each won it in turn; the Pratiharas held it longest, but the war exhausted all three.
summary.zh: 一个多世纪里，西部的瞿折罗-普罗蒂哈拉、孟加拉的波罗和德干的罗湿陀罗拘陀为争夺戒日王的旧都曲女城反复交战。三方轮流得手，普罗蒂哈拉控制最久，但战争耗尽了三方的国力。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: India: the tripartite struggle
Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India (2008), ch. 10

note: Start and end dates are conventional: from Vatsaraja and Dharmapala’s clash in the 780s to Indra III’s Rashtrakuta raid on Kannauj in 916.

summary.en: The Pala king Dharmapala founded the monastic university of Vikramashila on the Ganges in Bihar. It became the leading centre of tantric Buddhism; its abbot Atisha left in about 1040 to teach in Tibet. Troops of Bakhtiyar Khalji destroyed it around 1203.
summary.zh: 波罗国王达摩波罗在比哈尔恒河畔创建超戒寺僧院大学。它成为密教的首要中心，其住持阿底峡约在1040年离寺前往西藏弘法。约1203年，该寺被巴赫蒂亚尔·卡尔吉的军队摧毁。

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India: Excavated remains of Vikramashila, Antichak
Taranatha, History of Buddhism in India (1608), tr. Lama Chimpa & A. Chattopadhyaya (1970)

note: Dharmapala reigned c. 770–810; the foundation is dated c. 800.

summary.en: The Rashtrakuta emperor Krishna III defeated the Chola army near Arakkonam; the Chola crown prince Rajaditya was killed by an arrow while fighting on his elephant. The Rashtrakutas held Tondaimandalam for about two decades, until the Cholas recovered under Parantaka II (Sundara Chola).
summary.zh: 罗湿陀罗拘陀皇帝克里希纳三世在阿拉科南附近击败朱罗军队，朱罗王储罗阇迪提耶在象背上作战时中箭身亡。此后罗湿陀罗拘陀控制通代曼达拉姆约二十年，直到朱罗在帕兰塔卡二世（孙陀罗·朱罗）时收复失地。

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Cōḷas (1955), ch. 7

name.zh: 克久拉霍的金德拉神庙群

summary.en: The Chandela kings raised some 85 Hindu and Jain temples at Khajuraho, of which about 25 survive. Their soaring spires imitate a mountain range, and their walls carry thousands of carved figures, a small share of them famously erotic.
summary.zh: 金德拉国王在克久拉霍兴建约85座印度教和耆那教神庙，现存约25座。其高耸的塔顶模仿连绵群山，墙面上雕满成千上万的人物形象，其中一小部分以情爱题材闻名。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Khajuraho Group of Monuments

note: The Lakshmana temple is dated by inscription to 954; the Kandariya Mahadeva to c. 1030.

story.en:
Khajuraho was a ritual capital of the Chandelas, a Rajput dynasty of Bundelkhand. Between about 950 and 1050 its kings and merchants built temples to Shiva, Vishnu and the Jain saints around a lake. The Lakshmana temple’s inscription of 954 records that King Yashovarman installed a Vishnu image obtained from his Pratihara overlord, a sign of the Chandelas’ rise.

The largest, the Kandariya Mahadeva, piles 84 miniature spires into one peak like the Himalaya around Mount Kailasa. Its walls show gods, dancers, warriors and couples; the erotic scenes, which have made the site famous, make up less than a tenth of the sculpture and are usually explained as auspicious or tantric imagery.

Ibn Battuta passed by in the 1330s and saw yogis living there. The temples, far from major routes, then faded from view until a British army engineer, T. S. Burt, was guided to them in 1838.
story.zh:
克久拉霍是本德尔坎德地区拉杰普特王朝金德拉的礼仪都城。约950至1050年间，国王和商人们环湖修建了供奉湿婆、毗湿奴和耆那祖师的神庙。拉克什曼神庙954年的铭文记载，国王耶输跋摩安奉了一尊从其宗主普拉蒂哈拉国王那里得来的毗湿奴像，这是金德拉崛起的标志。

最大的坎达利亚·摩诃提婆神庙把84座小塔堆叠成一座主峰，宛如环绕冈仁波齐的喜马拉雅群山。墙面上刻有神祇、舞者、武士和情侣；令此地闻名的情爱场景不到雕刻总数的十分之一，通常被解释为吉祥或密教意象。

14世纪30年代伊本·白图泰路经此地，见到有瑜伽士在此居住。由于远离主要交通线，这些神庙后来渐被遗忘，直到1838年英国陆军工程师T. S. 伯特被向导带到这里。

name.zh: 什拉瓦纳贝拉戈拉的戈玛泰什瓦拉巨像

summary.en: Chavundaraya, minister of the Western Ganga kings, had a 17-metre statue of the Jain saint Bahubali carved from the granite summit of Vindhyagiri hill. One of the largest monolithic statues in the world, it is anointed every twelve years in the Mahamastakabhisheka festival.
summary.zh: 西恒伽王朝大臣查文达拉亚命人在温迪亚吉里山顶的花岗岩上雕出一尊高17米的耆那教圣者巴胡巴利像。它是世界上最大的整石雕像之一，每十二年举行一次“大灌顶节”为其灌浴。

note: Dated c. 981–983 from inscriptions and literary references.

summary.en: Rajaraja I’s armies took northern Sri Lanka in 993 and sacked Anuradhapura, making Polonnaruwa a Chola provincial capital. In 1017 Rajendra I completed the conquest and carried King Mahinda V and the royal regalia to India; Sinhalese rule returned only with Vijayabahu I in 1070.
summary.zh: 993年罗阇罗阇一世的军队攻取斯里兰卡北部，洗劫阿努拉德普勒，以波隆纳鲁沃为朱罗行省首府。1017年罗金陀罗一世完成征服，把国王摩哂陀五世和王权象征物掳到印度；直到1070年维阇耶巴忽一世时僧伽罗人才恢复统治。

sources.title: K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Cōḷas (1955)

story.en:
The Culavamsa, written by monks who hated the invaders, says the Cholas “broke open all the relic chambers” and “took away all the precious things” like blood-sucking demons. Chola inscriptions tell the same story from the other side: Rajaraja’s men crossed the sea and burned Ilam (Lanka).

The conquest made the island a Chola province, Mummudi-chola-mandalam. The rulers moved the capital to Polonnaruwa, nearer the eastern ports, built Shiva temples there and collected taxes in rice. Mahinda V held out in the southern hill region of Ruhuna until 1017, when he was captured and shipped to the Chola country, where he died twelve years later.

Resistance continued from Ruhuna, and in 1070 Vijayabahu I took Polonnaruwa. He kept it as his capital, and Anuradhapura, royal seat for some 1,400 years, never recovered.
story.zh:
由痛恨入侵者的僧人编写的《小史》说，朱罗人像吸血的恶魔一样“打开了所有舍利室”，“掠走了一切珍宝”。朱罗铭文则从另一方讲述了同一事件：罗阇罗阇的军队渡海焚烧了伊兰（楞伽）。

这次征服使该岛成为朱罗的一个行省“蒙穆迪朱罗曼达拉姆”。统治者把首府迁到更靠近东部港口的波隆纳鲁沃，在那里修建湿婆神庙，以稻米征税。摩哂陀五世在南部山地罗哈那坚持抵抗，直到1017年被俘并被押往朱罗本土，十二年后死在那里。

罗哈那的抵抗从未停止。1070年维阇耶巴忽一世攻取波隆纳鲁沃并以之为都，作为王都约1,400年的阿努拉德普勒从此再未复兴。

name.en: Rajendra’s Ganges expedition and Gangaikonda Cholapuram
name.zh: 罗金陀罗的恒河远征与恒河征服者朱罗城

summary.en: Rajendra I sent an army north through Kalinga to the Ganges, where it defeated the Pala king Mahipala, and celebrated by founding a new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, “the city of the Chola who took the Ganges”, with a great Shiva temple and a reservoir filled, it was said, with Ganges water.
summary.zh: 罗金陀罗一世派军北上，经羯陵伽直抵恒河，击败波罗国王摩希波罗。为庆祝胜利，他新建都城“恒河征服者朱罗城”，并修建宏伟的湿婆神庙和一座据说注入了恒河水的水库。

label.en: Vangala and Dandabhukti: defeats Mahipala of the Palas
label.zh: 万加拉与丹达布克提：击败波罗王摩希波罗

label.en: Rajendra meets the returning army on the Godavari
label.zh: 罗金陀罗在戈达瓦里河迎接凯旋之师
新都恒河征服者朱罗城

sources.title: Tiruvalangadu copper plates of Rajendra I, South Indian Inscriptions III
K. A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Cōḷas (1955), ch. 9
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Great Living Chola Temples

note: The expedition is dated c. 1021–1023: it first appears in Rajendra’s inscriptions of 1023. The QID is the temple, whose first recorded endowment dates from 1035. Route stops are approximate.

story.en:
Rajaraja I had made the Cholas masters of the south. His son Rajendra wanted a deed to outdo him, and the Ganges, the holiest river of the north, was the trophy. His inscriptions say an army under a trusted general marched up the east coast, through Vengi and Kalinga, defeated a string of kings including the Pala ruler Mahipala, and reached the river.

Rajendra himself waited on the Godavari to meet the returning troops. According to the Tiruvalangadu plates, the defeated kings were made to carry Ganges water in pots on their heads back to the Chola country.

The water filled a vast tank, the Chola-gangam, at a new capital that took the name of the victory, Gangaikonda Cholapuram. Its temple, with a tower slightly smaller but more graceful than his father’s at Thanjavur, is now part of the Great Living Chola Temples World Heritage site. The city itself has almost vanished, but the name still announces the boast.
story.zh:
罗阇罗阇一世已使朱罗成为南方霸主。其子罗金陀罗想要建立超越父亲的功业，而北方最神圣的恒河便是最好的战利品。他的铭文记载，一支由亲信大将率领的军队沿东海岸北上，穿过文吉和羯陵伽，击败包括波罗国王摩希波罗在内的一连串君主，抵达恒河。

罗金陀罗本人则在戈达瓦里河畔等候凯旋的军队。据蒂鲁瓦兰加杜铜板铭文，战败的国王们被迫头顶水罐，把恒河水运回朱罗国土。

这些水注满了新都的一座巨型水库“朱罗恒河”，新都也以这场胜利命名为“恒河征服者朱罗城”。城中神庙的塔比其父在坦贾武尔所建的略小，却更为秀美，今为“伟大的朱罗王朝现存神庙”世界遗产的一部分。城市本身几乎消失殆尽，但这个名字至今仍在宣示当年的豪言。

name.zh: 贝鲁尔的契纳克沙瓦神庙

summary.en: The Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana built a temple to Vishnu at his capital Belur, traditionally to mark a victory over the Cholas at Talakad. Carved in soft soapstone on a star-shaped plan, it is famous for its bracket figures of dancers (madanikas).
summary.zh: 曷萨拉国王毗湿奴伐弹那在都城贝鲁尔修建毗湿奴神庙，传说是为纪念在塔拉卡德击败朱罗。神庙以软质皂石雕成，平面呈星形，以斜撑上的舞女雕像（马达尼卡）闻名。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas
Adam Hardy, Indian Temple Architecture: Form and Transformation (1995)

summary.en: The Kashmiri poet Kalhana wrote the Rajatarangini (“River of Kings”), nearly 8,000 Sanskrit verses tracing the kings of Kashmir. Using inscriptions, land grants and earlier chronicles, he produced what is often called the first critical history written in India.
summary.zh: 克什米尔诗人迦尔诃纳写成《王河》，以近8,000颂梵文诗句追述克什米尔历代国王。他利用碑铭、赐地文书和更早的编年史，写出了常被称为印度第一部具有考证精神的史书。

sources.title: Kalhaṇa’s Rājataraṅgiṇī, tr. M. A. Stein (1900)

summary.en: Parakramabahu I joined older tanks at Polonnaruwa into a reservoir of some 2,500 hectares behind a bund about 12.5 km long, the “Sea of Parakrama”. It fed rice fields that made his kingdom the granary of the island and still irrigates the district.
summary.zh: 波罗迦罗摩巴忽一世把波隆纳鲁沃的几座旧水库连成一座面积约2,500公顷、堤长约12.5公里的大水库，即“波罗迦罗摩海”。它灌溉的稻田使其王国成为全岛粮仓，至今仍在灌溉当地农田。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Ancient City of Polonnaruwa

note: The reservoir enlarged earlier tanks and its building date within the reign is not recorded.

story.en:
Sri Lanka’s dry zone gets most of its rain in a few months, and for over a thousand years its kings had built tanks to store it. Parakramabahu I took this to a new scale. The Culavamsa puts into his mouth a famous resolve: in a land like this, not even a little water that comes from the rain must flow into the ocean without being made useful to man.

At Polonnaruwa his engineers linked three older tanks into one sheet of water held by a long earthen bund, with stone sluices and channels distributing it to paddy fields. The chronicle credits him with restoring or building more than 160 tanks and thousands of channels.

The surplus paid for monasteries, a council that reunited the quarrelling Buddhist orders, and expeditions to south India and Burma. After his reign the kingdom weakened, the jungle reclaimed many works, and the capital moved south-west. But the Parakrama Samudra, restored in the 20th century, still waters the rice fields around the ruined city.
story.zh:
斯里兰卡干旱地带的雨水集中在少数几个月，一千多年来历代国王都修建水库蓄水。波罗迦罗摩巴忽一世把这一传统推向前所未有的规模。《小史》借他之口说出一句名言：在这样的土地上，即使是一点雨水，也不能未经造福于人就流入大海。

他的工匠在波隆纳鲁沃把三座旧水库连成一片水面，以一道长长的土堤拦蓄，再用石砌水闸和渠道把水分配到稻田。编年史说他修复或新建了160多座水库和数千条水渠。

剩余的粮食供养了寺院，资助了一次使分裂的佛教僧团重新统一的会议，以及远征南印度和缅甸的军事行动。他死后王国衰落，许多工程被丛林吞没，都城也向西南迁移。但20世纪修复的波罗迦罗摩海，至今仍灌溉着这座废墟之城周围的稻田。

name.en: Bakhtiyar Khalji’s raids on Bihar and Bengal
name.zh: 巴赫蒂亚尔·卡尔吉对比哈尔与孟加拉的袭掠

summary.en: A Ghurid commander, Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji, raided Bihar, sacking the great Buddhist monasteries, and surprised the Sena king Lakshmana Sena at Nadia. The great monastic centres of Buddhism’s homeland never recovered, and the campaigns founded Muslim rule in Bengal.
summary.zh: 古尔王朝将领穆罕默德·本·巴赫蒂亚尔·卡尔吉袭掠比哈尔，洗劫了几座佛教大寺院，又在纳迪亚突袭塞纳国王罗刹摩那·塞纳。佛教故乡的大寺院从此一蹶不振，这些征战也开启了穆斯林对孟加拉的统治。

sources.title: Minhaj-i Siraj Juzjani, Tabaqat-i Nasiri, tr. H. G. Raverty (1881), vol. I, pp. 551–560
Richard M. Eaton, The Rise of Islam and the Bengal Frontier, 1204–1760 (1993), ch. 1

note: Minhaj describes the sack of a fortified monastery at “Bihar”, usually identified with Odantapuri (Bihar Sharif); the destruction of Nalanda is inferred from Tibetan accounts (Dharmasvamin, 1234–36) and archaeology. Dates are approximate. No Wikidata item covers these raids (checked 2026-11); Q2698200 is Bakhtiyar himself and Q27628354 only his 1206 Tibet campaign.

story.en:
Minhaj-i Siraj, who visited Bengal about forty years later and finished his chronicle in 1260, heard the story from one of Bakhtiyar’s veterans. With about two hundred horsemen the commander stormed a walled place in Bihar, killed its shaven-headed inhabitants and found it full of books; only afterwards did his men learn that it was a college, a vihara, which gave the province of Bihar its name.

That monastery was probably Odantapuri; Nalanda and Vikramashila were probably also struck in these years. When the Tibetan pilgrim Dharmasvamin visited Nalanda in 1235 he found two monasteries still in use and a ninety-year-old teacher with about seventy students, hiding from raiding soldiers. Without royal patrons the great libraries and colleges were never rebuilt.

In about 1204 Bakhtiyar rode into the Sena king’s residence at Nadia with a vanguard so small that it was taken for horse traders; the old king fled by a back door. Bengal became a Muslim-ruled province and later a great sultanate. Bakhtiyar himself died after a disastrous campaign towards Tibet.
story.zh:
约四十年后到访孟加拉、1260年完成史书的明哈吉·西拉吉从巴赫蒂亚尔的一名老兵那里听到这个故事：这位将领率约两百骑兵攻入比哈尔的一处有城墙的地方，杀死了那里剃发的居民，发现里面满是书籍；事后他的士兵才知道这是一所学院，即“毗诃罗”（寺院），比哈尔省也由此得名。

那座寺院很可能是飞行寺（奥丹塔普里）；那烂陀和超戒寺很可能也在这些年间遭到打击。1235年西藏求法僧达摩斯瓦明到访那烂陀时，只见两座寺院仍在使用，一位九十岁的老师带着约七十名学生躲避来犯的士兵。失去王室赞助，这些宏大的图书馆和学院再未重建。

约1204年，巴赫蒂亚尔率领一支小得被误认为马贩子的先锋部队闯入塞纳国王驻跸的纳迪亚，老国王从后门出逃。孟加拉由此成为穆斯林统治的行省，后来又成为强大的苏丹国。巴赫蒂亚尔本人则在一次进军西藏的惨败后死去。

name.zh: 拉玛帕（鲁德雷什瓦拉）神庙

summary.en: Built by Recharla Rudra, a general of the Kakatiya king Ganapatideva, the Shiva temple at Palampet is named after its sculptor Ramappa. Its bracket figures of dancers in black basalt and its light “floating” bricks made it a World Heritage site in 2021.
summary.zh: 由卡卡提亚国王迦那帕蒂提婆的将领雷查尔拉·鲁陀罗修建，位于帕兰佩特的这座湿婆神庙以雕刻师拉玛帕命名。其黑色玄武岩舞女斜撑雕像和轻盈的“浮砖”使它于2021年列入世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple, Telangana
Cynthia Talbot, Precolonial India in Practice (2001)

summary.en: King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty built a temple to the sun god Surya on the Odisha coast in the form of a colossal chariot, with 24 carved stone wheels and seven horses. Its great tower collapsed long ago; the surviving hall is a World Heritage site.
summary.zh: 东恒伽王朝国王那罗辛哈提婆一世在奥里萨海岸修建太阳神苏利耶的神庙，其形如巨大的战车，有24个石雕车轮和七匹骏马。主塔早已坍塌，现存的前殿为世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sun Temple, Konârak
Thomas E. Donaldson, Hindu Temple Art of Orissa, vol. 2 (1986)

note: Narasimhadeva I reigned 1238–1264; the temple is usually dated c. 1250. Wikidata’s 1201 is not supported by the main sources.

story.en:
Narasimhadeva I was a warrior king who carried the war against the Muslim governors of Bengal into their own territory. His temple to the sun, on the shore where sailors could see it, was designed as Surya’s chariot: twelve pairs of wheels, each about three metres across and carved with spokes that work as sundials, drawn by seven stone horses.

The main tower, perhaps 60 to 70 metres high, stood behind a hall for worshippers. Sailors called the dark mass the Black Pagoda and used it as a landmark. The tower had fallen by the mid-19th century; why is still argued over, with explanations ranging from weak foundations on sandy soil to lightning and deliberate damage.

In 1903 the British filled the surviving hall with sand and sealed it to stop it collapsing. The poet Rabindranath Tagore wrote that here the language of stone surpasses the language of man.
story.zh:
那罗辛哈提婆一世是一位尚武的国王，曾把对孟加拉穆斯林总督的战争打进对方境内。他在海岸边修建的这座太阳神庙远远就能被水手望见，设计成太阳神苏利耶的战车：十二对车轮，每个直径约三米，车辐雕刻精细，可作日晷使用，由七匹石马牵引。

高约60至70米的主塔立在信众礼拜的前殿之后。水手把这团黑色建筑称为“黑塔”，用作航标。到19世纪中叶主塔已经坍塌，原因至今仍有争议，从沙质地基不稳到雷击和人为破坏，说法不一。

1903年英国人用沙子填满现存的前殿并加以封闭，以防坍塌。诗人泰戈尔写道，在这里，石头的语言胜过了人类的语言。

name.en: Muhammad bin Tughluq moves the capital to Daulatabad
name.zh: 穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克迁都道拉塔巴德

summary.en: To rule his new Deccan conquests, Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq renamed the Yadava fortress of Devagiri “Daulatabad” and ordered the elite of Delhi, and by some accounts much of its population, to move 1,100 km south. The scheme was abandoned within a decade, but it spread Muslim settlers and Persian culture into the Deccan.
summary.zh: 为统治新征服的德干，苏丹穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克把亚达瓦王朝的要塞德瓦吉里改名为“道拉塔巴德”，下令德里的精英、据某些记载还包括大批居民南迁1,100公里。该计划不到十年即告放弃，却把穆斯林移民和波斯文化带入了德干。

sources.title: Ibn Battuta, Rihla, tr. H. A. R. Gibb, vol. III (1971)
Peter Jackson, The Delhi Sultanate (1999), ch. 13
Richard M. Eaton, A Social History of the Deccan, 1300–1761 (2005), ch. 1

note: The QID is the fortress itself (built from the 12th century). How many people were forced to move is disputed.

story.en:
Delhi chroniclers who disliked the sultan, above all Ziauddin Barani, described the move as a catastrophe: the whole city emptied, the road lined with the dead, and Delhi left so deserted that not a cat or dog remained. Ibn Battuta, who arrived a few years later, added the tale of a blind man dragged all the way to Daulatabad, of whom only a leg arrived.

The reality was more limited. The sultan moved the court, officials, scholars and Sufis, and built a road with rest houses between the two cities. Delhi was not abandoned, and when revolts broke out in the north he moved the court back to Delhi and many of the migrants returned north.

Yet the move had lasting effects. Many settlers stayed, and in 1347 these settlers and their sons rebelled and founded the independent Bahmani Sultanate. Daulatabad’s hill fortress, with its dark rock-cut passages and moat, became the key to the Deccan for later rulers.
story.zh:
不喜欢这位苏丹的德里史家，尤其是齐亚乌丁·巴拉尼，把这次迁都描写成一场浩劫：全城清空，沿途尸骨相望，德里荒凉得连猫狗都不剩。几年后来到印度的伊本·白图泰又补充了一个故事：一个盲人被一路拖到道拉塔巴德，到达时只剩下一条腿。

实际情况要有限得多。苏丹迁走的是宫廷、官员、学者和苏非派人士，并在两城之间修建了设有驿站的道路。德里并未被废弃；北方叛乱爆发后，他把宫廷迁回德里，许多移民也随之北返。

然而迁都影响深远。许多移民留了下来，1347年这些移民及其子弟起兵，建立了独立的巴赫曼尼苏丹国。道拉塔巴德山城以其幽暗的凿岩通道和护城河，成为后世统治者控制德干的锁钥。

name.en: Ibn Battuta in India, the Maldives and Ceylon
name.zh: 伊本·白图泰在印度、马尔代夫和锡兰

summary.en: The Moroccan traveller served Muhammad bin Tughluq as a judge in Delhi for eight years, was sent as envoy to China, was shipwrecked at Calicut, served as qadi in the Maldives, climbed Adam’s Peak in Ceylon and visited Bengal before sailing on to Southeast Asia.
summary.zh: 摩洛哥旅行家在德里为穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克担任法官八年，后被派往中国出使，在卡利卡特遭遇船难，在马尔代夫当过法官，登上锡兰的亚当峰，并游历孟加拉，然后启程前往东南亚。

label.en: Delhi: appointed qadi by the sultan
label.zh: 德里：被苏丹任命为法官

label.en: Leaves on the embassy to China; ambushed near Koil (Aligarh)
label.zh: 启程出使中国，在科伊尔（阿里格尔）附近遇袭

label.en: Calicut: the embassy’s junk is wrecked
label.zh: 卡利卡特：使团的大船沉没
马尔代夫：在女苏丹哈迪雅治下任法官
在苏德卡万（吉大港）登陆孟加拉

label.en: Visits the Sufi Shah Jalal at Sylhet
label.zh: 在锡尔赫特拜访苏非圣人沙·贾拉勒
从索纳尔冈启航前往苏门答腊

sources.title: Ibn Battuta, The Travels of Ibn Baṭṭūṭa A.D. 1325–1354, tr. H. A. R. Gibb & C. F. Beckingham, vols. III–IV (1971–94)
Ross E. Dunn, The Adventures of Ibn Battuta (1986; rev. 2005), chs. 9–10

note: Ibn Battuta’s own chronology is inconsistent; dates follow Dunn.

story.en:
Ibn Battuta reached the Indus in 1333 hoping for a post at the court of the richest ruler in the Muslim world, and he got one. Muhammad bin Tughluq made him a qadi of Delhi with a huge salary, and Ibn Battuta soon ran up debts that the sultan generously paid. But he also watched the sultan’s cruelty and, after a spell of disfavour, was glad to be sent off as envoy to China in 1342.

The journey went wrong at once. Rebels ambushed the party, and at Calicut the junk carrying the gifts sank in a storm with most of his companions. Afraid to return to Delhi, he went to the Maldives, married into the elite and served as qadi, until his strict rulings made him unwelcome.

He then climbed Adam’s Peak in Ceylon to see the giant footprint, survived another shipwreck, visited a famous Sufi in the hills of Sylhet and finally sailed east from Sonargaon in Bengal. His account of Delhi remains one of the liveliest portraits of the sultanate.
story.zh:
1333年伊本·白图泰来到印度河畔，希望在伊斯兰世界最富有的君主宫廷中谋得一官半职，他如愿以偿。穆罕默德·本·图格鲁克任命他为德里法官，薪俸极丰；白图泰很快债台高筑，苏丹又慷慨地替他还清。但他也目睹了苏丹的残暴，在一度失宠之后，1342年被派往中国出使时他颇感庆幸。

旅程一开始就出了岔子。叛军伏击了使团；在卡利卡特，载着礼品的大船在风暴中沉没，他的大多数同伴遇难。他不敢回德里，便去了马尔代夫，与当地上层联姻并担任法官，直到他严厉的判决使他不再受欢迎。

此后他登上锡兰的亚当峰瞻仰巨大的足印，再次死里逃生于船难，在锡尔赫特山中拜访一位著名的苏非，最终从孟加拉的索纳尔冈启航东行。他对德里的描述至今仍是苏丹国最生动的写照之一。

name.zh: 胜利之城毗奢耶那伽罗（亨比）

summary.en: The brothers Harihara and Bukka founded a capital among the granite boulders on the Tungabhadra in 1336. By the 16th century Vijayanagara was one of the largest cities in the world, with temples, bazaars, palaces and waterworks; after the defeat at Talikota in 1565 it was sacked and abandoned.
summary.zh: 1336年，诃里诃罗与布卡兄弟在栋格珀德拉河畔的花岗岩巨石间建立都城。到16世纪，毗奢耶那伽罗已是世界上最大的城市之一，遍布神庙、集市、宫殿和水利设施；1565年塔利科塔战败后，城市遭洗劫并被废弃。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Group of Monuments at Hampi
John M. Fritz & George Michell, Hampi Vijayanagara (2011)

note: The founding date of 1336 is traditional (it is linked to the sage Vidyaranya); Harihara I’s earliest records date from the 1340s.

story.en:
Tradition says that Harihara and Bukka, two brothers who had served the Kakatiyas and been carried off by the Delhi sultan, were sent back south to restore order and instead founded their own kingdom, blessed by the sage Vidyaranya. They chose a defensible site where the Tungabhadra cuts through a landscape of boulders already sacred as the kingdom of the monkey king in the Ramayana.

The city grew in rings of walls around a royal centre and a sacred centre. Foreign visitors were dazzled. The Persian envoy Abdur Razzaq (1443) wrote that it had no equal anywhere; the Portuguese visitor Domingo Paes (c. 1520) compared it to Rome and described markets heaped with precious stones, and the nine-day Mahanavami festival.

After the army of the Deccan sultans destroyed the imperial forces at Talikota in 1565, the court fled and the city was looted for months. Its ruins, spread over more than 40 square kilometres, are now one of India’s great archaeological sites.
story.zh:
传说诃里诃罗与布卡兄弟原为卡卡提亚王朝效力，后被德里苏丹掳走，又被派回南方平乱，他们却在智者维迪亚兰亚的祝福下建立了自己的王国。他们选中栋格珀德拉河穿过巨石地貌的一处险要之地，这里早已因《罗摩衍那》中猴王之国的传说而被视为圣地。

城市以王宫区和宗教区为核心，外绕数重城墙。外国访客为之倾倒：波斯使节阿卜杜·拉扎克（1443年）写道，天下无与伦比；葡萄牙旅行者多明戈·派斯（约1520年）把它比作罗马，描述了堆满宝石的集市以及为期九天的大九夜节。

1565年德干诸苏丹联军在塔利科塔歼灭帝国军队后，宫廷出逃，城市遭连月洗劫。如今面积逾40平方公里的遗址是印度最重要的考古遗址之一。

name.en: Conversion of the Maldives to Islam
name.zh: 马尔代夫皈依伊斯兰教

summary.en: According to Maldivian chronicles the Buddhist king of the islands accepted Islam in 1153 from a visiting Muslim scholar, taking the title Sultan Muhammad al-Adil. The Maldives became a sultanate that lasted, apart from a brief republic in 1953, until 1968.
summary.zh: 据马尔代夫编年史记载，1153年这些岛屿的佛教国王从一位来访的穆斯林学者那里接受伊斯兰教，取称号苏丹穆罕默德·阿迪勒。马尔代夫由此成为一个除1953年短暂共和外一直延续到1968年的苏丹国。

sources.title: Ibn Battuta, The Travels, tr. H. A. R. Gibb & C. F. Beckingham, vol. IV (1994), Maldives chapter
Clarence Maloney, People of the Maldive Islands (1980)

note: The date comes from the later Tarikh chronicle; the scholar is variously named Abu al-Barakat al-Barbari (the Moroccan of Ibn Battuta’s account) or Yusuf Shamsuddin of Tabriz. No Wikidata item covers the conversion as an event (checked 2026-11): Q7293385 is the Rannamaari legend and Q3081535 the general topic “Islam in the Maldives”, so no QID is given.

story.en:
Ibn Battuta, who lived in the Maldives in 1343–44, recorded the story the islanders told. Every month a demon rose from the sea, lit up like a ship full of lamps, and the people had to leave a young girl in a temple by the shore for it; she was found dead in the morning. A Maghribi traveller, Abu al-Barakat, took a girl’s place one night and recited the Qur’an until the demon sank back into the sea. The king and his people accepted Islam.

The legend survives in Maldivian tradition as the tale of Rannamaari. Historians see a longer process: Muslim merchants had sailed these waters for centuries, and the atolls lay on the routes between Arabia, India and Southeast Asia.

Islam shaped Maldivian law and the sultanate for eight centuries, and coral-stone mosques such as the Old Friday Mosque of Malé (completed 1658) show the islands’ distinctive craftsmanship.
story.zh:
1343至1344年住在马尔代夫的伊本·白图泰记录了岛民讲述的故事：每个月都有一个魔怪从海中升起，像一艘点满灯火的船；人们必须把一个少女留在海边的神庙里献给它，第二天早上少女便会死去。一位马格里布旅行者阿布·巴拉卡特某夜代替少女留在庙中，诵读《古兰经》，直到魔怪沉回海里。国王和民众于是皈依了伊斯兰教。

这一传说作为“兰纳马里”的故事保存在马尔代夫传统中。历史学家则认为这是一个更漫长的过程：穆斯林商人在这片海域航行已有数百年，而这些环礁正处于阿拉伯、印度与东南亚之间的航线上。

此后八个世纪，伊斯兰教塑造了马尔代夫的法律与苏丹政权；马累老星期五清真寺（1658年建成）等珊瑚石清真寺体现了群岛独特的工艺。

summary.en: Nilakantha Somayaji of Kerala completed the Tantrasangraha, an astronomical treatise that revised the planetary model for Mercury and Venus. With the Yuktibhasha (c. 1530) it preserves the Kerala school’s infinite series for π and trigonometric functions, first found by Madhava.
summary.zh: 喀拉拉的尼拉坎塔·索马亚吉完成天文学著作《系统汇编》，修正了水星和金星的行星模型。它与《理论阐释》（约1530年）一起保存了喀拉拉学派由马德哈瓦首创的圆周率和三角函数无穷级数。

sources.title: K. Ramasubramanian & M. S. Sriram, Tantrasaṅgraha of Nīlakaṇṭha Somayājī (2011)
Kim Plofker, Mathematics in India (2009), ch. 7

story.en:
In the villages of central Kerala, between the 14th and 16th centuries, a chain of Brahmin astronomers passed their learning from teacher to pupil over several generations: Madhava, Parameshvara, Damodara, Nilakantha, Jyeshthadeva and others. They were practical men, correcting calendars and eclipse predictions by observation, but their search for exact values took them into new mathematics.

Madhava found that π could be written as an endless sum, 1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − 1/7 …, and devised correction terms and faster-converging series; with 21 terms of one such series he obtained π to eleven decimal places. Similar series for sine, cosine and arctangent were found again in 17th-century Europe by Newton, Gregory and Leibniz. Nilakantha, who completed the Tantrasangraha around 1500, also proposed, in his commentary on the Aryabhatiya, a planetary model in which the five known planets circle the sun, which in turn circles the earth, close to Tycho Brahe’s system.

The British official Charles Whish brought these texts to European notice in 1834. Whether any of it reached Europe earlier through Jesuits in Kerala is unproven.
story.zh:
14至16世纪间，在喀拉拉中部的村庄里，一批婆罗门天文学家数代师承相传：马德哈瓦、帕拉梅什瓦拉、达摩达拉、尼拉坎塔、杰什塔提婆等人。他们是务实的学者，凭观测修订历法和日月食预报，而对精确数值的追求把他们带进了新的数学领域。

马德哈瓦发现圆周率可以写成无穷级数 1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − 1/7 ……，并设计了修正项和收敛更快的级数，仅用其中一个级数的前21项就把圆周率算到小数点后十一位。类似的正弦、余弦和反正切级数在17世纪的欧洲由牛顿、格雷戈里和莱布尼茨重新发现。约1500年完成《系统汇编》的尼拉坎塔还在《阿耶波多历书》注释中提出已知五大行星绕太阳运行、太阳又绕地球运行的模型，与第谷体系相近。

1834年英国官员查尔斯·维什使这些著作为欧洲所知。至于其中内容是否更早通过在喀拉拉的耶稣会士传到欧洲，尚无定论。

summary.en: Krishnadevaraya of Vijayanagara routed Ismail Adil Shah of Bijapur outside the fortress of Raichur in the disputed Krishna–Tungabhadra doab and took the town. The chronicle of the Portuguese horse trader Fernão Nunes, written in the 1530s, describes the vast camp and the role of Portuguese gunners.
summary.zh: 毗奢耶那伽罗的克里希纳德瓦拉亚在克里希纳河与栋格珀德拉河之间的争议河间地，于赖久尔要塞外击溃比贾布尔的伊斯梅尔·阿迪勒·沙，并夺取该城。葡萄牙马商费尔南·努内斯在1530年代写成的编年史记述了庞大的营地和葡萄牙炮手的作用。

sources.title: Fernão Nunes, Chronicle, in Robert Sewell, A Forgotten Empire (1900)
Richard M. Eaton, A Social History of the Deccan (2005), ch. 4

name.zh: 卡瑙季（比尔格拉姆）之战

summary.en: A year after his defeat at Chausa, the Mughal emperor Humayun was routed by Sher Khan Sur on the Ganges near Kannauj. Humayun fled to Sindh and Persia, and Sher Shah ruled north India until his death in 1545.
summary.zh: 在乔萨战败一年后，莫卧儿皇帝胡马雍又在卡瑙季附近的恒河畔被舍尔汗·苏尔击溃。胡马雍逃往信德和波斯，舍尔沙统治北印度直至1545年去世。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sher Shah of Sur
Gulbadan Begum, Humayun-nama, tr. A. S. Beveridge (1902)

name.en: Charminar and the founding of Hyderabad
name.zh: 查尔米纳尔与海得拉巴的建立

summary.en: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the four-minaret Charminar at the crossing of the main streets of his new capital, Hyderabad, laid out beside the crowded fortress of Golconda. Tradition links it to the end of a plague and to the founding of the city in the Islamic millennium year.
summary.zh: 穆罕默德·库利·库特布·沙在新都海得拉巴主干道的交汇处建起四塔门查尔米纳尔，新都规划在拥挤的戈尔康达要塞旁。传说它与一场瘟疫的结束有关，并象征该城在伊斯兰历一千年时建立。

sources.title: Richard M. Eaton, A Social History of the Deccan (2005)

name.en: Temple of the Tooth at Kandy

summary.en: Vimaladharmasuriya I brought the Buddha’s Tooth Relic, the palladium of Sinhalese kingship, to his new capital at Kandy and built a temple beside the palace. The Sri Dalada Maligawa has housed it ever since; its annual Esala Perahera procession parades a replica on an elephant.
summary.zh: 维摩罗达摩苏利耶一世把象征僧伽罗王权的佛牙舍利迎至新都康提，在王宫旁建寺供奉。自那时起，佛牙寺一直供奉此舍利；每年的埃萨拉游行节都用大象驮着舍利复制品巡游。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Sacred City of Kandy
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Temple of the Tooth
John S. Strong, Relics of the Buddha (2004), ch. 7

note: The relic reached Sri Lanka by tradition in the 4th century; the present buildings largely date from the 18th century.

story.en:
According to the chronicle Dathavamsa, a tooth of the Buddha taken from his funeral pyre was smuggled to Sri Lanka in the 4th century by a princess of Kalinga who hid it in her hair. From then on, whoever held the relic had a claim to rule, and it moved with the capital from Anuradhapura to Polonnaruwa, Dambadeniya, Kotte and finally Kandy.

In 1560 the Portuguese seized what they said was the tooth at Jaffna, and in 1561 Archbishop Gaspar of Goa publicly ground it to powder and burned it. Sinhalese kings replied that the relic they held was the real one, and Vimaladharmasuriya I enshrined it at Kandy around 1595.

The relic’s guardianship was so central to kingship that the British, after taking Kandy in 1815, became its official custodians for a time. A Tamil Tiger truck bomb damaged the temple in 1998; it was restored and remains Sri Lanka’s holiest Buddhist site.
story.zh:
据编年史《佛牙史》记载，从佛陀荼毗火堆中取出的一颗佛牙，在4世纪由一位羯陵伽公主藏于发髻中偷运到斯里兰卡。此后谁掌握佛牙，谁就有统治的名分；佛牙随都城迁移，从阿努拉德普勒到波隆纳鲁沃、丹巴德尼亚、科特，最后到康提。

1560年葡萄牙人在贾夫纳缴获了据称是佛牙的舍利，1561年果阿大主教加斯帕尔当众将其研成粉末并焚毁。僧伽罗国王则回应说，他们手中的才是真舍利；约1595年维摩罗达摩苏利耶一世把它供奉在康提。

守护佛牙对王权至关重要，以至于英国人在1815年占领康提后，一度成为其正式守护者。1998年泰米尔猛虎组织的卡车炸弹损坏了寺庙，修复后它仍是斯里兰卡最神圣的佛教圣地。

summary.en: Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal built a fortress-monastery at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers, which served as Bhutan’s seat of government until 1955. Its relics, including the Rangjung Kharsapani image brought from Tibet, made it the heart of the new Drukpa state.
summary.zh: 夏仲·阿旺朗杰在父河与母河交汇处修建了这座要塞兼寺院，直到1955年它一直是不丹的政府所在地。其中供奉的圣物，包括从西藏带来的“自生观音”像，使它成为新建竹巴国家的核心。

sources.title: Karma Phuntsho, The History of Bhutan (2013)

note: Construction began in 1637 and the dzong was consecrated in 1638.

summary.en: Invited by the king of Kandy to expel the Portuguese, the Dutch East India Company took Galle (1640), Colombo (1656) and Jaffna (1658) and kept the coasts for itself. It ran a cinnamon monopoly, introduced Roman-Dutch law and rebuilt Galle Fort, until Britain seized the colony in 1796.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司应康提国王之邀驱逐葡萄牙人，先后攻取加勒（1640年）、科伦坡（1656年）和贾夫纳（1658年），却把沿海地区据为己有。公司垄断肉桂贸易，引入罗马-荷兰法，重建加勒堡，直到1796年英国夺取该殖民地。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sri Lanka: The Dutch
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications
K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (rev. 2005), ch. 12

summary.en: In the war of succession that followed Shah Jahan’s illness, Aurangzeb and Murad defeated their elder brother Dara Shikoh near Agra. Aurangzeb then confined Shah Jahan in the Agra fort, imprisoned Murad and later had Dara executed.
summary.zh: 沙贾汗病重后爆发的继位战争中，奥朗则布与穆拉德在阿格拉附近击败长兄达拉·希科。奥朗则布随后把沙贾汗软禁在阿格拉堡，囚禁穆拉德，后又处死达拉。

sources.title: François Bernier, Travels in the Mogul Empire, tr. A. Constable (1891)
Jadunath Sarkar, History of Aurangzib, vol. II (1912)

summary.en: On the Brahmaputra at Guwahati, the Ahom general Lachit Borphukan defeated a large Mughal army and fleet under Raja Ram Singh I of Amber. The river battle defeated the last major Mughal attempt to conquer Assam.
summary.zh: 在古瓦哈提的布拉马普特拉河上，阿洪将军拉齐特·博尔普坎击败安伯王公拉姆·辛格一世统率的莫卧儿大军和船队。这场河战挫败了莫卧儿最后一次大规模征服阿萨姆的企图。

sources.title: S. K. Bhuyan, Lachit Barphukan and His Times (1947)
Edward Gait, A History of Assam (rev. 1926)

story.en:
Aurangzeb sent the Rajput general Ram Singh to recover Guwahati, which the Ahoms had retaken in 1667. Ram Singh brought tens of thousands of troops and a fleet, but the Ahom commander Lachit Borphukan refused open battle, fortified the hills and fought a long war of raids along the river.

According to Assamese tradition, while earthworks were being raised under pressure of time, Lachit found that his maternal uncle had let the work slacken and cut off his head, saying that his uncle was not greater than his country. No contemporary document records it, but it is central to his memory in Assam.

In March 1671 the Mughal fleet broke into the narrow stretch of river at Saraighat. Lachit, seriously ill, had himself carried onto a boat and led the counter-attack of small, fast Ahom boats, which trapped and destroyed the larger Mughal vessels. He died the following year. Lachit Divas on 24 November honours him, and the National Defence Academy gives a medal in his name.
story.zh:
奥朗则布派拉杰普特将领拉姆·辛格收复阿洪人在1667年夺回的古瓦哈提。拉姆·辛格率数万大军和一支船队而来，但阿洪统帅拉齐特·博尔普坎拒绝正面交战，他在山地设防，沿河进行长期袭扰。

据阿萨姆传统说法，在时间紧迫下赶筑土垒时，拉齐特发现舅舅督工懈怠，便将其斩首，说舅舅并不比国家更重要。此事不见于同时代文献，却是阿萨姆人记忆中拉齐特形象的核心。

1671年3月，莫卧儿船队闯入萨拉伊加特的狭窄河段。重病中的拉齐特让人把自己抬上船，指挥轻快的阿洪小船反击，围困并摧毁了较大的莫卧儿战船。他于次年去世。每年11月24日的“拉齐特日”纪念他，印度国防学院也设有以他命名的奖章。

summary.en: Shivaji Bhonsle, who had fought Bijapur and the Mughals for three decades, was crowned Chhatrapati in a Vedic ceremony at his hill fort of Raigad. The coronation made the Maratha kingdom a sovereign Hindu state with its own era, coinage and council of eight ministers.
summary.zh: 与比贾布尔和莫卧儿人作战三十年的西瓦吉·蓬斯勒在他的山城赖加德以吠陀仪式加冕为“查特拉帕蒂”（君王）。这次加冕使马拉塔王国成为拥有自己纪元、货币和八大臣会议的主权印度教国家。

sources.title: Henry Oxenden, diary of the English embassy at Raigad (1674), in H. Fawcett (ed.), The English Factories in India, New Series vol. I (1936)

note: The QID is the fort itself.

story.en:
By 1674 Shivaji controlled a chain of forts and much of the western coast, had escaped from house arrest at Aurangzeb’s court in Agra in 1666, and twice sacked the Mughal port of Surat. But he was legally still the son of a Bijapur noble. To make himself a king equal to the Mughal emperor and the sultans, he needed a coronation, and that required proof that his family were Kshatriyas.

The Benares scholar Gaga Bhatta produced a genealogy linking the Bhonsles to the Sisodia Rajputs of Mewar. On 6 June 1674 at Raigad, Shivaji was invested with the sacred thread, weighed against gold and other metals that were given away, and enthroned. An English envoy, Henry Oxenden, attended and secured trading rights.

Shivaji started a new era from the coronation and minted coins with the title Chhatrapati. He died six years later, but the kingdom he had defined survived Aurangzeb’s quarter-century war against it and grew into the Maratha Confederacy.
story.zh:
到1674年，西瓦吉已控制一连串山城和西海岸大片地区，1666年从奥朗则布在阿格拉宫廷的软禁中脱身，还两次洗劫莫卧儿港口苏拉特。但在名分上，他仍只是一位比贾布尔贵族的儿子。要成为与莫卧儿皇帝和诸苏丹平起平坐的国王，他需要加冕，而这又要求证明他的家族属于刹帝利。

瓦拉纳西学者伽伽·跋陀编出一份世系，把蓬斯勒家族与梅瓦尔的锡索迪亚拉杰普特人联系起来。1674年6月6日，西瓦吉在赖加德佩戴圣线，以等重的黄金及其他金属称身并施舍，随后登上王座。英国使节亨利·奥克森登出席典礼，并获得了贸易特权。

西瓦吉以加冕之年开创新纪元，铸造带有“查特拉帕蒂”称号的钱币。六年后他去世，但他所奠定的王国挺过了奥朗则布长达四分之一个世纪的征讨，并发展成马拉塔联盟。

summary.en: After an eight-month siege, Aurangzeb took the fortress of Golconda when a bribed officer opened a gate. The last Qutb Shahi king, Abul Hasan, was imprisoned at Daulatabad, and the Mughal Empire reached its greatest extent.
summary.zh: 经过八个月的围攻，一名被收买的军官打开城门，奥朗则布攻占戈尔康达要塞。末代库特布·沙希国王阿布勒·哈桑被囚于道拉塔巴德，莫卧儿帝国疆域达到极盛。

sources.title: Jadunath Sarkar, History of Aurangzib, vol. IV (1919)
Richard M. Eaton, A Social History of the Deccan (2005), ch. 7

summary.en: At the Vaisakhi festival at Anandpur, Guru Gobind Singh initiated five Sikhs, the Panj Piare, into a new order, the Khalsa (“the pure”), with a baptism of sweetened water stirred with a sword. Men took the name Singh (women later Kaur), and members adopted the five outward signs of the faith.
summary.zh: 在阿南德普尔的拜萨基节上，古鲁·戈宾德·辛格以剑搅拌的甜水为五位锡克教徒（五爱者）施洗，创立新的团体“卡尔萨”（纯洁者）。男性成员取名辛格（女性取名考尔是后来的事），成员并佩戴信仰的五种外在标志。

sources.title: W. H. McLeod, Sikhs of the Khalsa: A History of the Khalsa Rahit (2003)
J. S. Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab (rev. 1998), ch. 5

note: The date is traditionally 30 March 1699; the detailed account of the ceremony comes from 18th-century Sikh sources.

story.en:
Gobind Singh had become Guru as a boy after the Mughal authorities beheaded his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, in Delhi in 1675. Sikh tradition says that at the Vaisakhi gathering of 1699 he came out of a tent with a drawn sword and asked who would give his head. One man stepped forward and was led inside; the Guru came out with a bloody sword and asked again, five times. Then he brought out all five alive, dressed like himself.

These Panj Piare (Five Beloved Ones), drawn from different castes, received amrit, water and sugar stirred with a double-edged sword, and the Guru then received it from them. Men of the Khalsa took the name Singh (lion); the name Kaur (princess) for women became standard later; all were to keep uncut hair, a comb, a steel bangle, a sword and a particular undergarment.

The Khalsa turned the Sikhs into a disciplined community able to fight. Within a century its warrior bands controlled the Punjab, and Ranjit Singh built a kingdom on them.
story.zh:
1675年，莫卧儿当局在德里将其父古鲁·德格·巴哈杜尔斩首，戈宾德·辛格年少即继任古鲁。锡克传统说，在1699年拜萨基节集会上，他手持出鞘之剑走出帐篷，问谁愿献出自己的头颅。一人上前，被带入帐中；古鲁提着染血的剑出来再问，如此五次。随后他把五人全都活着带了出来，五人装束与他相同。

这五位来自不同种姓的“五爱者”接受了“甘露”，即用双刃剑搅拌的糖水，古鲁随后也从他们手中受洗。卡尔萨的男子取名“辛格”（狮子），女子名“考尔”（公主）则是后来才成为定制的；人人须蓄发、佩梳子、钢镯、短剑，并穿特定的内衣。

卡尔萨把锡克教徒变成了一个有纪律、能作战的群体。不到一个世纪，其武装团体就控制了旁遮普，兰吉特·辛格在此基础上建立了王国。

summary.en: Marthanda Varma of Travancore defeated a Dutch East India Company force that had landed at Colachel, one of the first defeats of a European army by an Indian state. The captured Dutch officer Eustachius De Lannoy went on to train and command Travancore’s army.
summary.zh: 特拉凡科尔的马尔坦达·瓦尔马击败在科拉切尔登陆的荷兰东印度公司军队，这是印度国家首次击败欧洲军队的战例之一。被俘的荷兰军官尤斯塔丘斯·德·兰诺伊后来为特拉凡科尔训练并统领军队。

sources.title: A. Sreedhara Menon, A Survey of Kerala History (1967)

name.en: Gorkha conquest of the Kathmandu Valley
name.zh: 廓尔喀征服加德满都谷地

summary.en: Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha took Nuwakot in 1744, blockaded the trade of the three Malla kingdoms for two decades, and finally took Kirtipur (1767), Kathmandu and Patan (1768) and Bhaktapur (1769). His conquest created the modern state of Nepal.
summary.zh: 廓尔喀的普里特维·纳拉扬·沙阿于1744年攻取努瓦科特，封锁马拉三王国的贸易长达二十年，最终攻取基尔蒂普尔（1767年）、加德满都和帕坦（1768年）以及巴克塔普尔（1769年）。这一征服造就了现代尼泊尔国家。

label.zh: 首次进攻基尔蒂普尔失败

label.en: Makwanpur taken; Mir Qasim’s Bengal force repulsed
label.zh: 攻取马克万普尔，击退米尔·卡西姆的孟加拉军

label.en: Kathmandu taken during Indra Jatra; Patan follows
label.zh: 因陀罗节期间攻取加德满都，帕坦随之陷落

sources.title: Ludwig F. Stiller, The Rise of the House of Gorkha (1973)
John Whelpton, A History of Nepal (2005), ch. 2

note: Wikidata’s campaign item runs to 1816 and includes the later expansion under Prithvi Narayan’s successors; this record covers the conquest of the valley.

story.en:
Gorkha was a poor hill kingdom; the Kathmandu Valley was rich from farming and the trade between India and Tibet. Prithvi Narayan Shah, king at twenty, spent years preparing: he obtained firearms in Banaras, made alliances with neighbouring hill chiefs and in 1744 seized Nuwakot, which controlled the route north.

He then strangled the valley economically, closing the passes so that salt, cotton and other goods could not get in. The Malla kings, quarrelling among themselves, called for help; in 1767 the East India Company sent a small expedition under Captain Kinloch, which was beaten back by disease and the Gorkhalis.

Kirtipur, on a ridge above the valley, resisted three assaults; when it surrendered in 1767 its men are said to have had their noses cut off. On 25 September 1768, while Kathmandu celebrated the festival of Indra Jatra, the Gorkhali army walked in, and Prithvi Narayan is said to have taken the seat prepared for the king. Bhaktapur fell the next year, and Kathmandu has been Nepal’s capital ever since.
story.zh:
廓尔喀是一个贫瘠的山地王国，而加德满都谷地则因农业和印藏贸易而富庶。二十岁即位的普里特维·纳拉扬·沙阿花了多年准备：他从瓦拉纳西获得火器，与邻近山地酋长结盟，并于1744年夺取控制北上商道的努瓦科特。

随后他对谷地实行经济封锁，关闭山口，使盐、棉布等货物无法运入。彼此争斗的马拉诸王求援；1767年东印度公司派金洛赫上尉率小股部队前来，被疾病和廓尔喀军击退。

位于谷地上方山脊的基尔蒂普尔抵挡了三次进攻；1767年投降时，据说城中男子被割去鼻子。1768年9月25日，加德满都正在庆祝因陀罗节，廓尔喀军队长驱直入，据说普里特维·纳拉扬坐上了为国王准备的座位。次年巴克塔普尔陷落，此后加德满都一直是尼泊尔首都。

summary.en: After the monsoon failed in 1769, famine swept Bengal and Bihar, recently placed under East India Company revenue control. Perhaps a third of the population of Bengal, about ten million people, died, while the Company kept up its tax collection.
summary.zh: 1769年季风失调后，饥荒席卷刚刚归东印度公司征税管辖的孟加拉和比哈尔。孟加拉人口约三分之一、即约一千万人死亡，而公司照旧征税。

sources.title: Rajat Datta, Society, Economy and the Market: Commercialization in Rural Bengal c. 1760–1800 (2000)
William Wilson Hunter, The Annals of Rural Bengal (1868), ch. 1

note: The death toll of ten million (a third of Bengal) comes from Warren Hastings’s 1772 report; some historians think it is exaggerated. Wikidata starts the famine in 1767.

story.en:
After Plassey and Buxar, the East India Company gained the diwani of Bengal in 1765: the right to collect its land revenue. It pressed for more money to pay its army and shareholders. When the rains failed in 1769, the rice harvest collapsed across much of Bengal and Bihar.

By 1770, contemporary accounts say, people were selling their children and eating leaves; travellers described corpses lying in the streets of Murshidabad and floating in the Hooghly. Company servants were accused of hoarding rice and selling it at huge profit. Yet revenue collections in 1771 were higher than in 1768, because the survivors were made to pay for the dead.

Warren Hastings reported in 1772 that a third of the inhabitants had perished. Abandoned land went back to jungle for decades. In London the scandal fed the debate that led to the Regulating Act of 1773, the first step in Parliament’s control over the Company’s rule in India.
story.zh:
普拉西和布克萨尔战役之后，东印度公司于1765年获得孟加拉的“迪瓦尼”，即征收田赋的权力。为了支付军费和股东红利，公司不断加征。1769年雨季失调，孟加拉和比哈尔大部分地区的稻谷收成全面崩溃。

据当时记载，到1770年人们卖儿鬻女、以树叶充饥；旅行者描述穆尔希达巴德街头横尸遍地，胡格利河上浮尸漂流。公司职员被指控囤积稻米、牟取暴利。然而1771年的税收反而高于1768年，因为幸存者被迫替死者缴税。

沃伦·黑斯廷斯在1772年报告说，三分之一的居民已经死亡。荒芜的土地数十年后才重新开垦。在伦敦，这一丑闻推动了导致1773年《管理法》的辩论，那是议会控制公司在印度统治的第一步。

summary.en: Governor-General Cornwallis fixed the land revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa forever, making the zamindars owners of the land in return for a set annual payment. It created a powerful landlord class while leaving cultivators exposed to rising rents.
summary.zh: 总督康沃利斯把孟加拉、比哈尔和奥里萨的田赋永久固定下来，使柴明达尔以每年缴纳定额田赋为条件成为土地所有者。它造就了强大的地主阶层，却让耕种者承受不断上涨的地租。

sources.title: Ranajit Guha, A Rule of Property for Bengal (1963)

summary.en: Major-General Arthur Wellesley, the future Duke of Wellington, defeated the combined armies of the Maratha chiefs Daulat Rao Scindia and the Raja of Berar, despite being heavily outnumbered. Wellington later called it the bloodiest action for its size he ever saw.
summary.zh: 少将阿瑟·韦尔斯利（后来的威灵顿公爵）在兵力悬殊的情况下击败马拉塔首领道拉特·拉奥·辛迪亚和贝拉尔王公的联军。威灵顿后来称，就规模而言，这是他见过的最血腥的战斗。

name.en: Anglo-Nepalese War and Treaty of Sugauli
name.zh: 英尼战争与《苏高利条约》

summary.en: Border disputes led the East India Company to invade Nepal. Gorkhali garrisons such as Balbhadra Kunwar’s at Nalapani held off much larger forces, but defeat forced Nepal to accept the Treaty of Sugauli, ceding Kumaon, Garhwal, much of the Terai and the lands it had taken from Sikkim.
summary.zh: 边界纠纷导致东印度公司入侵尼泊尔。巴尔巴德拉·昆瓦尔在纳拉帕尼等地的廓尔喀守军抵挡了数倍于己的敌军，但战败迫使尼泊尔接受《苏高利条约》，割让库马盎、加瓦尔、特莱平原大部以及从锡金夺取的土地。

sources.title: John Pemble, Britain’s Gurkha War: The Invasion of Nepal, 1814–16 (2008)
John Whelpton, A History of Nepal (2005)

note: Marker at Nalapani (Khalanga fort, Dehradun), the war’s best-known siege.

story.en:
The Gorkhali state had expanded along the whole length of the Himalaya from Sikkim to the Sutlej, and its border with Company territory in the Terai lowlands was full of disputes. In 1814 Governor-General Lord Hastings sent four columns into the hills.

At Nalapani, a small hill fort near Dehradun, about 600 Gorkhalis under Balbhadra Kunwar, women and children among them, held out for a month against some 3,500 Company troops. Major-General Rollo Gillespie was killed leading an assault. When the water ran out, the survivors cut their way out. The British raised a memorial to their own dead and, unusually, another honouring Balbhadra and his men as brave adversaries.

David Ochterlony drove the Nepalese from the western hills in 1815, and when Nepal balked at the peace terms his 1816 advance towards Kathmandu forced it to ratify the Treaty of Sugauli. Nepal lost about a third of its territory and accepted a British resident in Kathmandu, but remained independent. Impressed by its enemies, the Company began recruiting Gurkha soldiers, a tradition that continues in the British and Indian armies.
story.zh:
廓尔喀国家已沿喜马拉雅山脉从锡金扩张到萨特莱杰河，它与公司领地在特莱低地的边界纠纷不断。1814年总督黑斯廷斯勋爵派四路纵队进入山区。

在德拉敦附近的小山堡纳拉帕尼，巴尔巴德拉·昆瓦尔率约600名廓尔喀人（其中有妇女儿童）对抗约3,500名公司军队，坚守了一个月。少将罗洛·吉莱斯皮在率队强攻时阵亡。水源断绝后，幸存者杀出重围。英国人为自己的阵亡者立碑，还罕见地另立一碑，纪念巴尔巴德拉及其部下这些英勇的对手。

1815年戴维·奥克特洛尼把尼泊尔军逐出西部山区；尼泊尔拒不接受和约条款后，他于1816年向加德满都进军，迫使尼泊尔批准《苏高利条约》。尼泊尔失去约三分之一领土，并接受英国驻加德满都代表，但保持了独立。公司对对手印象深刻，开始招募廓尔喀士兵，这一传统至今延续于英国和印度军队。

summary.en: Kandyan chiefs, alienated by their king Sri Vikrama Rajasinha, helped a British force take Kandy and signed a convention deposing him and placing the kingdom under the British Crown. It ended over two thousand years of monarchy on the island and united the whole island under one colonial government.
summary.zh: 与国王室利·维克拉马·罗阇辛哈离心离德的康提贵族协助英军攻占康提，并签署条约废黜国王，把王国置于英国王室之下。它结束了岛上两千多年的君主统治，使全岛统一于一个殖民政府之下。

sources.title: K. M. de Silva, A History of Sri Lanka (rev. 2005), ch. 16
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sri Lanka: British rule
P. E. Pieris, Tri Sinhala: The Last Phase, 1796–1815 (1939)

note: Signed on 2 March 1815 in the Audience Hall at Kandy; Wikidata gives 10 March, the date of its proclamation.

story.en:
Sri Vikrama Rajasinha, the last king of Kandy, came from the south Indian Nayakkar family that had held the throne since 1739. His growing suspicion of his nobles turned to terror: when his chief minister Ehelepola rebelled and fled to the British, the king had Ehelepola’s wife and children executed.

The British governor, Robert Brownrigg, used the crisis. In February 1815 his troops marched into the hills almost unopposed, and the king was found hiding near Medamahanuwara and captured. On 2 March the chiefs met the British in the royal Audience Hall and signed a convention that deposed the king, vested the kingdom in the British Crown and promised to protect Buddhism and Kandyan customs. As the Union Jack went up, a Buddhist monk is said to have pulled it down in protest.

The king was exiled to Vellore in India, where he died in 1832. The chiefs soon felt cheated, and the great rebellion of 1817–18 was put down with great severity.
story.zh:
康提末代国王室利·维克拉马·罗阇辛哈出身自1739年起占据王位的南印度纳亚卡尔家族。他对贵族日益猜忌，以至于滥施恐怖：首相埃赫勒波拉叛逃投英后，国王处决了埃赫勒波拉的妻儿。

英国总督罗伯特·布朗里格乘机而动。1815年2月，英军几乎未遇抵抗便开进山区，国王在梅达马哈努瓦拉附近藏身时被俘。3月2日，贵族们在王宫议事厅与英方会面，签署条约废黜国王，把王国移交英国王室，并承诺保护佛教和康提习俗。据说英国国旗升起时，一名佛教僧人上前将其扯下以示抗议。

国王被流放到印度韦洛尔，1832年死在那里。贵族们很快觉得受骗，1817至1818年的大起义遭到严酷镇压。

summary.en: Governor-General William Bentinck made sati, the burning of widows on their husbands’ pyres, a crime in the Bengal Presidency. Ram Mohan Roy had campaigned against the practice for over a decade; orthodox Hindus appealed to the Privy Council and lost.
summary.zh: 总督威廉·本廷克在孟加拉管区把萨蒂（寡妇在丈夫火葬柴堆上自焚）定为犯罪。拉姆·莫汉·罗伊为反对这一习俗已奔走十余年；正统印度教徒向枢密院上诉，最终败诉。

sources.title: Lata Mani, Contentious Traditions: The Debate on Sati in Colonial India (1998)
Lynn Zastoupil, Rammohun Roy and the Making of Victorian Britain (2010)

story.en:
Sati was never universal, but in early 19th-century Bengal, especially around Calcutta, its numbers rose: official returns recorded over 8,000 cases between 1815 and 1828. Ram Mohan Roy is said to have been driven to act after seeing his own sister-in-law burned. He argued from the Hindu law books that the scriptures did not require it, and published tracts in Bengali and English.

The East India Company had long avoided interfering in religious custom. William Bentinck, who arrived as Governor-General in 1828, consulted army officers and judges, concluded that a ban would not cause a mutiny, and on 4 December 1829 issued Regulation XVII declaring sati “culpable homicide”.

Orthodox Calcutta leaders founded the Dharma Sabha and petitioned London. Ram Mohan went to England in part to oppose their appeal, which the Privy Council rejected in 1832. Historians now stress that the debate was conducted largely by men, about women whose own voices are rarely heard in the record.
story.zh:
萨蒂从来不是普遍习俗，但在19世纪初的孟加拉，尤其是加尔各答周边，案例不断增加：官方记录显示1815至1828年间超过8,000起。据说拉姆·莫汉·罗伊目睹嫂子被焚后决心行动。他依据印度教法典论证经典并不要求殉夫，并用孟加拉文和英文发表小册子。

东印度公司长期避免干涉宗教习俗。1828年就任总督的威廉·本廷克征询军官和法官的意见，认定禁令不会引发兵变，于1829年12月4日颁布第十七号条例，宣布萨蒂属于“应受惩处的杀人罪”。

加尔各答正统派领袖成立“正法会”向伦敦请愿。拉姆·莫汉前往英国，部分目的就是反对他们的上诉；1832年枢密院驳回了上诉。今天的历史学家强调，这场辩论主要由男性进行，而当事女性自己的声音在记录中鲜少出现。

name.en: Kot massacre and the rise of the Ranas
name.zh: 科特大屠杀与拉纳家族的崛起

summary.en: After the murder of a royal favourite, Queen Rajya Lakshmi summoned the court to the Kot, an armoury courtyard by the palace in Kathmandu, where Jung Bahadur Kunwar and his brothers killed dozens of nobles. Jung Bahadur became prime minister and founded the hereditary Rana regime, which ruled Nepal until 1951.
summary.zh: 一名王室宠臣被杀后，王后拉吉亚·拉克什米把朝臣召集到加德满都王宫旁的兵器库庭院“科特”，忠格·巴哈杜尔·昆瓦尔及其兄弟在此杀死数十名贵族。忠格·巴哈杜尔出任首相，建立世袭的拉纳政权，统治尼泊尔直到1951年。

sources.title: John Whelpton, Kings, Soldiers and Priests: Nepalese Politics and the Rise of Jang Bahadur Rana, 1830–1857 (1991)

story.en:
Nepal’s court in the 1840s was a tangle of rival noble families, a weak king, Rajendra, and an ambitious junior queen, Rajya Lakshmi Devi. On the night of 14 September 1846 her favourite, Gagan Singh, was shot dead while at prayer. The queen called all the courtiers to the Kot and demanded the murderer.

What followed is told differently by different sides, but the outcome is clear: by morning dozens of the leading nobles lay dead, many cut down by soldiers loyal to Jung Bahadur Kunwar, a young officer who emerged as commander-in-chief and prime minister. Within months he had exiled the queen, whom the king followed to Benares, and in 1847 he deposed the king.

Jung Bahadur made the premiership hereditary in his family, took the title Rana and reduced the Shah kings to figureheads. He visited Britain and France in 1850 and sent troops to help the British in 1857. The Ranas ruled for 104 years, until King Tribhuvan escaped to India and returned in 1951.
story.zh:
19世纪40年代的尼泊尔宫廷错综复杂：贵族家族相互倾轧，国王拉金德拉软弱，年轻的二王后拉吉亚·拉克什米·德维野心勃勃。1846年9月14日夜，她的宠臣加甘·辛格在祈祷时被枪杀。王后把所有朝臣召到“科特”，要求交出凶手。

此后的经过各方说法不一，但结果很清楚：到天亮时，数十名重臣横尸当场，许多人死于效忠忠格·巴哈杜尔·昆瓦尔的士兵刀下；这位年轻军官随即成为总司令兼首相。几个月内，他流放了王后（国王随她去了贝拿勒斯），并于1847年废黜了国王。

忠格·巴哈杜尔使首相之位在家族内世袭，自称“拉纳”，把沙阿国王变成傀儡。1850年他访问英法；1857年他还派兵援助英国人。拉纳家族统治了104年，直到特里布文国王出走印度并于1951年返国。

name.en: First passenger train in India: Bombay to Thane
name.zh: 印度第一列客运火车：孟买至塔纳

summary.en: A train of 14 carriages hauled by three locomotives carried some 400 guests 34 km from Bori Bunder in Bombay to Thane, opening the Great Indian Peninsula Railway. By 1900 India had about 40,000 km of track, built for trade and troops and paid for by guaranteed returns to British investors.
summary.zh: 一列由三台机车牵引的14节车厢列车载着约400名宾客，从孟买博里班德尔驶抵34公里外的塔纳，大印度半岛铁路由此开通。到1900年印度铁路已约4万公里，其修建服务于贸易与军队调动，资金来自向英国投资者保证的固定回报。

sources.title: Ian J. Kerr, Engines of Change: The Railroads That Made India (2007)

note: The QID is the railway company (founded 1849). The 1853 line was still run by the East India Company, before Crown rule (1858).

summary.en: Drought linked to a strong El Niño destroyed harvests across the Deccan and south India. Between about five and ten million people died, while grain continued to be exported and relief was kept deliberately meagre on grounds of economy.
summary.zh: 与强烈厄尔尼诺相关的干旱摧毁了德干和南印度的收成。约五百万至一千万人死亡，与此同时粮食继续出口，赈济出于节省开支的考虑被刻意压低。

sources.title: Mike Davis, Late Victorian Holocausts: El Niño Famines and the Making of the Third World (2001), ch. 1
Report of the Indian Famine Commission (1880)

note: Estimates of excess deaths range from about 5.5 million (official) to over 10 million.

story.en:
The monsoon of 1876 failed over the Deccan plateau and Madras, and the next year’s rains were poor too. Behind it, climate historians now see one of the strongest El Niño events on record, which also brought famine to northern China and Brazil.

The Viceroy, Lord Lytton, was committed to free-market principles and to economy. Grain moved by the new railways to where prices were highest, including export markets, while the hungry in the countryside could not afford it. Sir Richard Temple, sent to cut relief costs, set the ration in relief camps at one pound of grain a day for heavy labour, less than the rations of the Buchenwald camp, as the historian Mike Davis later pointed out; doctors protested, and death rates in the camps soared. That winter Lytton held the lavish Delhi Durbar proclaiming Queen Victoria Empress of India.

The disaster fed early Indian nationalist critiques of the “drain of wealth” to Britain. It also led to the Famine Commission of 1880 and the Famine Codes, which set rules for declaring famine and organising relief.
story.zh:
1876年德干高原和马德拉斯的季风失调，次年雨水也不足。今天的气候史学家认为，其背后是有记录以来最强的厄尔尼诺事件之一，它同时给华北和巴西带来了饥荒。

总督李顿勋爵信奉自由市场原则，力主节省开支。粮食通过新修的铁路运往价格最高的地方，包括出口市场，而农村的饥民买不起粮食。被派去削减赈济开支的理查德·坦普尔爵士把赈济营重体力劳动者的口粮定为每天一磅谷物；历史学家迈克·戴维斯后来指出，这比布痕瓦尔德集中营的配给还少。医生们提出抗议，营中死亡率急剧上升。就在那个冬天，李顿在德里举行奢华的“杜尔巴”盛典，宣布维多利亚女王为印度女皇。

这场灾难为早期印度民族主义者批判财富“外流”至英国提供了依据，也促成了1880年的饥荒委员会和《饥荒法典》，后者规定了宣布饥荒和组织赈济的规则。

name.en: Tagore wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
name.zh: 泰戈尔获诺贝尔文学奖

summary.en: Rabindranath Tagore received the Nobel Prize in Literature for Gitanjali (Song Offerings), his own English versions of Bengali devotional poems published in London in 1912 with a preface by W. B. Yeats. He was the first non-European to win the literature prize and the first Asian Nobel laureate.
summary.zh: 泰戈尔凭《吉檀迦利》（献歌）获诺贝尔文学奖。这部诗集是他本人从孟加拉语宗教诗歌翻译的英文版，1912年在伦敦出版，叶芝作序。他是首位获得文学奖的非欧洲人，也是首位亚洲诺贝尔奖得主。

sources.title: NobelPrize.org: The Nobel Prize in Literature 1913
Krishna Dutta & Andrew Robinson, Rabindranath Tagore: The Myriad-Minded Man (1995)

note: Marker at Santiniketan, where Tagore heard the news.

summary.en: Working with K. S. Krishnan at the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in Calcutta, C. V. Raman showed that a small fraction of light scattered by liquids changes colour, revealing the vibrations of molecules. The discovery won the 1930 Nobel Prize and is marked as India’s National Science Day.
summary.zh: 拉曼与K. S. 克里希南在加尔各答印度科学培育协会合作，证明液体散射的光中有一小部分颜色发生改变，从而揭示了分子的振动。这一发现获1930年诺贝尔奖，2月28日被定为印度国家科学日。

sources.title: C. V. Raman & K. S. Krishnan, ‘A new type of secondary radiation’, Nature 121 (1928)
NobelPrize.org: The Nobel Prize in Physics 1930

story.en:
Raman did his early research in the evenings, after his job as a government accountant, in the modest laboratory of the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science. On the voyage home from Britain in 1921 he studied why the sea looks blue and concluded, against Lord Rayleigh, that the water itself scatters light.

Back in Calcutta he and his students spent years on light scattering in liquids. Using sunlight focused through a telescope lens and filters of complementary colours, they saw a faint glow of a different colour from the incoming light. In February 1928, with a mercury lamp and a spectroscope, Raman and K. S. Krishnan showed clear new lines: a fingerprint of molecular vibrations.

Raman was so sure of the importance that he booked passage to Stockholm before the Nobel Prize was announced. He received it in 1930. Raman spectroscopy, made easy by lasers, is now used everywhere from chemistry labs to identifying fake medicines and studying minerals on Mars.
story.zh:
拉曼早年在政府会计工作之余，每晚在印度科学培育协会简陋的实验室里做研究。1921年从英国回国途中，他研究海水为何呈蓝色，得出与瑞利勋爵不同的结论：是水本身散射了光。

回到加尔各答后，他和学生们花了数年时间研究液体中的光散射。他们用望远镜透镜聚焦阳光，配以互补色滤光片，看到了一种颜色不同于入射光的微弱辉光。1928年2月，拉曼与K. S. 克里希南用汞灯和分光镜拍到了清晰的新谱线，这是分子振动的“指纹”。

拉曼对这一发现的重要性深信不疑，在诺贝尔奖公布之前就订好了去斯德哥尔摩的船票。1930年他如愿获奖。借助激光而变得简便的拉曼光谱学，如今从化学实验室到鉴别假药、研究火星矿物，无处不用。

summary.en: Gandhi fasted in Yerwada jail against the British award of separate electorates to the “depressed classes”. Ambedkar, under heavy pressure, agreed instead to seats reserved for them within joint electorates, a system that shaped Indian democracy.
summary.zh: 甘地在耶拉瓦达监狱绝食，反对英国给予“受压迫阶层”单独选区。在巨大压力下，安贝德卡尔改为同意在联合选区内为他们保留席位，这一制度深刻影响了印度民主。

sources.title: Christophe Jaffrelot, Dr Ambedkar and Untouchability (2005), ch. 3

summary.en: At Gowalia Tank in Bombay, the Congress demanded an immediate end to British rule and Gandhi called on Indians to “do or die”. The leadership was arrested within hours; strikes, sabotage and parallel governments followed and were crushed, with about 100,000 people jailed.
summary.zh: 国大党在孟买戈瓦利亚池广场要求立即结束英国统治，甘地号召印度人“不成功便成仁”。数小时内领导人全部被捕；随后爆发了罢工、破坏活动和平行政府，均遭镇压，约十万人入狱。

sources.title: Paul Greenough, ‘Political mobilization and the underground literature of the Quit India Movement’, Social Scientist 27 (1999)

story.en:
In 1942 Japanese armies had taken Burma and stood on India’s border, and Britain had declared India at war without consulting Indian leaders. The Cripps Mission’s offer of dominion status after the war satisfied no one. Gandhi concluded that Britain should leave at once and let India face Japan on its own terms.

On 8 August the All-India Congress Committee passed the Quit India resolution at Gowalia Tank in Bombay, and Gandhi told the crowd: “Do or die. We shall either free India or die in the attempt.” Before dawn the next day Gandhi, Nehru and the entire leadership were arrested.

Without leaders, the movement became a spontaneous uprising. Students and peasants attacked railway lines, telegraph wires and police stations, and in places such as Satara, Midnapore and Ballia rebels set up their own governments. The British used troops, aircraft machine-gunned crowds in Bihar, and about 100,000 people were jailed. Militarily the revolt failed, but it showed that India could no longer be ruled without consent.
story.zh:
1942年，日军已攻占缅甸、兵临印度边境，而英国未经与印度领袖协商就宣布印度参战。克里普斯使团提出的战后自治领地位方案无人满意。甘地认为英国应立即撤离，让印度按自己的方式面对日本。

8月8日，全印国大党委员会在孟买戈瓦利亚池广场通过“退出印度”决议，甘地对人群说：“不成功便成仁。我们要么解放印度，要么为此而死。”次日黎明前，甘地、尼赫鲁及全体领导层被捕。

失去领袖后，运动变成了自发的起义。学生和农民袭击铁路、电报线和警察局；在萨塔拉、米德纳普尔和巴利亚等地，起义者建立了自己的政府。英国出动军队，在比哈尔甚至用飞机扫射人群，约十万人入狱。起义在军事上失败了，但它表明，没有印度人的同意，印度已无法再被统治。

name.zh: 第一次印巴克什米尔战争

summary.en: When Pashtun tribal fighters backed by Pakistan invaded Jammu and Kashmir in October 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh acceded to India, which airlifted troops to Srinagar. The war ended with a UN-brokered ceasefire on 1 January 1949, leaving the state divided along a line that still separates Indian and Pakistani control.
summary.zh: 1947年10月，受巴基斯坦支持的普什图部落武装侵入查谟和克什米尔，土邦王公哈里·辛格宣布加入印度，印度随即空运部队到斯利那加。战争以联合国斡旋的1949年1月1日停火结束，土邦沿一条至今仍分隔印巴控制区的界线被一分为二。

sources.title: Srinath Raghavan, War and Peace in Modern India (2010), ch. 4
Alastair Lamb, Kashmir: A Disputed Legacy 1846–1990 (1991)

note: Marker at Srinagar, where Indian troops landed on 27 October 1947.

story.en:
At Partition the princely states were told to join India or Pakistan. Jammu and Kashmir had a Muslim majority and a Hindu Dogra ruler, Hari Singh, who hoped to stay independent. In October 1947, after a revolt in Poonch, thousands of armed tribesmen from Pakistan’s North-West Frontier swept into the valley, looting Baramulla on the way to Srinagar.

The maharaja fled to Jammu and on 26 October signed the Instrument of Accession to India. The next morning Indian troops landed at Srinagar airfield in Dakota transports and held the city. Over the following year fighting spread to the mountains of Poonch, Ladakh and Gilgit, where local forces rebelled against the maharaja and joined Pakistan, and the Pakistani army itself entered the war.

India took the dispute to the United Nations, which called for a ceasefire and a plebiscite. The ceasefire came on 1 January 1949; the plebiscite never happened. The ceasefire line, renamed the Line of Control in 1972, remains one of the most militarised borders in the world.
story.zh:
分治时，各土邦被要求加入印度或巴基斯坦。查谟和克什米尔居民多为穆斯林，统治者却是印度教多格拉王公哈里·辛格，他希望保持独立。1947年10月，在蓬奇发生叛乱后，数千名来自巴基斯坦西北边境的武装部落民涌入克什米尔谷地，在进军斯利那加途中洗劫了巴拉穆拉。

王公逃往查谟，于10月26日签署加入印度的文书。次日清晨，印度军队乘达科塔运输机在斯利那加机场着陆，守住了城市。此后一年，战火蔓延到蓬奇、拉达克和吉尔吉特的山区；吉尔吉特的地方部队反叛王公、投向巴基斯坦，巴基斯坦正规军也加入了战争。

印度把争端提交联合国，联合国呼吁停火并举行公民投票。停火于1949年1月1日实现，公投却始终没有举行。这条停火线在1972年改称“实际控制线”，至今仍是世界上军事化程度最高的边界之一。

name.zh: 马球行动：兼并海得拉巴

summary.en: When the Nizam of Hyderabad refused to join India and the Razakar militia terrorised the countryside, the Indian army invaded in a five-day “police action”. The Nizam surrendered on 17 September 1948; communal killings during and after the operation cost tens of thousands of lives.
summary.zh: 海得拉巴尼扎姆拒绝加入印度，拉扎卡尔民兵在乡间制造恐怖，印度军队遂发动为期五天的“警察行动”。1948年9月17日尼扎姆投降；行动期间及其后的教派仇杀造成数万人死亡。

sources.title: A. G. Noorani, The Destruction of Hyderabad (2013)

note: Death tolls from the communal violence are disputed; the Sunderlal report estimated 27,000–40,000.

summary.en: East Bengal’s students protested against making Urdu the sole state language of Pakistan, though Bengali was the mother tongue of most of its people. Police fired on demonstrators near Dhaka University on 21 February 1952; in 1956 Bengali became a state language. UNESCO later made 21 February International Mother Language Day.
summary.zh: 尽管孟加拉语是巴基斯坦多数人口的母语，当局却要把乌尔都语定为唯一国语，东孟加拉学生为此抗议。1952年2月21日警察在达卡大学附近向示威者开枪；1956年孟加拉语成为国语之一。联合国教科文组织后来把2月21日定为国际母语日。

story.en:
In March 1948 Muhammad Ali Jinnah told a crowd in Dhaka that Urdu and no other language would be the state language of Pakistan. More than half of Pakistan’s citizens spoke Bengali, and students at once objected. The issue simmered until January 1952, when Prime Minister Khawaja Nazimuddin repeated the Urdu-only policy.

Students called a strike for 21 February and defied a ban on gatherings. When they marched out of the university grounds, police opened fire near the medical college hostel. Abul Barkat, Rafiquddin Ahmed, Abdul Jabbar and others were killed; students built a memorial overnight, which the police tore down. The Shaheed Minar (Martyrs’ Monument) now stands on the site.

The movement forced the government to recognise Bengali as a state language in the 1956 constitution, and it became the seedbed of Bengali nationalism that led to independence in 1971. In 1999 UNESCO proclaimed 21 February International Mother Language Day, observed worldwide since 2000.
story.zh:
1948年3月，穆罕默德·阿里·真纳在达卡对民众说，乌尔都语、而非其他语言，将是巴基斯坦的国语。巴基斯坦一半以上的公民讲孟加拉语，学生们当即表示反对。问题一直悬而未决，直到1952年1月总理赫瓦贾·纳齐穆丁重申只用乌尔都语的政策。

学生们号召在2月21日罢课，并违抗集会禁令。当他们走出校园时，警察在医学院宿舍附近开枪。阿布尔·巴尔卡特、拉菲库丁·艾哈迈德、阿卜杜勒·贾巴尔等人遇难；学生们连夜建起纪念碑，又被警察拆毁。如今烈士纪念碑就矗立在原址上。

运动迫使政府在1956年宪法中承认孟加拉语为国语之一，它也成为孕育孟加拉民族主义、最终导致1971年独立的温床。1999年联合国教科文组织宣布2月21日为国际母语日，自2000年起在全世界纪念。

name.en: Ambedkar’s conversion to Buddhism at Nagpur
name.zh: 安贝德卡尔在那格浦尔皈依佛教

summary.en: B. R. Ambedkar and his wife took refuge in Buddhism at a ceremony in Nagpur, then administered 22 vows to some 400,000 followers, most of them Dalits. The site is now Deekshabhoomi, and the conversions gave Buddhism a mass following in India again.
summary.zh: B. R. 安贝德卡尔与妻子在那格浦尔的仪式上皈依佛教，随后为约40万名追随者（多为达利特）授以22条誓言。仪式所在地今称“迪克沙布米”，这次集体皈依使佛教在印度重新拥有大批信众。

sources.title: Eleanor Zelliot, From Untouchable to Dalit (1992)
Christopher Queen, ‘Dr. Ambedkar and the hermeneutics of Buddhist liberation’, in Engaged Buddhism (1996)

story.en:
In 1935, at a conference at Yeola, Ambedkar declared that although he had been born a Hindu he would not die one. For twenty years he studied the alternatives before choosing Buddhism, a religion born in India that rejected caste and that he reinterpreted as a path of reason and social liberation.

On 14 October 1956, Vijayadashami, the day traditionally held to be that of Ashoka’s conversion, Ambedkar and his wife Savita took the Three Refuges and Five Precepts from the Burmese monk U Chandramani in an open field in Nagpur. He then led the huge crowd in 22 vows, including renouncing Hindu gods and rituals and affirming the equality of all people.

Ambedkar died less than two months later, in Delhi. But the conversions continued, and India’s Buddhists, counted at about 180,000 in the 1951 census, numbered some 3.25 million by 1961, most of them in Maharashtra. Every year on the anniversary hundreds of thousands gather at Deekshabhoomi.
story.zh:
1935年在耶奥拉的一次会议上，安贝德卡尔宣布：虽然他生为印度教徒，却不会作为印度教徒死去。此后二十年间他研究各种选择，最终选定佛教，这一诞生于印度、拒斥种姓的宗教，被他重新诠释为理性与社会解放之道。

1956年10月14日，即胜利十日节（维杰耶达舍米），传统上被视为阿育王皈依佛教之日，安贝德卡尔与妻子萨维塔在那格浦尔一片空地上，从缅甸僧人吴旃陀罗摩尼那里受三皈五戒。随后他带领庞大的人群宣誓22条誓言，包括放弃印度教神祇与仪式、确认人人平等。

不到两个月后，安贝德卡尔在德里去世。但皈依仍在继续，印度佛教徒从1951年人口普查时的约18万人增至1961年的约325万人，大多数在马哈拉施特拉邦。每年纪念日，都有数十万人聚集在迪克沙布米。

summary.en: After Pakistan sent infiltrators into Kashmir (Operation Gibraltar), India opened a front in the Punjab towards Lahore. Large tank battles at Asal Uttar and Chawinda ended in stalemate; a UN ceasefire was followed by the Soviet-brokered Tashkent Declaration in January 1966.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦向克什米尔派遣渗透人员（直布罗陀行动）后，印度在旁遮普开辟进攻拉合尔的战线。阿萨尔乌塔尔和查温达的大规模坦克战以僵持告终；联合国停火之后，双方于1966年1月在苏联斡旋下签署《塔什干宣言》。

sources.title: Srinath Raghavan, War and Peace in Modern India (2010)

note: Marker at Chawinda (Sialkot sector), scene of the largest tank battle.

summary.en: After a court voided her 1971 election, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi had a state of emergency declared, suspending civil liberties, censoring the press and jailing opposition leaders. Forced sterilisations and slum clearances bred anger, and in 1977 voters turned her out in favour of the Janata Party.
summary.zh: 法院宣布其1971年当选无效后，总理英迪拉·甘地促使宣布全国紧急状态，中止公民自由，审查新闻，监禁反对派领导人。强制绝育和清拆贫民窟激起民愤，1977年选民将她赶下台，人民党上台执政。

sources.title: Gyan Prakash, Emergency Chronicles: Indira Gandhi and Democracy’s Turning Point (2019)
Ramachandra Guha, India after Gandhi (2007), ch. 22

story.en:
On 12 June 1975 the Allahabad High Court found Indira Gandhi guilty of electoral malpractice and barred her from office for six years. Opposition leaders led by the veteran Gandhian Jayaprakash Narayan called for mass civil disobedience. On the night of 25 June President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed signed a proclamation of internal emergency; before dawn the police had arrested Narayan, Morarji Desai and hundreds of others, and electricity to Delhi’s newspaper presses was cut.

For 21 months India was ruled by decree. More than 100,000 people were detained without trial. Parliament extended its own term and amended the constitution to shield the prime minister. Her son Sanjay Gandhi drove campaigns to clear slums in Delhi and to sterilise men, often by coercion, with millions of operations in a single year.

In January 1977, believing she would win, Indira Gandhi called elections and released her opponents. The new Janata coalition swept the north, and she lost her own seat. The episode remains a reference point in Indian debates about democracy.
story.zh:
1975年6月12日，阿拉哈巴德高等法院裁定英迪拉·甘地在选举中舞弊，禁止她六年内担任公职。以老甘地主义者贾亚普拉卡什·纳拉扬为首的反对派领导人号召大规模公民不服从。6月25日夜，总统法赫鲁丁·阿里·艾哈迈德签署国内紧急状态公告；天亮前，警察逮捕了纳拉扬、莫拉尔吉·德赛等数百人，德里各报印刷厂的电力被切断。

此后21个月，印度依靠法令统治。十余万人未经审判被拘押。议会延长了自己的任期，并修改宪法以保护总理。她的儿子桑杰·甘地推动在德里清拆贫民窟和对男子实施绝育，往往带有强制，一年之内手术达数百万例。

1977年1月，英迪拉·甘地自信能够获胜，宣布举行选举并释放反对派。新成立的人民党联盟横扫北方，她连自己的议席也丢了。这段经历至今仍是印度讨论民主问题时的参照点。

summary.en: Facing a balance-of-payments crisis, with reserves enough for only a few weeks of imports, the government of P. V. Narasimha Rao and finance minister Manmohan Singh devalued the rupee, dismantled the “licence raj”, cut tariffs and opened India to foreign investment.
summary.zh: 面对外汇储备仅够支付几周进口的国际收支危机，纳拉辛哈·拉奥政府和财政部长曼莫汉·辛格让卢比贬值，拆除“许可证统治”，削减关税，向外国投资开放。

sources.title: Vinay Sitapati, Half-Lion: How P. V. Narasimha Rao Transformed India (2016)
Montek Singh Ahluwalia, Backstage: The Story behind India’s High Growth Years (2020)

story.en:
By mid-1991 India was nearly bankrupt. The Gulf War had raised oil prices and cut remittances, political instability had scared lenders, and foreign exchange reserves had fallen to about a billion dollars. The new government had to pledge the country’s gold: aircraft flew some 47 tonnes to the Bank of England and the Bank of Japan as collateral.

The prime minister, P. V. Narasimha Rao, appointed an economist, Manmohan Singh, as finance minister. In July the rupee was devalued twice, and on 24 July an industrial policy abolished licensing for most industries, the same day Singh presented a budget that cut tariffs and opened sectors to foreign capital. He ended his speech by quoting Victor Hugo: no power on earth can stop an idea whose time has come.

Growth rose to an average of about 6 per cent a year in the following decades, and the software and services industries boomed. Critics point to growing inequality and agrarian distress, but the reforms were never reversed by any later government.
story.zh:
到1991年年中，印度几近破产。海湾战争推高油价并减少了侨汇，政局动荡吓退了贷款方，外汇储备跌至约10亿美元。新政府不得不抵押国家黄金：约47吨黄金被空运到英格兰银行和日本银行作为担保。

总理纳拉辛哈·拉奥任命经济学家曼莫汉·辛格为财政部长。7月卢比两次贬值；7月24日，新的工业政策废除了大多数行业的许可证制度，同一天辛格提交预算，削减关税并向外资开放多个行业。他在演讲结尾引用维克多·雨果的话：时机已到的思想，世上任何力量都无法阻挡。

此后数十年，经济年均增长约6%，软件和服务业蓬勃发展。批评者指出不平等加剧和农业困境，但此后没有任何一届政府逆转这些改革。

summary.en: India carried out five underground nuclear tests at Pokhran in the Thar Desert and declared itself a nuclear-weapon state; Pakistan replied two weeks later with six tests in the Chagai Hills of Balochistan. Both countries faced sanctions, and South Asia became a nuclear-armed region.
summary.zh: 印度在塔尔沙漠的博克兰进行五次地下核试验，宣布成为有核武器国家；两周后巴基斯坦在俾路支省查盖山进行六次核试验作为回应。两国都受到制裁，南亚成为拥核地区。

sources.title: Feroz Hassan Khan, Eating Grass: The Making of the Pakistani Bomb (2012)

note: India’s first test, “Smiling Buddha”, took place at the same range on 18 May 1974.

summary.en: Pakistani soldiers and militants occupied high ridges on the Indian side of the Line of Control above Kargil in Ladakh. India retook the peaks in two months of mountain fighting at altitudes above 5,000 metres, and Pakistan withdrew under US pressure.
summary.zh: 巴基斯坦士兵和武装分子占领了拉达克卡吉尔上方实际控制线印度一侧的高山山脊。印度在海拔5,000米以上的山地激战两个月后夺回各峰，巴基斯坦在美国压力下撤军。

sources.title: Peter R. Lavoy (ed.), Asymmetric Warfare in South Asia: The Causes and Consequences of the Kargil Conflict (2009)

summary.en: Ten gunmen of the Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba landed by boat and attacked a railway terminus, two luxury hotels, a café, a hospital and a Jewish centre over four days, killing 166 people. The sole surviving attacker was tried and executed.
summary.zh: 十名来自巴基斯坦“虔诚军”的枪手乘船登陆，在四天内袭击了火车总站、两家豪华酒店、一家咖啡馆、一所医院和一个犹太中心，造成166人死亡。唯一幸存的袭击者受审后被处决。

sources.title: Cathy Scott-Clark & Adrian Levy, The Siege: The Attack on the Taj (2013)

summary.en: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake centred in Gorkha district killed about 9,000 people, destroyed or damaged some 750,000 houses and brought down temples in the Durbar Squares of Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur. An avalanche it triggered killed climbers at Everest base camp.
summary.zh: 震中位于廓尔喀县的7.8级地震造成约9,000人死亡，约75万所房屋被毁或受损，加德满都、帕坦和巴克塔普尔杜巴广场的多座神庙倒塌。地震引发的雪崩还在珠峰大本营造成登山者死亡。

sources.title: Government of Nepal, National Planning Commission: Post Disaster Needs Assessment (2015)
USGS: M 7.8 – 36 km E of Khudi, Nepal
The Himalayan Times: Kashthamandap temple inaugurated (April 2022)

story.en:
Just before noon on Saturday 25 April 2015, the Indian plate lurched under the Himalaya along a fault some 150 km long. The epicentre was near Barpak in Gorkha district, the homeland of the dynasty that had unified Nepal, but the rupture ran east beneath the Kathmandu Valley, lifting the city by about a metre in under a minute.

In the hill villages stone and mud houses collapsed almost completely; in Kathmandu the nine-storey Dharahara tower, crowded with Saturday visitors, fell, killing some 180 people, and the Kasthamandap, the wooden pavilion that gave the city its name, was reduced to rubble. On Everest an avalanche swept through base camp, killing at least 19 people. A strong aftershock on 12 May added to the toll.
